commits.message:
[Performance][Model] Tile Qwen4Exp HC gate mix on Ascend A2/A3/A5 (#21901)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds an eight-row Triton tile for Qwen4Exp HyperConnection
`gate_mix`.
The existing one-row kernel remains the fallback. The row-block kernel
processes
an `8 x 512` tile, reduces the launched-program count by up to 8x, and
preserves
the original FP32 accumulation order.

The dispatch threshold is based on the integrated wrapper, not the
kernel alone:

- A2/A3: row-block starts at 2048 rows.
- A5: row-block starts at 1024 rows.

At 1024 rows the direct kernel is faster on all three devices, but
host-side
output allocation and custom-op dispatch dominate on A2/A3. A5 crosses
over
earlier and benefits from the row-block path at 1024 rows.

The shared `8 x 512` tile is close to the best measured per-device tile
at
1024 rows:

- A2: `8 x 512` is `80.00 us`; the best measured `4 x 512` variant is
  `78.86 us`, a 1.45% difference.
- A5: `8 x 512` is `14.63 us`; the best measured `32 x 128` variant is
  `14.57 us`, a 0.41% difference.

`512` divides the production `group_dim=2560` exactly, preserves column
alignment, and keeps one shared tile instead of adding per-device
tuning.
One hoisted mask is reused for all stream loads and the output store,
including
production-aligned and tail widths.

The implementation also handles column tails, combined row/column tails,
and
element offsets beyond `INT32_MAX`. The normal prefill path remains
int32.

No environment variable or user configuration is added.

### Operator integration

- Public wrapper: `hc_gate_mix(x, gate, hc_count)`
- Registered custom op: `qwen4_exp_ascend_hc_gate_mix`
- Production caller: `vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/model.py`
- Validated model ABI: BF16 `[rows, 10240]` inputs, `hc_count=4`, BF16
output
  `[rows, 2560]`
- Operator guide:
  `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/qwen4_exp_hc_gate_mix.md`

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Large Qwen4Exp prefills can use the row-block operator path on A2,
A3, and
A5. Smaller prefills and unsupported profiles retain the existing
one-row path.
A release-note fragment is included.

### How was this patch tested?

Environment:

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| CANN | 9.1.0 |
| Python | 3.11.10 |
| torch / torch-npu | 2.10.0+cpu / 2.10.0.post4 |
| triton-ascend | 3.6.0.post2 |
| EvalScope | 1.14.1 |

Functional validation:

| Check | A2 | A3 | A5 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CPU dispatch/profile tests | 35 passed | 34 passed | 35 passed |
| Nightly Triton operator tests | 10 passed | 10 passed | 10 passed |
| Bitwise parity with legacy kernel | pass | pass | pass |
| NPUGraph replay | pass | pass | pass |
| Forced `WIDE_OFFSETS=True` parity | pass | pass | pass |
| Actual int32 boundary reference parity | pass | pass | pass |

The nightly suite now covers `group_dim=513` at rows 1024 and 1025, with
both
contiguous and row-strided inputs. These cases compare the row-block
kernel
against both the legacy kernel and the PyTorch reference, exercising
column
tails and combined row/column tails.

The int64 path has two levels of coverage. CPU tests check the exact
209,715/209,716-row host boundary and all three tensor strides. Separate
A2, A3,
and A5 runs each allocated 209,716 rows, selected `WIDE_OFFSETS=True`,
exceeded
`INT32_MAX` with `max_offset=2,147,491,839`, and matched PyTorch 64-bit
indexing
with `max_abs_error=0.0`.

The final PR does not modify `tests/manual/`. During kernel bring-up,
the
pre-existing manual script was used as a local NPU harness so boundary
and
replay cases could be run directly on the target board before nightly
integration existed. Once the coverage was formalized, refreshed-input
NPUGraph
replay moved to the nightly operator test and the temporary manual cases
were
removed. All deterministic coverage introduced by this PR now lives in
`tests/ut/` and `tests/e2e/nightly/`.

#### Real-serving compile reuse

A fresh-cache TP2 A3 serving probe hooked
`_hc_gate_mix_row_block_kernel._do_compile` in both real worker
processes:

| Phase | Input rows | Compilations |
|---|---:|---:|
| Startup | capture/warmup | 2 |
| Serving | 1024 | 0 |
| Serving | 2049 | 0 |
| Serving | 4096 | 0 |
| Serving | 8191 | 0 |
| Serving | 8192 | 0 |

The startup calls prepare the row-block variant once per worker.
Changing the
row count reuses it. The 1024-row request remains on the legacy kernel.

JIT specialization analysis:

- `rows` is annotated `do_not_specialize`, so changing only the row
count does
  not create another variant.
- `WIDE_OFFSETS` remains a compile-time constant for the rare
large-offset
  path.
- Exact-tile mask switches were removed. A3 measurements showed that
always
using the hoisted mask costs only 0.55% at 1024 rows and 0.04% at 8192
rows;
removing the switches avoids two constexpr keys, extra branches, and
separate
  compile variants.
- The real-serving probe observed one row-block variant per worker and
no
  unbounded row-count specialization.

#### Profiling follow-up

`msprof` was run on A3 with CANN 9.1.0, TP2 + EP, eager execution, and
four
`input=8192 / output=1` requests. The run completed `4/4` with
`failed=0`.
Profiling adds large collection overhead, so these numbers are used only
for
relative hotspot analysis, not as latency evidence.

The A3 trace was captured on one TP rank. The other rank did not produce
a
usable device trace. Its normalized NPU task-time distribution was:

| Kernel group | Share |
|---|---:|
| `_hc_combine_norm_kernel` | 12.86% |
| `ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFwd` | 8.97% |
| Grouped matmul path | 11.23% |
| `FusedInferAttentionScore` | 5.14% |
| AllToAllV AI CPU launch | 4.69% |
| `_hc_gate_mix_row_block_kernel` | 4.12% |
| Lightning Indexer + QSA mask preparation | 7.35% |

The optimized gate-mix kernel is no longer the dominant kernel-level
hotspot.
Further end-to-end work should focus on combine/norm, grouped matmul,
AllToAllV
launch overhead, and QSA index/mask preparation. Those items are outside
this
PR's operator scope.

#### 1024-row crossover

Medians use nine alternating rounds and 30 launches per sample.
Direct-kernel
timing uses preallocated output; wrapper timing includes allocation and
custom-op
dispatch.

| Device | Legacy direct | Row-block direct | Direct delta | Legacy
wrapper | Row-block wrapper | Wrapper delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A2 | 93.99 us | 81.71 us | -13.06% | 143.46 us | 173.85 us | +21.17% |
| A3 | 72.01 us | 45.88 us | -36.29% | 73.96 us | 88.11 us | +19.13% |
| A5 | 34.34 us | 14.47 us | -57.88% | 34.79 us | 18.18 us | -47.75% |

How to read this table:

- `direct` compares kernel execution only. The row-block kernel is
faster on
  every device because it launches fewer programs.
- `wrapper` compares the complete call path: output allocation, Python
validation, hardware-profile checks, custom-op dispatch, and Triton
launch.
On A2/A3 at 1024 rows, this host-bound overhead is larger than the
kernel
  time saved, so the complete row-block path is slower.
- The A2/A3 1024-row wrapper numbers are a forced experiment used to
select the
crossover. They are not the production configuration: both devices
retain
  the legacy path below 2048 rows.
- A5 crosses over earlier because its kernel saving is much larger, so
the
  complete row-block wrapper remains faster even after adding the common
  wrapper overhead.

Focused A3 decomposition at 1024 rows confirms the boundary:

| Path | Device time | Host enqueue |
|---|---:|---:|
| Output allocation only | 7.15 us | 6.25 us |
| Legacy direct | 73.05 us | 45.38 us |
| Row-block direct | 52.75 us | 50.83 us |
| Allocation + row-block direct | 64.87 us | 62.92 us |
| Row-block internal dispatch | 80.66 us | 77.56 us |
| Row-block `torch.ops` call | 90.58 us | 88.57 us |
| Row-block public wrapper | 94.52 us | 91.99 us |

The row-block kernel saves about 20 us, but allocation and host dispatch
add
more than that at this small row count. The family-specific thresholds
are
therefore part of the optimization, not evidence that the row-block
kernel is
slower.

`rows` with and without `do_not_specialize` differs by less than 1.3% in
these
direct measurements. The 1024-row behavior change is therefore caused by
the
integrated host crossover and dispatch threshold, not by the
specialization
annotation or kernel math.

#### A3 official end-to-end benchmark and accuracy

`vllm bench serve` configuration:

```text
random dataset, input=8192, output=1, 100 requests per arm
TP2 + EP, eager execution, max-num-batched-tokens=8192
fresh server and warmup for every arm
baseline -> candidate -> candidate -> baseline
```

| Concurrency | Throughput delta | Mean TTFT delta | P99 TTFT delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | +1.73% | -1.70% | -2.54% |
| 4 | +4.41% | -4.60% | -13.94% |
| 16 | +1.49% | -1.47% | -1.36% |

All reported performance arms completed `100/100` requests with
`failed=0`.

Full EvalScope GSM8K used all 1319 samples, greedy decoding, seed 42,
and
`max_tokens=512`:

| Run | Baseline | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Run 1 | 92.57% | 91.21% | -1.36 pp |
| Run 2, reversed order | 91.58% | 91.36% | -0.22 pp |

Both runs completed `1319/1319` with zero errors. Model-level accuracy
varies
by about 1 pp across fresh server runs; the reversed-order run is nearly
equal.
The kernel itself is bitwise equal to the legacy implementation in the
tested
shape classes. No accuracy improvement is claimed.

### Merge status and scope

- A3 has full model-level performance and accuracy evidence.
- A2/A5 have full operator-level parity, tail, graph replay,
compilation, and
  timing evidence.
- Full A2/A5 model serving is not feasible with this checkpoint on the
available
hardware: the checkpoint is about 181 GB, while A2 has 32 GB HBM and A5
has
128 GB HBM. No A2/A5 model-level performance or accuracy claim is made.
- The Git merge state is `MERGEABLE`; GitHub reports `BLOCKED` because
required
  CODEOWNERS approvals are still missing.
- `DCO`, lint/static checks, CPU tests, nightly operator tests, and
local
  validation pass on the current local validation head.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM-Ascend project
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from vllm.triton_utils import HAS_TRITON, triton
+
+from tests.e2e.nightly.single_node.ops.singlecard_ops.triton.dcp_test_utils import assert_dcp_close
+from vllm_ascend.device.hardware_profile import HardwareCapability, get_current_hardware_profile
+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.qwen4_exp import hc as hc_module
+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.qwen4_exp.hc import (
+    _HC_GATE_MIX_BLOCK_SIZE,
+    _HC_GATE_MIX_ROWS_PER_BLOCK,
+    _hc_gate_mix_kernel,
+    _hc_gate_mix_row_block_kernel,
+    hc_gate_mix,
+)
+
+pytestmark = [
+    pytest.mark.skipif(not HAS_TRITON, reason="Triton is not available"),
+    pytest.mark.skipif(
+        not get_current_hardware_profile().supports(HardwareCapability.QWEN4EXP_HC_GATE_MIX_ROW_BLOCK),
+        reason="Qwen4Exp HC row-block kernel is not enabled for this hardware profile",
+    ),
+]
+
+HC_COUNT = 4
+GROUP_DIM = 2560
+HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE = HC_COUNT * GROUP_DIM
+DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
+
+
+def _make_input(rows: int, width: int, *, row_strided: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if not row_strided:
+        return torch.randn((rows, width), device="npu", dtype=DTYPE) * 0.5
+    backing = torch.randn((rows, width + 16), device="npu", dtype=DTYPE) * 0.5
+    result = backing[:, :width]
+    assert result.stride(1) == 1 and not result.is_contiguous()
+    return result
+
+
+def _reference_gate_mix(x: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor, group_dim: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    grouped_x = x.float().unflatten(-1, (HC_COUNT, group_dim))
+    grouped_gate = torch.sigmoid(gate.float()).unflatten(-1, (HC_COUNT, group_dim))
+    return (grouped_x * grouped_gate).mean(dim=-2).to(x.dtype)
+
+
+def _legacy_gate_mix(x: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor, group_dim: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    output = x.new_empty((x.shape[0], group_dim))
+    _hc_gate_mix_kernel[(x.shape[0], triton.cdiv(group_dim, _HC_GATE_MIX_BLOCK_SIZE))](
+        x,
+        gate,
+        output,
+        x.stride(0),
+        gate.stride(0),
+        output.stride(0),
+        GROUP_DIM=group_dim,
+        HC_COUNT=HC_COUNT,
+        BLOCK_SIZE=_HC_GATE_MIX_BLOCK_SIZE,
+    )
+    return output
+
+
+def _row_block_gate_mix(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    gate: torch.Tensor,
+    group_dim: int,
+    *,
+    wide_offsets: bool = False,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    output = x.new_empty((x.shape[0], group_dim))
+    _hc_gate_mix_row_block_kernel[
+        (
+            triton.cdiv(x.shape[0], _HC_GATE_MIX_ROWS_PER_BLOCK),
+            triton.cdiv(group_dim, _HC_GATE_MIX_BLOCK_SIZE),
+        )
+    ](
+        x,
+        gate,
+        output,
+        x.shape[0],
+        x.stride(0),
+        gate.stride(0),
+        output.stride(0),
+        GROUP_DIM=group_dim,
+        HC_COUNT=HC_COUNT,
+        ROWS_PER_BLOCK=_HC_GATE_MIX_ROWS_PER_BLOCK,
+        BLOCK_SIZE=_HC_GATE_MIX_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        WIDE_OFFSETS=wide_offsets,
+    )
+    return output
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("rows", "row_strided"),
+    (
+        (2047, False),
+        (2048, False),
+        (2049, True),
+    ),
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_hc_gate_mix_row_block_matches_legacy_kernel(rows: int, row_strided: bool) -> None:
+    x = _make_input(rows, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE, row_strided=row_strided)
+    gate = _make_input(rows, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE, row_strided=row_strided)
+
+    actual = hc_gate_mix(x, gate, HC_COUNT)
+    legacy = _legacy_gate_mix(x, gate, GROUP_DIM)
+    expected = _reference_gate_mix(x, gate, GROUP_DIM)
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, legacy, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    assert_dcp_close(actual, expected)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", (1024, 1025))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("row_strided", (False, True))
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_hc_gate_mix_row_block_combined_tails(rows: int, row_strided: bool) -> None:
+    group_dim = 513
+    x = _make_input(rows, HC_COUNT * group_dim, row_strided=row_strided)
+    gate = _make_input(rows, HC_COUNT * group_dim, row_strided=row_strided)
+
+    actual = _row_block_gate_mix(x, gate, group_dim)
+    legacy = _legacy_gate_mix(x, gate, group_dim)
+    expected = _reference_gate_mix(x, gate, group_dim)
+    torch.npu.synchronize()
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, legacy, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    assert_dcp_close(actual, expected)
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_hc_gate_mix_row_block_npugraph_replay() -> None:
+    rows = 2049
+    x = _make_input(rows, HYPER_HIDDEN_SIZE, row_strided=True)

+# qwen4_exp_hc_gate_mix
+
+Source: `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/qwen4_exp/hc.py` (public wrapper:
+`hc_gate_mix`).
+
+## Description
+
+- **Function**: Applies the HyperConnection (HC) gate to each token row and
+  reduces the configured HC streams into one output row. The operator is
+  model-specific to Qwen4Exp.
+- **Formula**: For row `r`, output column `c`, and `H = hc_count`:
+
+    ```text
+    output[r, c] =
+        sum(sigmoid(gate[r, s * group_dim + c]) *
+            x[r, s * group_dim + c]) / H
+        for s in [0, H)
+    ```
+
+    The multiplication and sum are evaluated in FP32 in stream order, then
+    converted to the input dtype for the output store.
+
+- **Algorithm flow**:
+    1. The Python wrapper validates the shape, divisibility, and inner-stride
+       contract and allocates `[rows, group_dim]` output storage.
+    2. For rows at or above the family-specific threshold on an enabled
+       hardware profile, the wrapper launches
+       `_hc_gate_mix_row_block_kernel` with grid
+       `(cdiv(rows, 8), cdiv(group_dim, 512))`.
+    3. Each row-block program owns an `8 x 512` tile. It initializes one FP32
+       accumulator and walks the HC streams with `tl.static_range`, preserving
+       the original load, sigmoid, multiply, and accumulate order.
+    4. Each program computes one hoisted 2-D mask and reuses it for all stream
+       loads and the final store.
+    5. If any input or output element offset can exceed `INT32_MAX`, row
+       indices are widened to int64 before multiplying by the row stride.
+       Normal prefill sizes retain the int32 path.
+    6. Smaller batches, unsupported hardware profiles, and empty inputs use the
+       existing one-row kernel or skip the launch respectively.
+- **Supported modes**: The row-block path is enabled for Atlas A2, Atlas A3,
+  and A5 profiles. Validation covered `Ascend910B4`, `Ascend910_9382`, and
+  `Ascend950PR_9579`. A5 gating is family-level, but `Ascend950DT` was not
+  separately profiled. NPU eager execution and NPUGraph capture/replay are
+  supported. The public wrapper keeps its existing PyTorch fallback for
+  non-NPU tensors.
+
+## Parameters
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> The public Python interface has three required arguments. Tensor strides and
+> kernel tile parameters are internal attributes prepared by the wrapper.
+
+| Parameter | Input/Output/Attribute | Description | Data type | Data format |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `x` | Input | Hidden states with shape `[rows, hc_count * group_dim]`; the validated model shape is `[rows, 10240]` | BF16 is declared and tested; output preserves the input dtype | ND, unit inner stride, arbitrary row stride |
+| `gate` | Input | Gate values with the same shape as `x`; its row stride is supplied independently | Same as `x` | ND, unit inner stride, padded row stride |
+| `hc_count` | Attribute | Number of HC streams; compile-time constant `H` in the kernel. The validated model value is `4` | Integer | Scalar |
+| Return value | Output | Newly allocated tensor with shape `[rows, group_dim]`; the validated model shape is `[rows, 2560]` | Same as `x` | Contiguous 2-D ND |
+| `rows` | Internal runtime attribute | Number of flattened token rows. It controls the launch grid and tail masks and is marked `do_not_specialize` | Integer | Scalar |
+| `stride_x_row`, `stride_gate_row`, `stride_output_row` | Internal runtime attributes | Element strides between adjacent input and output rows | Integer | Scalar |
+| `GROUP_DIM` | Internal compile-time attribute | Number of columns per HC stream; validated model value is `2560` | Integer | Scalar |
+| `HC_COUNT` | Internal compile-time attribute | Number of HC streams processed by the static loop | Integer | Scalar |
+| `ROWS_PER_BLOCK` | Internal compile-time attribute | Rows owned by one program; fixed to `8` | Integer | Scalar |
+| `BLOCK_SIZE` | Internal compile-time attribute | Columns owned by one program tile; fixed to `512` | Integer | Scalar |
+| `WIDE_OFFSETS` | Internal compile-time attribute | Widen row indices to int64 when any maximum element offset exceeds `INT32_MAX` | Boolean | Scalar |
+
+## Constraints
+
+- `x` and `gate` must be matching 2-D tensors on the same NPU. The wrapper
+  raises `ValueError` for a shape mismatch.
+- The hidden dimension must be divisible by `hc_count`, and both inputs must
+  have unit inner stride (`stride(1) == 1`). The row stride may include padding;
+  the row-strided tail case is covered on real NPU.
+- The public wrapper is out-of-place. It returns newly allocated storage and
+  does not mutate `x` or `gate`.
+- The validated input dtype is BF16, matching the Qwen4Exp model path. The
+  tested shape is `hc_count=4`, `group_dim=2560`, and hidden width `10240`.
+- The row-block path requires `QWEN4EXP_HC_GATE_MIX_ROW_BLOCK` and a row count
+  at or above the hardware profile threshold. The integrated wrapper uses
+  2048 rows on A2/A3 and 1024 rows on A5 based on measured host-side crossover;
+  other rows and profiles retain the one-row kernel.
+- For a contiguous width-10,240 row, the first row whose element offset can
+  exceed `INT32_MAX` is 209,715. The host selects
+  `WIDE_OFFSETS=True` for that range. The int64 branch is compiled and checked
+  against the legacy kernel on A2, A3, and A5. Boundary runs on all three
+  devices allocated 209,716 rows, selected the wide-offset path, and matched
+  PyTorch 64-bit indexing with zero maximum absolute error.
+- No device tensor value is read on the host. The host uses only shape, dtype,
+  and stride metadata.
+- NPUGraph capture and replay keep tensor addresses, shape, strides, and launch
+  arguments fixed. Refreshing input values before replay is supported and is
+  covered by the nightly test.
+- `rows`, `GROUP_DIM`, `HC_COUNT`, `ROWS_PER_BLOCK`, `BLOCK_SIZE`, and
+  `WIDE_OFFSETS` are the main JIT keys.
+  `rows` is marked `do_not_specialize` and the nightly compile-reuse test
+  records compile events to verify that row count changes reuse one variant.
+  A forced wide-offset case covers that separate constexpr branch.
+- No dedicated warmup registration is added. This existing model-specific path
+  uses the same wrapper at compilation and runtime; normal startup or graph
+  capture prepares the bounded launch variants used by serving.
+
+## Serving Compile Behavior
+
+A real TP2 A3 serving probe used a fresh Triton cache and recorded every
+`_hc_gate_mix_row_block_kernel` compilation in both worker processes:
+
+| Phase | Input rows | Compilations |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Startup | capture/warmup | 2 |
+| Serving | 1024 | 0 |
+| Serving | 2049 | 0 |
+| Serving | 4096 | 0 |
+| Serving | 8191 | 0 |
+| Serving | 8192 | 0 |
+
+The two startup compilations are the row-block variant for each TP worker.
+Changing only the row count reuses that variant. A 1024-row request remains on
+the legacy kernel and therefore does not compile the row-block kernel.
+
+## Origin and Differences
+
+- **Origin**: The math and public interface mirror the upstream Qwen4Exp
+  HyperConnection glue operator. The existing one-row Triton implementation
+  was already in this module; this change adds the Ascend row-block
+  specialization.
+- **Differences**:
+    - NPU adaptation for performance: processes eight rows per Triton program
+      for large prefill batches, reducing the program count by up to 8x and
+      amortizing scheduling overhead without changing FP32 accumulation order.
+    - Tile tuning: at 1024 rows, the shared `8 x 512` tile measured `80.00 us`
+      on A2, within 1.45% of the best measured `4 x 512` variant (`78.86 us`),
+      and `14.63 us` on A5, within 0.41% of the best measured `32 x 128`
+      variant (`14.57 us`). A shared tile avoids per-device tuning. `512`
+      divides the production `group_dim=2560` exactly, while one hoisted mask
+      supports both exact and tail widths without additional JIT variants. The
+      `8 x 512` FP32 accumulator occupies 16 KiB before stream loads.
+    - Modified for specific vLLM-Ascend logic: hardware capability gating
+      enables the row-block path on A2, A3, and A5, while preserving the
+      one-row kernel elsewhere.
+    - Added an int64 address branch for tensors whose maximum row-major offset
+      exceeds int32 range.
+    - CUDA PDL hooks from the upstream implementation are intentionally omitted
+      because triton-ascend launches on an NPU stream.
+- **Replacement plan**: This is a permanent performance specialization of the
+  existing operator. A temporary replacement or removal plan is N/A.
+- **Production integration**: `vllm_ascend/models/qwen4_exp/model.py` replaces
+  `upstream_hc.hc_gate_mix` with this operator before the upstream Qwen4Exp
+  model classes are imported. The custom op is registered as
+  `qwen4_exp_ascend_hc_gate_mix`.
+
+## Test Cases
+
+The reference implementation is `_reference_gate_mix` in the nightly test:
+it evaluates the same grouping, sigmoid, multiply, and mean operations in
+PyTorch FP32 before casting to BF16. The legacy Triton kernel is a separate
+bitwise-parity oracle.
+
+The single-operator NPU suite is located under the nightly single-card Triton
+directory:
+
+```bash
+pytest -q \
+  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_qwen4_exp_hc.py
+```
+
+The suite uses `hc_count=4` and BF16 inputs. It covers:
+
+- rows `2047`, `2048`, and `2049`, including the dispatch boundary;
+- `group_dim=513` with rows `1024` and `1025`, including row tails, column
+  tails, and combined row-and-column masks;
+- contiguous inputs and row-strided inputs, where each input row retains unit
+  inner stride but has a padded row stride;
+- a non-contiguous, row-strided tail input;
+- bitwise output parity between the row-block and legacy kernels with
+  `rtol=0, atol=0`;
+- the unified BF16 reference tolerance (`rtol=2^-6`, `atol=2^-6`), requiring
+  at least 99 percent of elements to pass and maximum absolute error no greater
+  than `1`;
+- NPUGraph replay after refreshing both input buffers;
+- a forced `WIDE_OFFSETS=True` launch checked bitwise against the legacy
+  kernel;
+- compile reuse across exact-row and row-tail batch counts. The test changes
+  row counts that exercise both divisible-by-16 and non-16 specialization
+  classes and verifies that they reuse the same kernel variant.
+
+CPU dispatch and hardware-capability tests remain in the unit-test suite with
+mocked Triton launch entry points:
+
+```bash
+pytest -q \
+  tests/ut/ops/test_qwen4_exp_hc.py \
+  tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py

+### NoPE Prolog V3
+
+On A2/A3, eligible dynamic W8A8 checkpoints automatically fuse the NoPE SFA
+projections, normalization and INT8 KV-cache write with
+`torch_npu.npu_mla_prolog_v3`. This path requires
+a torch_npu/CANN build that supports `rope_dim=0` for this operator.
+The MLA down and query-up projections must be INT8; checkpoints that keep those
+projections in BF16 retain native preprocessing. A BF16 indexer retains its original query
+projection and normalization, whose cost remains part of the layer.
+Use BF16 activations and INT8 KV cache in the serving command:
+
+```bash
+--dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype int8
+```
+
+Selection applies to prefill, decode and MTP calls on eligible NoPE SFA layers.
+It requires D=256, Hckv=512 and Hcq=1536/2048. A5/MXFP8, C16, PCP, DCP and
+other incompatible configurations retain native preprocessing. No additional
+configuration switch is needed.
+

commits.message:
[Feature] Support HiSparse with PCP decode request sharding (#21892)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable BF16 and native C8 HiSparse with prefill PCP and standard PCP
decode request sharding on Ascend 950 Model Runner V2.

- Use rank-local inputs for query and request-state handling, and
rank-major gathered rows for Resident cache and Host mirror writes. BF16
preprocessing sizes its workspace for all gathered rows and uses the
same write mapping as C8.
- Reuse Core's residency scheduling, DMA, completion fences and PCP
decode sharding policy. KV history is replicated across PCP ranks.
- Keep Target, draft prefill and later replicated draft decode layouts
aligned across graph capture and replay. The sharding changes from
#22069 are included.

Ascend-only change with no new operator or configuration switch. Base
HiSparse #20926 and Core PCP reuse #21846 are already in main.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. BF16 and native C8 HiSparse support PCP prefill and request-sharded
decode on Ascend 950 MRV2. Decode graphs and MTP are covered. Configure
eager Host mirroring and per-rank Host pools as described in the feature
guide. DCP, MultiConnector and external disaggregated P/D remain outside
the supported scope.

### How was this patch tested?

- Current BF16 functional runtime and test files match the on-device and
CPU-tested artifacts by SHA-256. Combined PCP CPU suite: 37 passed,
including BF16/FP16 write contracts, padded slots and PCP2/4 gathered
lengths. Prior C8 combined head `64dd8404`: 339 targeted CPU tests
passed.
- Ascend 950 PCP2, GLM5.3 with main KV and indexer BF16, TP4/EP8, MTP3
and decode graphs. Two-request graph smoke and completed 4- and
8-request waves. Forced BF16 Host-to-device recovery passed 6/6 device
checks. End-to-end BF16 was tested; FP16 coverage is CPU-only.
- The prior native C8 combined-stack validation completed all 16
requests at 32K input / 8K output on the same 18.8 GiB KV pool.
Whole-run output throughput was 460.97 → 583.65 tokens/s with HiSparse,
and preemptions decreased from 2 to 0. The input hashes matched; the
actual decode batches differed as the OFF run peaked at 11 running
requests. This is C8 capacity evidence for the previously tested
combined revision, not a BF16 performance result.
- For the BF16 functional patch, Ruff check, Ruff format and `git diff
--check` passed. Full repository CI has not been manually triggered.

This PR uses the existing unquantized SFA path. BF16 prefill performance
is addressed separately in #22371, which can merge independently.

### Checklist

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: empty local queries, padding,
sharded and replicated layouts, graph and draft transitions.
- [x] **Regression test**: request ownership and gathered Resident/Host
writes, including BF16.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: unsupported connector
composition and parallel configurations.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: CPU contracts, device recovery
and model smoke tests.

AI assistance was used for implementation, review and validation.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+def prepare_pcp_query_metadata(metadata, states, local_states, world_size):
+    """Keep graph inputs at fixed addresses across capture and real steps."""
+    states.fill_(-1)
+    states[: local_states.numel()].copy_(local_states)
+    count = metadata.num_input_tokens * world_size
+    # Keep the fixed backing address, but expose only this batch's request rows.
+    metadata.hisparse_request_state_indices = states[: local_states.numel()]
+    metadata.hisparse_num_write_tokens = count
+    # Gathered slots already mark padding with -1; scatter needs no row counter.
+    metadata.hisparse_num_valid_write_rows = None
+    metadata.hisparse_write_has_prefill = metadata.pcp_has_global_prefill
+
+
+def get_pcp_write_request_ids(global_batch, gather_indices, write_mask):
+    rows = torch.bucketize(gather_indices.contiguous(), global_batch.query_start_loc[1:].contiguous(), right=True).to(
+        torch.int32

+    rows.masked_fill_(~write_mask, -1)

+
+
+def prepare_pcp_query_states(cache, metadata):

+    states = getattr(metadata, "hisparse_request_state_indices", None)

+        for member in cache.index_group_caches:
+            member.runtime.request_state_indices = states
+            member.host_mirror_required = metadata.hisparse_write_has_prefill or member.runtime.eager_host_mirror
+
+
+def hisparse_write_target(cache, metadata, num_input_rows, num_slot_rows):
+    """Gathered writes include padding and must not use Core's decode row cap."""
+    count = getattr(metadata, "hisparse_num_write_tokens", None)
+    if count is None:
+        return cache.write_target(num_input_rows, num_slot_rows)

[CI] Move five A3-800T weekly cases to the nightly 560T matrix (#22246)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Moves five A3-800T weekly single-node cases to the nightly A3-560T
matrix so they run with higher frequency on the 560T runner pool:

- `structured_output_qwen3` and `test_qwen3_grid_exceed_65536`: already
registered in nightly `a3-560t.multi_card` by #22175, so only the weekly
(800T) duplicates are removed here.
- `openai-api-compatibility` (800i-4),
`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-w8a8-A3-accuracy` (800i-2),
`Qwen3.6_35B_27B_A3_acceptance_rate` (800i-2): newly registered in
nightly `a3-560t.multi_card` and dropped from the weekly
`a3.single_node` section.

Test-only config change: no source code or test assets are modified.

## Related issues

Follow-up to #22175.

## Test cases passed

All five cases passed on the latest Weekly-A3 run (run 43611842460).
Case classification follows the reviewer guidance from #22175: all five
run with tensor parallelism > 1, so they belong in `multi_card`.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

[BugFix][Attention] Fix GLM DFlash2 FA3 HND caches and target graph warmup (#22159)

Current scope (`555017b3c`): GLM DFlash2 automatic FA3 selection
requires an eager draft (`speculative_config.enforce_eager=true`); the
target may still use graph execution. Early FA3 initialization and
resolved-layout binding are retained. The focused FA3 and DSpark
integration CPU contracts pass all 126 cases; full CI and hardware
validation remain required.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable the optional A2/A3 FA3 backend for eligible local GLM DFlash2
drafts while preserving the target attention backend and physical HND KV
storage. Prerequisite #20167 is merged; this PR contains the focused
follow-up.

- Preserve physical HND cache writes and expose the logical FA3 view
through a zero-copy transpose.
- Complete one-time generic FA3 native scheduler initialization in the
selected attention implementation constructor, **before model
profiling**. Retain inputs/results through synchronization and cache
successful initialization per worker/device/operator contract. The
constructor owns configuration/NPU availability eligibility;
initialization has no speculative-method or eager-only restriction. The
helper accepts an already-validated NPU device.
- Remove late initialization from the metadata builder and remove the
DFlash-specific target metadata filter. Keep draft attention groups, KV
allocation/binding, and connector initialization intact.
- Retain hardware, local PCP/DCP, dtype and fallback guards for backend
admission.

Controlled two-node A3 experiments found that first
`ComputeFAMetadataV3` CPU-function registration could remain pending
after profiling, including when initialized from the metadata builder.
Target warmup then waited in an all_reduce/NPUEvent synchronization
path. Initializing before profiling passed both with and without
metadata filtering; filtering is therefore not required to avoid the
observed hang in that configuration. The lower-level runtime/driver
mechanism remains unresolved.

The process-local initialization cache is written only after successful
synchronization. Forward and per-step metadata construction do not
update it or add these synchronization barriers. No pool policy, driver,
environment-variable or parallel-topology changes are included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Eligible local GLM DFlash2 drafts can use optional FA3 with HND KV
caches while the target retains its own attention and graph path. HND
layout resolution also honors the connector preference when no
environment override is set. Eager and graph draft configurations share
the admission/warmup logic; graph-draft hardware validation remains
pending.

### How was this patch tested?

Latest review update (`3d37ff50b`):
- **234 CPU contract tests passed** in the Ascend container, including
DFlash, DSpark, MTP and no-speculation configurations,
missing/unavailable NPU, constructor ordering, per-device deduplication,
and retry after failed initialization. CPU contracts explicitly disable
NPU availability.
- **8 A3 native FA3 cases passed eager and NPU graph capture/replay
against a CPU reference**: Q/KV heads 32/4 and 16/1, head dimension128,
FP16/BF16, causal/non-causal. This validates representative
scheduler/operator paths, not full MiniMax/Step5 models or A5 hardware.
- Both changed files passed Ruff0.14.0 and targeted mypy
(`--follow-imports skip --check-untyped-defs --ignore-missing-imports`,
Python3.10); full CI remains required.
- Updated four-node GLM P/D validation is in progress with a
decode-first proxy. Previous image-overlay run completed FULL capture on
all32 D workers, but P/D inference failed because the platform generated
an incompatible prefill-first proxy; that run is not counted as P/D
correctness.

Earlier evidence:

- Previous `22045b375` baseline after merging current main (including
Step5 routing and MTP padding fixes) staged in an isolated Ascend
container; source SHA256 values checked against the local changes. **472
tests passed**:

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
python3 -m pytest -q \
  tests/ut/attention/test_minimax_fa3.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_flash_attn.py \
  tests/ut/attention/test_step5_fa3.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_adaptive_verification.py \
  tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v2_kv_cache.py
```

- All six PR Python files passed mypy with `--follow-imports skip
--check-untyped-defs` for Python **3.10, 3.11 and 3.12**. Tests cover
constructor-before-builder ordering, eager/graph configuration,
non-DFlash/no-speculation fallbacks, absent/unavailable NPU, unresolved
block size, synchronization/deduplication and draft KV/group
preservation.
- Ruff 0.14.0 check/format, codespell, typos, forbidden-import,
boolean-context-manager, long-function, symbolic-meta, package-init,
logger and `git diff --check` checks passed. The complete pre-commit
invocation could not finish installing all hook tools because a download
connection closed; full CI remains pending.
- Earlier controlled hardware comparison: two A3 D nodes, DP16/TP2/EP32,
HND, eager DFlash2 draft and FULL_DECODE_ONLY target graphs. Pre-profile
initialization **with and without** metadata filtering completed 32 KV
connector initializations, target capture on all 32 ranks and the fixed
first 8-token direct request. Operator-call and constructor warmup
arguments match this revision; redundant builder initialization and
diagnostics were removed. This used a frozen deployed vLLM ABI with
adapted sources, **not a full latest-PR deployment**.
- Uninitialized/unfiltered runs reproduced the target warmup stall after
all 32 KV connector initializations, with matching native registration
evidence both with and without host communication tracing. A post-KV CPU
barrier did not fix builder-time registration. Filter-only attempts
stopped at 31 KV initializations due to a separate HYBM
address-reservation failure and are excluded from the comparison.
- Full latest-PR 32-rank deployment, draft-graph execution, full
P/D/pool correctness, A2 execution, long-context accuracy and
performance regression coverage remain pending. No broad
accuracy/performance claim is made from the startup/direct-request
experiments.

### Checklist

- [x] Focused regression tests and guarded fallbacks.
- [x] Preserve draft KV storage, attention groups and target parallel
configuration.
- [x] Native initialization completes before profiling; no added
per-step synchronization.
- [ ] Required CI and remaining hardware/accuracy/performance coverage.

[Performance][Model] Fuse the Step5 head-wise attention gate and indexer QKZ norm+RoPE kernels (#22401)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Following up on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20946.
Two model-specific Triton operator fusions for Step5-Preview on Ascend;
both replace eager chains that materialize intermediates and move
gate/indexer views across op boundaries (TensorMove on NPU):

1. **`gated_scale`** — fuses the post-attention head-wise gate (`attn *
sigmoid(gate)`) into one kernel, and (when `total_num_kv_heads >=
tp_size` and the packed shards are unquantized) packs the sliding-window
qkv and gate projections into one `qkvg` GEMM, so one matmul yields `[Q
| K | V | gate]` and the separate `g_proj` launch disappears. Callers:
`AscendStep5DSAAttention.forward`, `AscendStep5Attention.forward`.
2. **`indexer_qkz_norm_rope`** — fuses the DSA sparse-indexer chain
(per-head RMSNorm on `index_q`, LayerNorm on `index_k`, NeoX RoPE on
both, `index_z` passthrough) into one kernel, reading the strided
`split_indexer` views in place and storing `index_q` as e4m3, the dtype
the fused indexer scoring already consumes. Caller:
`AscendStep5DSAAttention._finish_indexer`.

Per gated layer per step this removes two eager kernels and one
materializing copy, plus one GEMM launch when qkv+gate packing is
active.

- Co-author for the indexer QKZ norm+RoPE operator optimization:
shengzhaotian <shengzhao_tian@163.com>.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

**Validation device:** Ascend 950DT only. Step5-Preview currently
targets 950DT; A2/A3 are not validated.

**Operator accuracy.** Single-operator e2e tests:
-
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_step5_gated_scale.py`
-
`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_step5_indexer_qkz_norm_rope.py`
- 42 single-operator tests passed on Ascend 950DT.

**Model accuracy.** GPQA-Diamond accuracy evaluation:
- Evaluation Settings: `temperature=1`, `top_p=0.95`,
`top_k=0`,`max_tokens=1048576`

- Results

| Dataset | Accuracy |
|---|---:|
| GPQA-Diamond | **94.44%** (374/396) |

- Baseline Reference
Record **#20946** reported **GPQA 93.43 / MMMU_PRO 76.07** on the
double-node A5 DT pod.

**Performance.** End-to-end decode ITL at 64K input / 4K output:

| Batch | Baseline (both off) | `gated_scale` | `indexer_qkz_norm_rope`
|
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 36.977 ms | 36.404 ms (−1.55%) | 36.239 ms (−2.00%) |
| 32 | 39.312 ms | 38.747 ms (−1.44%) | 39.271 ms (−0.10%) | 

Conditions: Ascend 950DT, 2 nodes x 8 NPUs, DP4 x TP4 (EP16), MTP3, LLM
64K input / 4K output, streaming benchmark. The A/B disables each fusion
independently on the same code base. Prefill throughput stayed within
~2% across variants (24.1K-25.4K tokens/s). Single-run variance is about
±1%.

**Warmup.** No JIT warmup registration is used for these kernels;
required variants compile on first execution or during ACLGraph capture.
Geometry/capacity checks remain in the wrappers.

**Recompilation risk assessment.**
- *White-box*: `gated_scale` has constexpr head count/head_dim and no
autotune; runtime integers specialize only on Triton's `==1` / `%16` /
other classes, fixed per layer shape and anchor. `indexer_qkz_norm_rope`
autotunes once per (`head_dim`, `rotary_dim`) layer shape; token counts
are deliberately excluded, so prefill batch size changes do not retune.
Its runtime integers (`tokens`, strides) use the same bounded
specialization classes.
- *Black-box*: on Ascend 950DT, token counts 64 / 333 / 1024 / 4096 all
reuse one autotune key (`head_dim=256`, `rotary_dim=16`); no per-batch
retune was observed. `do_not_specialize` is not needed because the
specialization classes are few and fixed in serving.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: decode-1 / odd-333 /
prefill-4096 tokens, both supported head dims, TP16/TP8/TP4 head counts,
gate columns past the base's logical width, zero-offset and packed
bases, out-of-range offset assertion, RoPE pos-0 identity.
- [ ] **Regression test**: not a bugfix; both tests assert equivalence
with the exact eager expressions being replaced (including the
historical pos-0 RoPE layout failure).
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: out-of-range `gate_col_offset`
raises; indexer wrapper rejects shape/dtype mismatches with loud errors.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: pure-torch references mirror the
eager numerics; tolerances follow the repository criterion, no CI-only
assertions.
- [x] **Performance impact**: internal benchmark numbers above (matched
conditions), and the operator docs record the per-layer kernel/copy
eliminations.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Single-operator accuracy test for the Step5 gated_scale Triton op.
+
+Compares the fused kernel output against the eager path it replaces:
+``attn_output.view(t, H, D) * gate.unsqueeze(-1).sigmoid()``. The gate is
+exercised in every layout the model feeds the single base+offset
+interface: a strided column view of a wider packed buffer with the packed
+buffer itself as base (the sliding-window qkvg layout), the same view with
+the buffer's front row-slice as base (the DSA qkv layout, where the gate
+columns live past the base's logical width), and a standalone contiguous
+gate with offset zero (the sliding-window g_proj fallback layout), so the
+kernel's addressing is covered end to end.
+
+Accuracy follows the repository operator criterion for the bf16 output:
+rtol = atol = 2^-6, at least 99% of elements within the combined tolerance,
+and the maximum absolute error <= 1. Shape coverage uses the real Step5
+attention geometry (head_dim 192 and the other supported 128; per-rank head
+counts 4/8/16 for TP16/TP8/TP4 on the 64-head checkpoint) with token counts
+spanning single-token decode, an odd boundary and a prefill chunk.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm_ascend.device.device_config import get_ascend_device_type
+from vllm_ascend.device.hardware import AscendDeviceType
+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.step5.gated_scale import gated_scale
+
+RTOL = 2.0**-6
+ATOL = 2.0**-6
+MAX_ABS_ERR = 1.0
+MIN_WITHIN_FRACTION = 0.99
+
+
+def _reference(attn_output: torch.Tensor, gate: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    num_tokens = attn_output.shape[0]
+    num_heads = gate.shape[-1]
+    head_dim = attn_output.shape[-1] // num_heads
+    return (attn_output.view(num_tokens, num_heads, head_dim) * gate.unsqueeze(-1).sigmoid()).view(num_tokens, -1)
+
+
+def _assert_bf16_close(actual: torch.Tensor, ref: torch.Tensor, name: str = "out") -> None:
+    a = actual.float()
+    r = ref.float()
+    diff = (a - r).abs()
+    within = diff <= ATOL + RTOL * r.abs()
+    frac = within.float().mean().item()
+    assert frac >= MIN_WITHIN_FRACTION, (
+        f"{name}: only {frac:.4%} elements within BF16 tolerance (max abs err {diff.max().item():.6f})"
+    )
+    assert diff.max().item() <= MAX_ABS_ERR, f"{name}: max abs err {diff.max().item():.6f} exceeds {MAX_ABS_ERR}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 333, 4096])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_heads", [4, 8, 16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_dim", [128, 192])
+def test_gated_scale_standalone_gate(num_tokens: int, num_heads: int, head_dim: int):
+    """g_proj layout: contiguous gate as its own base, offset 0."""
+    device = "npu"
+
+    torch.manual_seed(123)
+    attn_output = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads * head_dim, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    gate = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    out = gated_scale(attn_output, gate, 0, num_heads)
+    ref = _reference(attn_output.clone(), gate.clone())
+
+    assert out.shape == attn_output.shape and out.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    _assert_bf16_close(out, ref)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 4096])
+def test_gated_scale_packed_base_gate(num_tokens: int):
+    """qkvg layout: gate as a strided column view, packed buffer as base."""
+    device = "npu"
+    num_heads, head_dim = 8, 192
+
+    torch.manual_seed(123)
+    kv_width = 2 * head_dim
+    row_width = num_heads * head_dim + kv_width + num_heads
+    packed = torch.randn(num_tokens, row_width, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    attn_output = packed[..., : num_heads * head_dim].contiguous()
+    gate = packed[..., -num_heads:]
+    assert gate.storage_offset() != 0
+
+    out = gated_scale(attn_output, packed, gate.storage_offset(), num_heads)
+    ref = _reference(attn_output.clone(), gate.contiguous())
+
+    _assert_bf16_close(out, ref)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 333, 4096])
+def test_gated_scale_front_slice_base_gate(num_tokens: int):
+    """DSA layout: front row-slice as base, gate beyond its logical width.
+
+    The gate columns live past the base's shape but inside its storage
+    row span, exactly how the DSA layer reads the gate tail of the fused
+    qkv+indexer row through the offset-0 qkv view.
+    """
+    device = "npu"
+    num_heads, head_dim = 8, 192
+
+    torch.manual_seed(123)
+    indexer_width = 4 * 256
+    qkv_width = num_heads * head_dim
+    combined = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens,
+        qkv_width + indexer_width + num_heads,
+        device=device,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+    )
+    gate_view = combined[..., -num_heads:]
+    qkv = combined[..., :qkv_width]
+    assert qkv.storage_offset() == 0
+    assert gate_view.storage_offset() >= qkv_width
+
+    attn_output = torch.randn(num_tokens, qkv_width, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    out = gated_scale(attn_output, qkv, gate_view.storage_offset(), num_heads)
+    ref = _reference(attn_output.clone(), gate_view.contiguous())
+
+    _assert_bf16_close(out, ref)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_heads", [8, 16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("head_dim", [128, 192])
+def test_gated_scale_eager_equivalence(num_heads: int, head_dim: int):
+    """The fused path must match the eager math per input element."""
+    device = "npu"
+
+    torch.manual_seed(123)
+    num_tokens = 333
+    row_width = num_heads * head_dim + num_heads
+    packed = torch.randn(num_tokens, row_width, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    attn_output = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads * head_dim, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    gate = packed[..., -num_heads:]
+
+    out = gated_scale(attn_output, packed, row_width - num_heads, num_heads)
+    ref = _reference(attn_output.clone(), gate.contiguous())
+
+    _assert_bf16_close(out, ref)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+def test_gated_scale_bounds_check():
+    """Out-of-range offsets must fail loudly instead of reading garbage."""
+    device = "npu"
+
+    num_heads, head_dim = 8, 192
+    packed = torch.randn(8, num_heads * head_dim + 4, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    attn_output = torch.randn(8, num_heads * head_dim, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
+        # offset + num_heads exceeds the base's row span.
+        gated_scale(attn_output, packed, packed.shape[1] - 4, num_heads)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+def test_gated_scale_empty_input():
+    """Zero tokens must return an empty output without launching a zero-sized grid."""
+    device = "npu"
+    num_heads, head_dim = 8, 192
+    attn_output = torch.empty((0, num_heads * head_dim), device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    gate = torch.empty((0, num_heads), device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    out = gated_scale(attn_output, gate, 0, num_heads)
+
+    assert out.shape == attn_output.shape
+    assert out.dtype == attn_output.dtype
+    assert out.numel() == 0

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Single-operator accuracy test for the Step5 fused indexer QKZ norm+RoPE op.
+
+Compares the fused kernel against a pure-torch reference replicating the
+module's eager path (``AscendStep5DSAAttention._finish_indexer``):
+- index_q: per-head RMSNorm (zero_centered -> weight + 1), no mean subtract
+- index_k: per-head LayerNorm (subtract mean, with bias)
+- NeoX RoPE on the first ``rotary_dim`` dims = rotary_dim//2 pairs
+  (pair layout: dims i and i + rotary_dim//2), angles from the caller's
+  cos/sin cache whose row width is rotary_dim//2.
+- index_z: passthrough copy.
+
+The inputs are the strided ``split`` views of one packed row -- the
+production layout (the ``split_indexer`` slices of the fused qkv+indexer
+GEMM output), so the kernel's in-place strided reads are covered.
+
+Accuracy follows the repository operator criterion: index_k (bf16) uses
+rtol = atol = 2^-6 with max abs error <= 1; index_q lands in e4m3
+(quantized at the kernel store) and is compared against the reference cast
+to the same dtype under rtol = 2^-3, atol = 2^-6, max abs error 4.0 (the
+criterion's max(fixed_limit, 32 * ULP(1.0)) rule with the 3-bit e4m3
+mantissa); both require at least 99% of elements within tolerance.
+index_z is a bit-exact passthrough.
+
+Regression coverage for the layout bug where the kernel treated
+``rotary_dim`` as a pair count: with sparse_indexer_rope_dim=32 it read
+dims 32-63 as the imaginary half and ran cache lookups past the 16-wide row
+into the next position's angles (the pos-0 identity test fails loudly on
+that bug).
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm_ascend.device.device_config import get_ascend_device_type
+from vllm_ascend.device.hardware import AscendDeviceType
+from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.step5.indexer_qkz_norm_rope import (
+    fused_indexer_qkz_norm_rope,
+)
+
+HEAD_DIM = 256  # proxy_dim
+ROTARY_DIM = 32  # sparse_indexer_rope_dim: 32 dims = 16 pairs
+EPS = 1e-6
+THETA = 10000000.0  # indexer rope_theta (DSA layers)
+
+# BF16 output criterion (repository operator standard).
+BF16_RTOL = 2.0**-6
+BF16_ATOL = 2.0**-6
+BF16_MAX_ABS_ERR = 1.0
+MIN_WITHIN_FRACTION = 0.99
+
+# index_q lands in e4m3 (quantized at the store). The repository criterion's
+# maximum-error rule is max(fixed_limit, 32 * ULP(1.0)); e4m3 has a 3-bit
+# mantissa, so ULP(1.0) = 2^-3 and the two quantizations may differ by one
+# code, bounded by rtol = 2^-3, atol = 2^-6 (near-zero slack), max abs 4.0.
+FP8_RTOL = 2.0**-3
+FP8_ATOL = 2.0**-6
+FP8_MAX_ABS_ERR = 4.0
+
+
+def _assert_close(
+    actual: torch.Tensor,
+    ref: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    rtol: float,
+    atol: float,
+    max_abs_err: float,
+    name: str,
+) -> None:
+    a = actual.float()
+    r = ref.float()
+    diff = (a - r).abs()
+    within = diff <= atol + rtol * r.abs()
+    frac = within.float().mean().item()
+    assert frac >= MIN_WITHIN_FRACTION, (
+        f"{name}: only {frac:.4%} elements within tolerance (max abs err {diff.max().item():.6f})"
+    )
+    assert diff.max().item() <= max_abs_err, f"{name}: max abs err {diff.max().item():.6f} exceeds {max_abs_err}"
+
+
+def _build_cos_sin_cache(max_pos: int, pairs: int, theta: float, device):
+    """Production [cos | sin] cache; callers may chunk it for references."""
+    idx = torch.arange(0, 2 * pairs, 2, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    inv_freq = 1.0 / (theta ** (idx / (2 * pairs)))
+    pos = torch.arange(max_pos, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    freqs = torch.outer(pos, inv_freq)
+    cache = torch.cat([freqs.cos(), freqs.sin()], dim=-1).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    return cache
+
+
+def _reference_indexer_norm_rope(
+    index_q: torch.Tensor,
+    index_k: torch.Tensor,
+    index_z: torch.Tensor,
+    q_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    k_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    k_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    cos: torch.Tensor,
+    sin: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    head_dim: int,
+    num_q_heads: int,
+    num_k_heads: int,
+    rotary_dim: int,
+    eps: float,
+    q_norm_weight_bias: float,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    tokens = index_q.shape[0]
+    dtype = index_q.dtype
+
+    def rms_norm(x_flat: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        x = x_flat.view(tokens, -1, head_dim).float()
+        variance = x.pow(2).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        normed = x * torch.rsqrt(variance + eps)
+        return (normed * (q_weight.float() + q_norm_weight_bias)).to(dtype)
+
+    def layer_norm(x_flat: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        x = x_flat.view(tokens, -1, head_dim).float()
+        mean = x.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        variance = x.var(dim=-1, unbiased=False, keepdim=True)
+        normed = (x - mean) * torch.rsqrt(variance + eps)
+        return (normed * k_weight.float() + k_bias.float()).to(dtype)
+
+    q = rms_norm(index_q)
+    k = layer_norm(index_k)
+
+    half = rotary_dim // 2
+
+    def apply_rope(x_flat: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        x = x_flat.view(tokens, -1, head_dim).float()
+        x1 = x[..., :half]
+        x2 = x[..., half:rotary_dim]
+        cos_t = cos[positions.long()].float()[:, None, :]
+        sin_t = sin[positions.long()].float()[:, None, :]
+        out = x.clone()
+        out[..., :half] = x1 * cos_t - x2 * sin_t
+        out[..., half:rotary_dim] = x1 * sin_t + x2 * cos_t
+        return out.to(dtype).view(x_flat.shape)
+
+    return apply_rope(q).view(tokens, -1), apply_rope(k).view(tokens, -1), index_z.clone()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 333, 4096])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_q_heads,num_k_heads", [(1, 1), (4, 1), (16, 1)])
+def test_fused_indexer_norm_rope_accuracy(num_tokens: int, num_q_heads: int, num_k_heads: int):
+    """Real Step5 geometry: 4 local Q heads (16 / index_tp_size=4), 1 K head;
+    16 is the unsharded (index TP=1) case and 1 the sharded boundary."""
+    device = "npu"
+
+    max_pos = 4096
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    q_len = num_q_heads * HEAD_DIM
+    k_len = num_k_heads * HEAD_DIM
+    x_cat = torch.randn(num_tokens, q_len + 2 * k_len, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    q_weight = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_weight = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_bias = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    positions = torch.randint(0, max_pos, (num_tokens,), device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    cos_sin_cache = _build_cos_sin_cache(max_pos, ROTARY_DIM // 2, THETA, device)
+    cos, sin = cos_sin_cache.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+
+    index_q, index_k, index_z = x_cat.split([q_len, k_len, k_len], dim=-1)
+    # Verify the inputs are views from a single tensor, not contiguous copies.
+    # index_q is the offset-0 slice (its data_ptr equals x_cat's); index_k and
+    # index_z sit at positive offsets.
+    assert index_q.storage().data_ptr() == x_cat.storage().data_ptr()
+    assert index_k.storage().data_ptr() == x_cat.storage().data_ptr()
+    assert index_z.storage().data_ptr() == x_cat.storage().data_ptr()
+    assert index_k.data_ptr() != x_cat.data_ptr()
+    assert index_z.data_ptr() != x_cat.data_ptr()
+
+    q_ref, k_ref, z_ref = _reference_indexer_norm_rope(
+        index_q,
+        index_k,
+        index_z,
+        q_weight,
+        k_weight,
+        k_bias,
+        cos,
+        sin,
+        positions,
+        head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+        num_q_heads=num_q_heads,
+        num_k_heads=num_k_heads,
+        rotary_dim=ROTARY_DIM,
+        eps=EPS,
+        q_norm_weight_bias=1.0,
+    )
+
+    q_out, k_out, z_out = fused_indexer_qkz_norm_rope(
+        index_q,
+        index_k,
+        index_z,
+        q_weight,
+        k_weight,
+        cos_sin_cache,
+        positions,
+        k_norm_bias=k_bias,
+        head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+        num_q_heads=num_q_heads,
+        num_k_heads=num_k_heads,
+        rotary_dim=ROTARY_DIM,
+        eps=EPS,
+        q_norm_weight_bias=1.0,
+    )
+
+    # index_q is e4m3 (quantized at the kernel store): compare against the
+    # reference cast to the same dtype under the e4m3 criterion.
+    q_ref8 = q_ref.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    assert q_out.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    _assert_close(q_out, q_ref8, rtol=FP8_RTOL, atol=FP8_ATOL, max_abs_err=FP8_MAX_ABS_ERR, name="Q")
+    _assert_close(k_out, k_ref, rtol=BF16_RTOL, atol=BF16_ATOL, max_abs_err=BF16_MAX_ABS_ERR, name="K")
+    assert torch.equal(z_ref, z_out), "Z passthrough mismatch"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+def test_fused_indexer_norm_rope_pos0_is_identity():
+    """At position 0 the rope angles are 0: rotated dims must equal the
+    normalized values. The buggy pair/dims layout already failed here (the
+    imaginary half landed outside the rotated window and cache reads ran
+    into the next position's angles)."""
+    device = "npu"
+
+    num_tokens, num_q_heads, num_k_heads = 4, 4, 1
+    torch.manual_seed(7)
+    q_len = num_q_heads * HEAD_DIM
+    k_len = num_k_heads * HEAD_DIM
+    x_cat = torch.randn(num_tokens, q_len + 2 * k_len, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    q_weight = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_weight = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_bias = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    positions = torch.zeros(num_tokens, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    cos_sin_cache = _build_cos_sin_cache(8, ROTARY_DIM // 2, THETA, device)
+    cos, sin = cos_sin_cache.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+
+    index_q, index_k, index_z = x_cat.split([q_len, k_len, k_len], dim=-1)
+
+    q_ref, k_ref, _ = _reference_indexer_norm_rope(
+        index_q,
+        index_k,
+        index_z,
+        q_weight,
+        k_weight,
+        k_bias,
+        cos,
+        sin,
+        positions,
+        head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+        num_q_heads=num_q_heads,
+        num_k_heads=num_k_heads,
+        rotary_dim=ROTARY_DIM,
+        eps=EPS,
+        q_norm_weight_bias=1.0,
+    )
+    q_out, k_out, _ = fused_indexer_qkz_norm_rope(
+        index_q,
+        index_k,
+        index_z,
+        q_weight,
+        k_weight,
+        cos_sin_cache,
+        positions,
+        k_norm_bias=k_bias,
+        head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+        num_q_heads=num_q_heads,
+        num_k_heads=num_k_heads,
+        rotary_dim=ROTARY_DIM,
+        eps=EPS,
+        q_norm_weight_bias=1.0,
+    )
+    # index_q is e4m3; one-ULP tolerance for the quantized comparison.
+    q_ref8 = q_ref.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    assert q_out.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    _assert_close(q_out, q_ref8, rtol=FP8_RTOL, atol=FP8_ATOL, max_abs_err=FP8_MAX_ABS_ERR, name="Q")
+    _assert_close(k_out, k_ref, rtol=BF16_RTOL, atol=BF16_ATOL, max_abs_err=BF16_MAX_ABS_ERR, name="K")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    get_ascend_device_type() != AscendDeviceType.A5,
+    reason="Requires Ascend A5",
+)
+def test_fused_indexer_norm_rope_empty_input():
+    """Zero tokens must return correctly typed empty outputs without a zero-sized grid."""
+    device = "npu"
+    num_q_heads, num_k_heads = 4, 1
+    q_len = num_q_heads * HEAD_DIM
+    k_len = num_k_heads * HEAD_DIM
+    x_cat = torch.empty((0, q_len + 2 * k_len), device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    index_q, index_k, index_z = x_cat.split([q_len, k_len, k_len], dim=-1)
+    q_weight = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_weight = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_bias = torch.randn(HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    cos_sin_cache = _build_cos_sin_cache(8, ROTARY_DIM // 2, THETA, device)
+    cos, sin = cos_sin_cache.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    positions = torch.empty((0,), device=device, dtype=torch.int32)

+# Step5 gated_scale
+
+## Description
+
+- **Function**: Applies the Step5 head-wise attention gate — sigmoid over
+  per-head gate logits broadcast-multiplied onto the attention output — in
+  one Triton kernel: `out[t, h, :] = attn[t, h, :] * sigmoid(gate[t, h])`.
+  It replaces the eager post-attention chain
+  `attn_output.view(t, H, D) * gate.unsqueeze(-1).sigmoid()` (two eager
+  kernels plus a materializing copy) with a single fused kernel. The
+  sigmoid and the multiply run in fp32, which is at least as accurate as
+  the bf16 eager path. The wrapper is registered as the custom op
+  `ascend_step5_gated_scale`
+  (`vllm.triton_utils.direct_register_custom_op`), so it is callable
+  through `torch.ops.vllm.ascend_step5_gated_scale` and safe for
+  torch.compile.
+- **Location**: `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/step5/gated_scale.py` — kernel
+  `_gated_scale_kernel`, wrapper `gated_scale`. Production callers:
+  `vllm_ascend/models/step5/model.py` (`AscendStep5DSAAttention.forward`
+  and `AscendStep5Attention.forward`), selected whenever the layer's
+  `use_head_wise_attn_gate` produces a gate. **Scope**: model-specific to
+  Step5-Preview; not a framework-wide primitive.
+- **Formula**: the gate is addressed through an **offset-0 base tensor plus
+  a scalar column offset**:
+    - `out[t] = attn[t] * sigmoid(base[t, gate_col_offset : gate_col_offset + H])`,
+      where `attn` is `[num_tokens, H * D]` viewed per head and `base` is
+      any tensor sharing the gate's storage with `storage_offset == 0`.
+    - DSA layers: the gate is the tail of the fused qkv+indexer GEMM row;
+      the base is the offset-0 `qkv` front view of that same row, so the
+      gate columns lie beyond the base's logical width but inside its
+      storage row span (`gate_col_offset = gate.storage_offset()`).
+    - Sliding-window layers: the packed `qkvg` GEMM output is the base when
+      `fuse_qkv_gate` packs q/k/v/gate into one GEMM, with
+      `gate_col_offset = q_size + 2 * kv_size`; otherwise the standalone
+      `g_proj` output is its own base with `gate_col_offset = 0`.
+    - Handing a mid-storage gate view to the op boundary instead would make
+      the dispatch layer materialize it first (TensorMove); callers declare
+      the layout explicitly and no materializing copy is issued.
+- **Algorithm flow** (one token row per program):
+    1. Grid `(num_tokens, cdiv(H, BLOCK_H))`; each program owns one token
+       and a `BLOCK_H`-wide head block (`BLOCK_H` sized to keep one token
+       row's gate+attention lanes within a 4096-lane budget).
+    2. Load the `BLOCK_H` gate logits at `base + t * stride + offset + h`,
+       sigmoid in fp32.
+    3. Load the `(BLOCK_H, BLOCK_D)` attention tile, multiply by the
+       per-head gate in fp32, store bf16 with head/dim masking.
+- **Supported modes**: Ascend 950PR/950DT (A5) on the Triton-Ascend
+  backend; execution evidence on Ascend950DT / 951DT. Atlas A2/A3 are not
+  validated for this operator (the Step5-Preview model itself is
+  A5-targeted); no A2/A3-incompatible construct is used (plain Triton
+  elementwise math), so porting is gated on hardware validation rather
+  than on code changes. Eager and ACLGraph decode capture paths both work
+  (the wrapper allocates the output and derives the grid from shapes
+  only). Any `num_heads` / `head_dim` combination is handled through
+  masking; per-token grids need no padding.
+
+## Parameters
+
+| Parameter | Input/Output/Attribute | Description | Data type | Data format |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `attn_output` | Input | Attention output to gate, `[num_tokens, num_heads * head_dim]` | bf16 | ND, row-major; row stride passed to the kernel |
+| `gate_base` | Input | Offset-0 tensor sharing the gate's storage; the gate is read as `gate_base[t, offset : offset + num_heads]` | bf16 | ND, row stride passed to the kernel |
+| `gate_col_offset` | Input | Scalar column offset of the gate inside `gate_base`'s storage row | int | - |
+| `num_heads` | Input | Gate width (heads), must satisfy `gate_col_offset + num_heads <= gate_base.stride(0)` | int | - |
+| return | Output | Gated attention output, same shape/dtype as `attn_output` | bf16 | ND |
+
+## Constraints
+
+- `gate_col_offset >= 0` and `gate_col_offset + num_heads <= gate_base.stride(0)`:
+  gate columns must stay inside the base's storage row span. Violations
+  fail loudly (assertion) instead of reading garbage.
+- `gate_base` must have `storage_offset == 0` and share the gate's storage;
+  the row stride used for addressing is `gate_base.stride(0)`, so a front
+  row-slice of a wider packed GEMM row qualifies and the gate tail is read
+  in place beyond the base's logical width.
+- `attn_output` is 2-D `[num_tokens, num_heads * head_dim]`;
+  `head_dim` is derived as `attn_output.shape[-1] // num_heads`.
+- In-place behavior: none. Inputs are read-only; the output is freshly
+  allocated. The op is registered with `mutates_args=[]`.
+- Specialization / recompilation profile: the grid varies with
+  `num_tokens`, so batch size changes never recompile (grid changes are not
+  part of the cache key). Compile-time specialization comes from the
+  `constexpr` head counts (required: grid and masks derive from them) and
+  from Triton's value/alignment classes of the runtime integer arguments
+  (`attn_output.stride(0)`, `gate_base.stride(0)`, `gate_col_offset`,
+  `out.stride(0)`; classes are `==1`, multiples of 16, other). All of those
+  are fixed per layer shape and anchor kind in serving (two anchors per
+  model: the DSA `qkv` view and the sliding-window `qkvg`/`g_proj` base),
+  so the steady-state variant set is one per (layer shape, anchor) pair —
+  no per-request compilation. `do_not_specialize` is deliberately not used:
+  the specializations are few, fixed and beneficial (alignment feeds
+  vectorization).
+
+## Origin and Differences
+
+- **Origin**: Adapted from the Step5 eager post-attention gate in vLLM
+  (`attn_output.view(t, H, D) * gate.unsqueeze(-1).sigmoid()`), fused the
+  same way the step4 internal `fuse-gate-chain` branch fused it for the
+  Step5 tailring deployment.
+- **Differences**:
+    - The eager path materializes the gate view at the op boundary and
+      launches a sigmoid kernel plus a broadcast multiply; the fused kernel
+      reads the gate in place through the offset-0 base (no TensorMove) and
+      runs both stages in fp32 in one launch.
+    - Numerics: fp32 sigmoid and multiply are at least as accurate as the
+      bf16 eager chain; output is rounded back to bf16 once.
+    - Upstream CUDA counterpart
+      (`vllm/models/step5/nvidia/ops/attention_gate.py::headwise_sigmoid_gate`):
+      same post-attention fallback role, but it reproduces the eager
+      numerics bit-for-bit (sigmoid re-rounded to the gate dtype before the
+      multiply, `enable_fp_fusion=False`) and supports an active-row mask
+      for CUDA-graph slot handling. This kernel keeps the full-fp32 chain
+      (one final rounding) and handles the padded rows through the caller's
+      zero-weight padding instead. The deeper upstream fusion (the gate
+      folded into the attention kernel epilogue via `dsa_gate` /
+      `forward_with_headwise_gate`) is a follow-up opportunity for the
+      Ascend block-sparse attention operators; this op mirrors upstream's
+      post-attention fallback tier first.
+    - Exposed as a registered custom op (`ascend_step5_gated_scale`) so the
+      fused call is torch.compile-friendly and has a registered fake impl.
+
+## Test Cases
+
+Single-operator accuracy tests compare the kernel against the eager path
+it replaces (`attn_output.view(t, H, D) * gate.unsqueeze(-1).sigmoid()`)
+under the repository bf16 criterion (`rtol = atol = 2^-6`, at least 99% of
+elements within tolerance, max abs error <= 1). The gate is exercised in
+every layout the model feeds the base+offset interface: a standalone
+contiguous gate with offset zero (the sliding-window `g_proj` layout), a
+strided column view of a wider packed buffer with the buffer itself as
+base (the `qkvg` layout), and the same view with the buffer's front
+row-slice as base (the DSA `qkv` layout, where the gate columns live past
+the base's logical width). Shapes use the real Step5 attention geometry
+(head_dim 192 plus the other supported 128; per-rank head counts 4/8/16
+for TP16/TP8/TP4 on the 64-head checkpoint) with token counts spanning
+single-token decode, an odd boundary and a prefill chunk; an out-of-range
+offset must fail loudly, and zero-token inputs return an empty output
+without launching a kernel.
+
+```bash
+pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_step5_gated_scale.py
+```
