+# Step5 indexer_qkz_norm_rope
+
+## Description
+
+- **Function**: Fuses the Step5 sparse-indexer post-projection chain of the
+  DSA layers — per-head RMSNorm on `index_q`, per-head LayerNorm on
+  `index_k`, NeoX RoPE on both, and a contiguous copy of `index_z` — into a
+  single Triton kernel. It replaces the eager chain in
+  `AscendStep5DSAAttention._finish_indexer`
+  (`k_norm -> q_norm -> rotary_emb -> contiguous(z)`), which materialized
+  every intermediate back to global memory and forced contiguous copies of
+  the strided `split_indexer` views. The kernel reads the three inputs in
+  place through their row strides (the production inputs are the
+  `split_indexer` slices of one packed qkv+indexer GEMM row), so no
+  materializing copy is issued on any input. `index_q` is stored as
+  `float8_e4m3fn`: its only consumer (the fused indexer scoring,
+  `indexer_score_topk` via `indexer_region_score`) wants fp8, so the
+  quantization rides along with the norm+RoPE store instead of a separate
+  cast at the scoring entry. The wrapper is a plain Python call into the Triton
+  kernel; Step5 currently runs with `do_not_compile`. Once the outer
+  `step5_sparse_attention_forward` custom op from #22342 is in place, that
+  op provides the torch.compile boundary.
+- **Location**: `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/step5/indexer_qkz_norm_rope.py` —
+  kernel `_indexer_qkz_norm_rope_kernel`, wrapper
+  `fused_indexer_qkz_norm_rope`. Production caller:
+  `vllm_ascend/models/step5/model.py`
+  (`AscendStep5DSAAttention._finish_indexer`), selected when
+  `0 < sparse_indexer_rope_dim < proxy_dim` (the production partial-RoPE
+  geometry). **Scope**: model-specific to Step5-Preview's dense-sparse
+  attention (DSA) layers; not a framework-wide primitive.
+- **Formula**:
+    - Input `index_q`: `[tokens, num_q_heads * head_dim]` (head_dim =
+      `proxy_dim`, 256 in production); `index_k` / `index_z`:
+      `[tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim]`. All three may be strided column
+      views of one packed buffer.
+    - index_q: RMSNorm per head over `D = head_dim`, fp32 reduction,
+      zero-centered weights add 1.0 (`q_norm_weight_bias`), no mean
+      subtraction, no bias: `y = x * rsqrt(mean(x^2) + eps) * (w + 1.0)`.
+    - index_k: LayerNorm per head (mean subtracted, optional bias):
+      `y = (x - mean) * rsqrt(var + eps) * w + b`.
+    - NeoX RoPE over the first `rotary_dim` dims = `rotary_dim // 2` pairs
+      (pair layout: dims `i` and `i + rotary_dim // 2`):
+      `out1 = y1*cos - y2*sin`, `out2 = y1*sin + y2*cos`; angles are read
+      from a single caller-provided `[cos | sin]` cache (last dimension
+      `rotary_dim`), rows gathered by `positions`; the sin half is
+      addressed as `cos + rotary_dim // 2`. The normed values are rounded to the input
+      dtype (bf16) before rotation, rotated in fp32 (matches the eager
+      path's dtype handoffs).
+    - Stores round through the input precision first (bf16 -> output
+      dtype), so index_q reproduces the unfused pipeline's bits
+      (kernel-store bf16 -> `.to(float8_e4m3fn)` cast) up to one e4m3 ULP;
+      same-dtype outputs take the second cast as a no-op. `index_z` is a
+      bit-exact passthrough.
+- **Algorithm flow** (persistent-style grid over tokens):
+   1. Grid `min(max(tiles_q, tiles_kz), num_vector_cores)`;
+      `ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q` / `ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ` are selected once per
+      layer shape (`head_dim`, `rotary_dim`) and reused for all token
+      counts, instead of being tuned again for each token-count bucket.
+   2. Q stage: each program loops over its token tiles; per tile the
+       head axis is chunked (`H_CHUNK` sized to a 4096-lane budget) and
+       each chunk is normed, rotated and stored through block pointers.
+   3. K stage rides the same traversal and additionally copies the Z rows
+       bit-exact (block-pointer load/store).
+- **Supported modes**: Ascend 950PR/950DT (A5) on the Triton-Ascend
+  backend; execution evidence on Ascend950DT. Atlas A2/A3 are not validated
+  for this operator (it uses the Triton-Ascend CANN `extension`
+  slice/compile-hint intrinsics and `num_vectorcore`), matching the other
+  Step5 operators. Eager and ACLGraph decode capture both work (the
+  wrapper allocates outputs and derives the grid from shapes only). The
+  fused path handles the configuration's allowed even `rotary_dim` values
+  up to `proxy_dim`; there is no eager fallback.
+
+## Parameters
+
+| Parameter | Input/Output/Attribute | Description | Data type | Data format |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `index_q` | Input | Indexer Q logits, `[tokens, num_q_heads * head_dim]` | bf16 | ND; may be a strided view, row stride passed to the kernel |
+| `index_k` | Input | Indexer K logits, `[tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim]` | bf16 | ND; may be a strided view |
+| `index_z` | Input | Indexer Z values, `[tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim]` | bf16 | ND; may be a strided view |
+| `q_norm_weight` | Input | Per-head RMSNorm scale for Q, `[head_dim]` | bf16 | ND (1-D) |
+| `k_norm_weight` | Input | Per-head LayerNorm scale for K, `[head_dim]` | bf16 | ND (1-D) |
+| `cos_sin_cache` | Input | Single `[cos \| sin]` cache for the indexer RoPE (last dim = `rotary_dim`); row stride passed to the kernel | bf16 | ND 2-D `[max_pos, rotary_dim]` |
+| `positions` | Input | Absolute position of each token | int32 / int64 | ND (1-D) |
+| `k_norm_bias` | Input | Required LayerNorm bias for K | bf16 | ND (1-D) |
+| `head_dim` | Attribute | Per-head width (`proxy_dim`, 256 in production) | int | - |
+| `num_q_heads` | Attribute | Local index Q heads (constexpr) | int | - |
+| `num_k_heads` | Attribute | Local index K heads (constexpr) | int | - |
+| `rotary_dim` | Attribute | Rotated dim count (`sparse_indexer_rope_dim`, 32 in production); converted to NeoX pairs internally | int | - |
+| `eps` | Attribute | Norm epsilon (default `1e-6`) | float | - |
+| `q_norm_weight_bias` | Attribute | Added to the Q norm scale: `1.0` for zero-centered weights, `0.0` otherwise | float | - |
+| return `index_q` | Output | `[tokens, num_q_heads * head_dim]`, normed + rotated, **float8_e4m3fn** (quantized at the store) | fp8 | ND |
+| return `index_k` | Output | `[tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim]`, normed + rotated | bf16 | ND |
+| return `index_z` | Output | `[tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim]`, bit-exact passthrough | bf16 | ND |
+
+## Constraints
+
+- `rotary_dim` must be even and `> 0`; it is a **dim count** (32 in
+  production), converted to `rotary_dim // 2` NeoX pairs internally. Passing
+  a pair count here historically corrupted the layout (imag half on dims
+  32-63 and cross-row cache reads); the pos-0 identity test guards it.
+- `index_q/k/z` must share the same token count; `index_q` width must equal
+  `num_q_heads * head_dim`, `index_k`/`index_z` widths `num_k_heads *
+  head_dim` (validated with loud errors).
+- `cos_sin_cache` must use the `[cos | sin]` layout with last dimension
+  exactly `rotary_dim`; `positions` must index valid rows.
+- `rotary_dim <= head_dim`.
+- Specialization / recompilation profile: compile-time specialization
+  comes from the `constexpr` head counts and flags (required: head chunking
+  and the static head loops derive from them; fixed per layer shape) and
+  from Triton's value/alignment classes of the runtime integer arguments
+  (`tokens`, the strides; classes `==1`, multiples of 16, other). The
+  autotuner keys only on `head_dim` and `rotary_dim`, deliberately excluding
+  token counts: the first call at each layer shape benchmarks the config
+  list once, and all subsequent token counts reuse that selection instead
+  of tuning again per batch. The selected configuration therefore depends on
+  the first batch seen by the process; this is a performance trade-off, not
+  a numerical difference. `do_not_specialize` is not used (the classes are
+  few, fixed in serving, and the alignment specialization feeds
+  vectorization).
+- In-place behavior: none. Inputs are read-only (strided reads are
+  supported); outputs are freshly allocated.
+
+## Origin and Differences
+
+- **Origin**: Adapted from the Step5 eager indexer chain in vLLM
+  (`index_k_norm -> index_q_norm -> sparse_indexer_rotary_emb` plus the Z
+  copy), fused for the tailring-npu deployment (internal
+  `fuse-kv-write-qknorm` / `fused-indexq-fp8` lineage) and co-designed with
+  the fused indexer scoring: the e4m3-at-store contract is what
+  `indexer_score_topk` (the aclnn IndexerRegionScore adapter) already

+    - The eager path materializes each stage (including contiguous copies

+    - Exposed as a plain Python wrapper around the Triton kernel. The

+      `step5_sparse_attention_forward` custom op once #22342 lands.
+
+## Test Cases
+
+Single-operator accuracy tests compare against a pure-torch reference
+mirroring the eager path's numerics (fp32 RMSNorm/LayerNorm, bf16 rounding
+before rotation, fp32 rotation), under the repository operator criterion:
+index_k (bf16) uses `rtol = atol = 2^-6` with max abs error <= 1; index_q

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""gated_scale -- Ascend release build (self-contained).
+
+Fused head-wise attention gate: sigmoid + broadcast multiply in one Triton
+kernel. Replaces the eager post-attention chain on Ascend --
+``attn_output.view(t, H, D) * gate.unsqueeze(-1).sigmoid()`` -- where the
+sigmoid and the multiply run in fp32, at least as accurate as the bf16 eager
+path.
+
+The gate is addressed through an offset-0 base tensor plus a scalar column
+offset: ``out[t] = attn[t] * sigmoid(base[t, off:off+H])``. The base must
+share the gate's storage and have ``storage_offset == 0`` -- for the DSA
+layers the front row-slice (the ``qkv`` view) of the fused qkv+indexer GEMM
+output, for the sliding-window layers either the packed ``qkvg`` GEMM
+output (when ``fuse_qkv_gate`` packs q/k/v/gate into one GEMM) or the
+standalone ``g_proj`` output, both with a scalar column offset. Handing a
+mid-storage gate view to the op boundary instead makes the dispatch layer
+materialize it first (TensorMove), so callers declare the layout explicitly
+and no materializing copy is issued. Gate columns may lie beyond the
+base's logical width as long as they stay inside its storage row span; the
+DSA layout reads the gate tail of the shared qkv+indexer row this way.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import direct_register_custom_op
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gated_scale_kernel(
+    attn_ptr,
+    gate_base_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    stride_attn_token,
+    gate_row_stride,
+    gate_col_offset,
+    stride_out_token,
+    NUM_HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    HEAD_DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_H: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    token = tl.program_id(0)
+    head_block = tl.program_id(1)
+    heads = head_block * BLOCK_H + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_H)
+    dims = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_D)
+    head_ok = heads < NUM_HEADS
+    dim_ok = dims < HEAD_DIM
+    mask = head_ok[:, None] & dim_ok[None, :]
+    g = tl.sigmoid(
+        tl.load(
+            gate_base_ptr + token * gate_row_stride + gate_col_offset + heads,
+            mask=head_ok,
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+    )
+    src = token * stride_attn_token + heads[:, None] * HEAD_DIM + dims[None, :]
+    x = tl.load(attn_ptr + src, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    dst = token * stride_out_token + heads[:, None] * HEAD_DIM + dims[None, :]
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + dst,
+        (x * g[:, None]).to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=mask,
+    )
+
+
+_LANE_BUDGET = 4096
+
+
+def _pick_head_block(num_heads: int, head_dim: int) -> int:
+    """Heads per program, sized to keep one token row's lanes within budget."""
+    if num_heads * head_dim <= _LANE_BUDGET:
+        return triton.next_power_of_2(num_heads)
+    return triton.next_power_of_2(max(1, min(num_heads, _LANE_BUDGET // head_dim)))
+
+
+def _gated_scale_impl(
+    attn_output: torch.Tensor,
+    gate_base: torch.Tensor,
+    gate_col_offset: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    gate_row_stride = gate_base.stride(0)
+    assert gate_col_offset >= 0 and num_heads > 0 and gate_col_offset + num_heads <= gate_row_stride, (
+        "gated_scale gate columns must stay inside the base's row span: "
+        f"offset={gate_col_offset}, num_heads={num_heads}, "
+        f"row_stride={gate_row_stride}"
+    )
+    if attn_output.shape[0] == 0:
+        return torch.empty_like(attn_output)
+    head_dim = attn_output.shape[-1] // num_heads
+    block_h = _pick_head_block(num_heads, head_dim)
+    out = torch.empty_like(attn_output)
+    _gated_scale_kernel[(attn_output.shape[0], triton.cdiv(num_heads, block_h))](
+        attn_output,
+        gate_base,
+        out,
+        attn_output.stride(0),
+        gate_row_stride,
+        gate_col_offset,
+        out.stride(0),
+        NUM_HEADS=num_heads,
+        HEAD_DIM=head_dim,
+        BLOCK_H=block_h,
+        BLOCK_D=triton.next_power_of_2(head_dim),
+    )
+    return out
+
+
+def _gated_scale_fake(
+    attn_output: torch.Tensor,
+    gate_base: torch.Tensor,
+    gate_col_offset: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return torch.empty_like(attn_output)
+
+
+direct_register_custom_op(
+    op_name="ascend_step5_gated_scale",
+    op_func=_gated_scale_impl,
+    mutates_args=[],
+    fake_impl=_gated_scale_fake,
+)
+
+
+def gated_scale(
+    attn_output: torch.Tensor,
+    gate_base: torch.Tensor,
+    gate_col_offset: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Apply the head-wise sigmoid gate: ``out[t] = attn[t] * sigmoid(gate[t])``.
+
+    ``attn_output`` is ``(tokens, num_heads * head_dim)``. The gate is
+    addressed through ``gate_base`` -- an offset-0 tensor sharing the gate's
+    storage -- as ``gate_base[t, gate_col_offset:gate_col_offset+num_heads]``.
+    The row stride is the base's own ``stride(0)``, so a front row-slice of a
+    wider packed GEMM row (the DSA ``qkv`` view) also qualifies and the kernel
+    reads the gate tail in place.
+    """
+    return torch.ops.vllm.ascend_step5_gated_scale(attn_output, gate_base, gate_col_offset, num_heads)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""indexer_qkz_norm_rope -- Ascend release build (self-contained).
+
+Independent publishable operator: the Step5 sparse-indexer Q/K norm + RoPE
+and the Z passthrough fused into one Triton kernel for Ascend (Triton-Ascend
+backend). It replaces the eager indexer chain in the DSA layers --
+per-head RMSNorm on index_q, per-head LayerNorm on index_k, NeoX RoPE on
+both, and a contiguous copy of index_z -- which materialized every
+intermediate back to global memory, with one kernel launch that reads the
+strided ``split_indexer`` views of the packed qkv+indexer GEMM output in
+place (no materializing copy on any of the three inputs).
+
+Numerical contract:
+
+- index_q: RMSNorm per head over ``head_dim`` in fp32, zero-centered weights
+  add 1.0 (``q_norm_weight_bias``), no mean subtraction, no bias; rounded to
+  the input dtype (bf16) before rotation, rotated in fp32.
+- index_k: LayerNorm per head (mean subtracted, learned ``k_norm_bias``),
+  same rounding/rotation contract.
+- RoPE: NeoX pairs over the first ``rotary_dim`` dims = ``rotary_dim // 2``
+  pairs (pair layout: dims i and i + rotary_dim // 2), angles read from the
+  a single caller-provided ``[cos | sin]`` cache (``cos_sin_cache``),
+  rows indexed by ``positions``.
+- index_q is stored as float8_e4m3fn: its only consumer (the fused indexer
+  scoring, ``indexer_score_topk``) wants fp8, so the quantization rides
+  along with the norm+rope store instead of a separate cast at the scoring
+  entry. The
+  store rounds through the input precision first (bf16 -> e4m3), which
+  reproduces the unfused pipeline's bits up to one e4m3 ULP.
+- index_k / index_z keep the input dtype (Z is a bit-exact passthrough).
+
+``rotary_dim`` follows the module convention (the number of rotated dims at
+the head of each indexer head, ``sparse_indexer_rope_dim``); the kernel works
+in NeoX pairs, so the wrapper converts dims -> pairs. Passing the dim count
+through unchanged made the kernel treat 32 dims as 32 pairs -- the
+imaginary half landed on dims 32-63 and cache reads ran past the 16-wide row
+into the next position's angles (the regression the pos-0 identity test
+guards).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+from vllm.triton_utils import HAS_TRITON, tl, triton
+
+if HAS_TRITON:
+    try:
+        import triton.language.extra.cann.extension as _extension_module  # type: ignore
+    except ImportError:
+        _extension_module = None
+
+
+def _npu_vec_core_num() -> int:
+    # Reuse the shared helper. Its initialization is idempotent, so device
+    # properties are queried only once per process rather than on every launch.
+    from vllm_ascend.ops.triton.triton_utils import (
+        get_vectorcore_num,
+        init_device_properties_triton,
+    )
+
+    init_device_properties_triton()
+    return get_vectorcore_num()
+
+
+def _pick_head_chunk(num_heads: int, head_dim: int) -> int:
+    budget_cols = 4096
+    width = num_heads * head_dim
+    if width <= budget_cols:
+        return num_heads
+    h = max(1, min(num_heads, budget_cols // head_dim))
+    return h
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _norm_rope_tile_npu_chunk(
+    x_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    cos_t,
+    sin_t,
+    token_start,
+    stride_x_token,
+    stride_out_token,
+    head_off,
+    w_hd,
+    b_hd,
+    w_real,
+    w_imag,
+    b_real,
+    b_imag,
+    eps,
+    weight_bias,
+    tokens,
+    CH: tl.constexpr,
+    TOTAL_HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    head_dim: tl.constexpr,
+    rotary_dim: tl.constexpr,
+    LAYERNORM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS_PER_PROGRAM: tl.constexpr,
+) -> None:
+    half = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)
+    half_ok = half < rotary_dim
+    gr = tl.arange(0, ROWS_PER_PROGRAM * CH)
+    tok = gr // CH
+    head = gr % CH
+    tok_abs = token_start + tok
+    row_ok = tok_abs < tokens
+    out_base = tok_abs * stride_out_token + head_off + head * head_dim
+
+    x_bp = tl.make_block_ptr(
+        base=x_ptr,
+        shape=(tokens, TOTAL_HEADS * head_dim),
+        strides=(stride_x_token, 1),
+        offsets=(token_start, head_off),
+        block_shape=(ROWS_PER_PROGRAM, CH * head_dim),
+        order=(1, 0),
+    )
+    values = tl.reshape(
+        tl.load(x_bp, boundary_check=(0,), padding_option="zero").to(tl.float32),
+        (ROWS_PER_PROGRAM * CH, head_dim),
+    )
+
+    cos = tl.reshape(
+        tl.broadcast_to(cos_t[:, None, :], (ROWS_PER_PROGRAM, CH, BLOCK_R)),
+        (ROWS_PER_PROGRAM * CH, BLOCK_R),
+    )
+    sin = tl.reshape(
+        tl.broadcast_to(sin_t[:, None, :], (ROWS_PER_PROGRAM, CH, BLOCK_R)),
+        (ROWS_PER_PROGRAM * CH, BLOCK_R),
+    )
+
+    if LAYERNORM:
+        mean = tl.sum(values, axis=1) / head_dim
+        centered = values - mean[:, None]
+        variance = tl.sum(centered * centered, axis=1) / head_dim
+    else:
+        mean = tl.zeros((ROWS_PER_PROGRAM * CH,), dtype=tl.float32)
+        variance = tl.sum(values * values, axis=1) / head_dim
+    rstd = tl.rsqrt(variance + eps)
+    result_tail = (values - mean[:, None]) * rstd[:, None] * (w_hd + weight_bias)
+    if LAYERNORM:
+        result_tail = result_tail + b_hd
+
+    if CH == 1:
+        xrow = tok_abs * stride_x_token + head_off + head * head_dim
+        real_raw = tl.load(
+            x_ptr + xrow[:, None] + half[None, :], mask=row_ok[:, None] & half_ok[None, :], other=0.0
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        imag_raw = tl.load(
+            x_ptr + xrow[:, None] + rotary_dim + half[None, :], mask=row_ok[:, None] & half_ok[None, :], other=0.0
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+    else:
+        real_raw = _extension_module.extract_slice(values, [0, 0], [ROWS_PER_PROGRAM * CH, BLOCK_R], [1, 1])
+        imag_raw = _extension_module.extract_slice(values, [0, rotary_dim], [ROWS_PER_PROGRAM * CH, BLOCK_R], [1, 1])
+    real = (real_raw - mean[:, None]) * rstd[:, None] * (w_real + weight_bias)
+    imaginary = (imag_raw - mean[:, None]) * rstd[:, None] * (w_imag + weight_bias)
+    if LAYERNORM:
+        real = real + b_real
+        imaginary = imaginary + b_imag
+    real = real.to(x_ptr.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32)
+    imaginary = imaginary.to(x_ptr.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32)
+    rotated_first = real * cos - imaginary * sin
+    rotated_second = real * sin + imaginary * cos
+
+    out_bp = tl.make_block_ptr(
+        base=out_ptr,
+        shape=(tokens, TOTAL_HEADS * head_dim),
+        strides=(stride_out_token, 1),
+        offsets=(token_start, head_off),
+        block_shape=(ROWS_PER_PROGRAM, CH * head_dim),
+        order=(1, 0),
+    )
+    # Store through the input precision first: when the output is narrower
+    # (index_q lands in e4m3 while the norm+rope math stages in bf16), the
+    # double rounding reproduces the unfused pipeline's bits exactly
+    # (kernel-store bf16 -> later .to(float8_e4m3fn) cast). Same-dtype
+    # outputs take the second cast as a no-op.
+    tl.store(
+        out_bp,
+        tl.reshape(
+            result_tail.to(x_ptr.dtype.element_ty).to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+            (ROWS_PER_PROGRAM, CH * head_dim),
+        ),
+        boundary_check=(0,),
+    )
+    mask_half = row_ok[:, None] & half_ok[None, :]
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + out_base[:, None] + half[None, :],
+        rotated_first.to(x_ptr.dtype.element_ty).to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=mask_half,
+    )
+    tl.store(
+        out_ptr + out_base[:, None] + rotary_dim + half[None, :],
+        rotated_second.to(x_ptr.dtype.element_ty).to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty),
+        mask=mask_half,
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _norm_rope_tile_npu(
+    x_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    cos_sin_cache_ptr,
+    positions_ptr,
+    token_idx,
+    token_start,
+    token_ok,
+    stride_x_token,
+    stride_out_token,
+    stride_cos,
+    w_all,
+    w_real,
+    w_imag,
+    b_all,
+    b_real,
+    b_imag,
+    eps,
+    weight_bias,
+    tokens,
+    num_heads: tl.constexpr,
+    head_dim: tl.constexpr,
+    rotary_dim: tl.constexpr,
+    LAYERNORM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS_PER_PROGRAM: tl.constexpr,
+    H_CHUNK: tl.constexpr,
+    N_FULL: tl.constexpr,
+    REM_HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+) -> None:
+    half = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)
+    half_ok = half < rotary_dim
+    w_hd = _extension_module.extract_slice(tl.reshape(w_all, (1, BLOCK_D)), [0, 0], [1, head_dim], [1, 1])
+    if LAYERNORM:
+        b_hd = _extension_module.extract_slice(tl.reshape(b_all, (1, BLOCK_D)), [0, 0], [1, head_dim], [1, 1])
+    else:
+        b_hd = tl.zeros((1, head_dim), dtype=tl.float32)
+
+    position = tl.load(positions_ptr + token_idx, mask=token_ok, other=0).to(tl.int32)
+    cos_t = tl.load(
+        cos_sin_cache_ptr + position[:, None] * stride_cos + half[None, :],
+        mask=token_ok[:, None] & half_ok[None, :],
+        other=0.0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    _extension_module.compile_hint(cos_t, "mayDiscretememaccess")
+    sin_t = tl.load(
+        cos_sin_cache_ptr + rotary_dim + position[:, None] * stride_cos + half[None, :],
+        mask=token_ok[:, None] & half_ok[None, :],
+        other=0.0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    _extension_module.compile_hint(sin_t, "mayDiscretememaccess")
+
+    for c in tl.static_range(N_FULL):
+        _norm_rope_tile_npu_chunk(
+            x_ptr,
+            out_ptr,
+            cos_t,
+            sin_t,
+            token_start,
+            stride_x_token,
+            stride_out_token,
+            c * H_CHUNK * head_dim,
+            w_hd,
+            b_hd,
+            w_real,
+            w_imag,
+            b_real,
+            b_imag,
+            eps,
+            weight_bias,
+            tokens,
+            CH=H_CHUNK,
+            TOTAL_HEADS=num_heads,
+            head_dim=head_dim,
+            rotary_dim=rotary_dim,
+            LAYERNORM=LAYERNORM,
+            BLOCK_R=BLOCK_R,
+            ROWS_PER_PROGRAM=ROWS_PER_PROGRAM,
+        )
+    if REM_HEADS > 0:
+        _norm_rope_tile_npu_chunk(
+            x_ptr,
+            out_ptr,
+            cos_t,
+            sin_t,
+            token_start,
+            stride_x_token,
+            stride_out_token,
+            N_FULL * H_CHUNK * head_dim,
+            w_hd,
+            b_hd,
+            w_real,
+            w_imag,
+            b_real,
+            b_imag,
+            eps,
+            weight_bias,
+            tokens,
+            CH=REM_HEADS,
+            TOTAL_HEADS=num_heads,
+            head_dim=head_dim,
+            rotary_dim=rotary_dim,
+            LAYERNORM=LAYERNORM,
+            BLOCK_R=BLOCK_R,
+            ROWS_PER_PROGRAM=ROWS_PER_PROGRAM,
+        )
+
+
+@triton.autotune(
+    configs=[
+        triton.Config({"ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q": q, "ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ": kv})
+        for q, kv in ((1, 2), (1, 4), (1, 8), (1, 16), (2, 2), (2, 4), (2, 8), (2, 16), (2, 32), (4, 16), (4, 32))
+    ],
+    # Token counts are intentionally excluded: tune once per layer shape and
+    # reuse the selected configuration for all subsequent token counts.
+    key=["head_dim", "rotary_dim"],
+)
+@triton.jit
+def _indexer_qkz_norm_rope_kernel(
+    x_q_ptr,
+    x_k_ptr,
+    x_z_ptr,
+    out_q_ptr,
+    out_k_ptr,
+    out_z_ptr,
+    q_weight_ptr,
+    k_weight_ptr,
+    k_bias_ptr,
+    cos_sin_cache_ptr,
+    positions_ptr,
+    tokens,
+    stride_x_q,
+    stride_x_k,
+    stride_x_z,
+    stride_out_q,
+    stride_out_k,
+    stride_cos,
+    eps,
+    weight_bias_q,
+    num_q_heads: tl.constexpr,
+    num_k_heads: tl.constexpr,
+    head_dim: tl.constexpr,
+    rotary_dim: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_D: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ: tl.constexpr,
+    H_CHUNK_Q: tl.constexpr,
+    H_CHUNK_K: tl.constexpr,
+    N_FULL_Q: tl.constexpr,
+    REM_Q: tl.constexpr,
+    N_FULL_K: tl.constexpr,
+    REM_K: tl.constexpr,
+) -> None:
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    nprog = tl.num_programs(0)
+
+    dims = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_D)
+    dim_ok = dims < head_dim
+    half = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)
+    half_ok = half < rotary_dim
+
+    w_all_q = tl.load(q_weight_ptr + dims, mask=dim_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    w_real_q = tl.load(q_weight_ptr + half, mask=half_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    w_imag_q = tl.load(q_weight_ptr + rotary_dim + half, mask=half_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    b_all_q = tl.zeros((BLOCK_D,), dtype=tl.float32)
+    b_real_q = tl.zeros((BLOCK_R,), dtype=tl.float32)
+    b_imag_q = tl.zeros((BLOCK_R,), dtype=tl.float32)
+    num_q_tiles = (tokens + ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q - 1) // ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q
+    for t in range(pid, num_q_tiles, nprog):
+        token_start = t * ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q
+        token_idx = token_start + tl.arange(0, ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q)
+        token_ok = token_idx < tokens
+        _norm_rope_tile_npu(
+            x_q_ptr,
+            out_q_ptr,
+            cos_sin_cache_ptr,
+            positions_ptr,
+            token_idx,
+            token_start,
+            token_ok,
+            stride_x_q,
+            stride_out_q,
+            stride_cos,
+            w_all_q,
+            w_real_q,
+            w_imag_q,
+            b_all_q,
+            b_real_q,
+            b_imag_q,
+            eps,
+            weight_bias_q,
+            tokens,
+            num_heads=num_q_heads,
+            head_dim=head_dim,
+            rotary_dim=rotary_dim,
+            LAYERNORM=False,
+            BLOCK_D=BLOCK_D,
+            BLOCK_R=BLOCK_R,
+            ROWS_PER_PROGRAM=ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q,
+            H_CHUNK=H_CHUNK_Q,
+            N_FULL=N_FULL_Q,
+            REM_HEADS=REM_Q,
+        )
+
+    w_all_k = tl.load(k_weight_ptr + dims, mask=dim_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    w_real_k = tl.load(k_weight_ptr + half, mask=half_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    w_imag_k = tl.load(k_weight_ptr + rotary_dim + half, mask=half_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    b_all_k = tl.load(k_bias_ptr + dims, mask=dim_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    b_real_k = tl.load(k_bias_ptr + half, mask=half_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    b_imag_k = tl.load(k_bias_ptr + rotary_dim + half, mask=half_ok, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    num_k_tiles = (tokens + ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ - 1) // ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ
+    for t in range(pid, num_k_tiles, nprog):
+        token_start = t * ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ
+        token_idx = token_start + tl.arange(0, ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ)
+        token_ok = token_idx < tokens
+        _norm_rope_tile_npu(
+            x_k_ptr,
+            out_k_ptr,
+            cos_sin_cache_ptr,
+            positions_ptr,
+            token_idx,
+            token_start,
+            token_ok,
+            stride_x_k,
+            stride_out_k,
+            stride_cos,
+            w_all_k,
+            w_real_k,
+            w_imag_k,
+            b_all_k,
+            b_real_k,
+            b_imag_k,
+            eps,
+            0.0,
+            tokens,
+            num_heads=num_k_heads,
+            head_dim=head_dim,
+            rotary_dim=rotary_dim,
+            LAYERNORM=True,
+            BLOCK_D=BLOCK_D,
+            BLOCK_R=BLOCK_R,
+            ROWS_PER_PROGRAM=ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ,
+            H_CHUNK=H_CHUNK_K,
+            N_FULL=N_FULL_K,
+            REM_HEADS=REM_K,
+        )
+        z_bp = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            base=x_z_ptr,
+            shape=(tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim),
+            strides=(stride_x_z, 1),
+            offsets=(token_start, 0),
+            block_shape=(ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ, num_k_heads * head_dim),
+            order=(1, 0),
+        )
+        z_vals = tl.load(z_bp, boundary_check=(0,), padding_option="zero")
+        z_out_bp = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            base=out_z_ptr,
+            shape=(tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim),
+            strides=(num_k_heads * head_dim, 1),
+            offsets=(token_start, 0),
+            block_shape=(ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ, num_k_heads * head_dim),
+            order=(1, 0),
+        )
+        tl.store(z_out_bp, z_vals.to(out_z_ptr.dtype.element_ty), boundary_check=(0,))
+
+
+def fused_indexer_qkz_norm_rope(
+    index_q: torch.Tensor,
+    index_k: torch.Tensor,
+    index_z: torch.Tensor,
+    q_norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    k_norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    cos_sin_cache: torch.Tensor,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    k_norm_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    head_dim: int,
+    num_q_heads: int,
+    num_k_heads: int,
+    rotary_dim: int,
+    eps: float = 1e-6,
+    q_norm_weight_bias: float = 1.0,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Fused Step5 sparse-indexer Q/K norm + RoPE with Z passthrough.
+
+    ``index_q`` is ``[tokens, num_q_heads * head_dim]`` (RMSNorm, zero-
+    centered weights add ``q_norm_weight_bias``), ``index_k`` /
+    ``index_z`` are ``[tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim]`` (K: LayerNorm with
+    ``k_norm_bias``; Z: passthrough). Inputs may be strided views (the
+    ``split_indexer`` slices of the packed qkv+indexer GEMM output) -- the
+    kernel reads them in place through their row strides. RoPE angles come
+    from a single caller-provided ``[cos | sin]`` cache
+    (``cos_sin_cache``), rows indexed by ``positions``; ``rotary_dim`` is
+    the rotated dim count and is converted to NeoX pairs internally.
+    Returns ``(index_q e4m3, index_k bf16, index_z bf16)``: the fp8
+    quantization of index_q rides along with the norm+rope store (its only
+    consumer, the fused indexer scoring, wants fp8).
+    """
+    # ``rotary_dim`` follows the module convention: the number of rotated
+    # dims at the head of each indexer head (sparse_indexer_rope_dim, e.g.
+    # 32). The kernel works in NeoX pairs: real = dims[:rotary_pairs],
+    # imag = dims[rotary_pairs:2*rotary_pairs], and indexes the cos/sin cache
+    # rows (width = rotary_pairs) by pair id. Passing the dim count through
+    # unchanged made the kernel treat 32 dims as 32 pairs -- imag landed on
+    # dims 32-63 and cache reads ran past the 16-wide row into the next
+    # position's angles. Convert dims -> pairs here.
+    if rotary_dim % 2 != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"rotary_dim must be even, got {rotary_dim}")
+    if cos_sin_cache.shape[-1] != rotary_dim:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "cos_sin_cache must be laid out as [cos | sin] with last "
+            f"dimension {rotary_dim}, got shape {tuple(cos_sin_cache.shape)}"
+        )
+    rotary_pairs = rotary_dim // 2
+
+    tokens = index_q.shape[0]
+    if index_k.shape[0] != tokens or index_z.shape[0] != tokens:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"index_q/k/z must have the same number of tokens, got "
+            f"{index_q.shape[0]}, {index_k.shape[0]}, {index_z.shape[0]}"
+        )
+    if index_q.shape[1] != num_q_heads * head_dim:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"index_q shape {tuple(index_q.shape)} does not match num_q_heads={num_q_heads} * head_dim={head_dim}"
+        )
+    if index_k.shape[1] != num_k_heads * head_dim or index_z.shape[1] != num_k_heads * head_dim:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"index_k and index_z must have shape ({tokens}, {num_k_heads * head_dim}), "
+            f"got {tuple(index_k.shape)} and {tuple(index_z.shape)}"
+        )
+    out_q = index_q.new_empty((tokens, num_q_heads * head_dim), dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    out_k = index_k.new_empty((tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim))
+    out_z = index_z.new_empty((tokens, num_k_heads * head_dim))
+    if tokens == 0:
+        return out_q, out_k, out_z
+    # index_q comes out pre-quantized to e4m3: its only consumer (the fused
+    # indexer scoring) wants fp8, so the quantization rides along with the
+    # norm+rope store instead of a separate cast at the scoring entry.
+
+    grid = lambda meta: (
+        min(
+            max(
+                (tokens + meta["ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q"] - 1) // meta["ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_Q"],
+                (tokens + meta["ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ"] - 1) // meta["ROWS_PER_PROGRAM_KZ"],
+            ),
+            _npu_vec_core_num(),
+        ),
+    )
+    _indexer_qkz_norm_rope_kernel[grid](
+        index_q,
+        index_k,
+        index_z,
+        out_q,
+        out_k,
+        out_z,
+        q_norm_weight,
+        k_norm_weight,
+        k_norm_bias,
+        cos_sin_cache,
+        positions,
+        tokens,
+        index_q.stride(0),
+        index_k.stride(0),
+        index_z.stride(0),
+        out_q.stride(0),
+        out_k.stride(0),
+        cos_sin_cache.stride(0),
+        eps,
+        q_norm_weight_bias,
+        num_q_heads=num_q_heads,
+        num_k_heads=num_k_heads,
+        head_dim=head_dim,
+        rotary_dim=rotary_pairs,
+        BLOCK_D=triton.next_power_of_2(head_dim),
+        BLOCK_R=triton.next_power_of_2(rotary_pairs),
+        H_CHUNK_Q=(hc_q := _pick_head_chunk(num_q_heads, head_dim)),
+        H_CHUNK_K=(hc_k := _pick_head_chunk(num_k_heads, head_dim)),
+        N_FULL_Q=num_q_heads // hc_q,
+        REM_Q=num_q_heads % hc_q,
+        N_FULL_K=num_k_heads // hc_k,
+        REM_K=num_k_heads % hc_k,
+    )
+    return out_q, out_k, out_z

[Feature][KV Pool] Enable prefill KV offload for GLM-5.3-Flash (#21256)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable prefill KV offload for GLM-5.3-Flash PD producers. AscendStore
uses Memcache to save and restore KV while layers rotate through a
shared NPU backing. Reuse waits for Store saves and outstanding PD reads
before overwriting a slot.

The GLM-5.3-Flash rules select main MLA and aligned KDA state for reuse.
Compressed indexer, tail, and MTP caches stay resident. Within each
block-stride bucket, the planner orders cache entries by layer, builds
packs with distinct cache groups, and assigns packs in slot rotation
order. A same-layer, same-group collision advances the search to the
next slot. The planner adds a slot when all existing slots conflict and
builds tensor descriptors directly from the slots. Core probes a
one-block layout to account for the backing. Independent layer IDs are
model-global.

With HBM prefix caching enabled, the scheduler keeps the existing local
block-hash lookup and counts external hits beyond the adopted local hit.
When a local hit includes rotating layers, the worker restores their KV
through AscendStore into the adopted block IDs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

GLM-5.3-Flash producers with text model type `glm5_next_text` can opt in
through `AscendStoreConnector` with `backend: memcache`, `use_layerwise:
true`, and `layerwise_num_shared_buffers`. In a `MultiConnector`
configuration, the planner reads the first AscendStore child. Leave
`layerwise_num_shared_buffers` unset for the Mooncake storage backend.
The planner recognizes the request without checking the backend, while
offload transfer requires the GVA data plane. Ordinary layerwise
pooling, models without registered reuse rules, and plans with no actual
rotation keep their native cache layouts.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Dual-node A5 setup

P and D each used TP8/DP1, Model Runner V2, FP8 KV, and MTP5. The setup
used [vLLM
`24420b7a`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58),
#21262, and #21891. Fill the placeholders in the commands below. For B,
C, and D, point both local Memcache configs at the MetaService on P. For
GPQA, add `--reasoning-parser glm47` to each `vllm serve` command.

#### Dual-node AISBench performance

Each case completed 192 requests through the PD proxy at concurrency 32
with 131,072 input tokens and one output token per request. The repeated
prefix covered 90% of the input. A, B, and C used the same single-prefix
dataset. D used eight prefixes. Each prefix was warmed once before
measurement.

The run used this PR source tree with the Mooncake Push slot-reuse
integration from #21891 and the worker query and lease batching from
#21262.

| Case | P-side configuration | Prefixes | Input tokens/s |Requests/s |
Mean TTFT (s) | P-side HBM hit rate | P-side external hit rate |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A | HBM and Mooncake Push | 1 | 184,525.99 | 1.4078 | 21.50 | 89.65% |
0.00% |
| B | Layerwise pool and Mooncake Push | 1 | 177,979.20 |1.3579 | 22.34
| Off | 89.65% |
| C | Layerwise pool with offload and Mooncake Push | 1 | 179,642.58 |
1.3706 | 22.14 | Off | 89.65% |
| D | HBM, layerwise pool with offload, and Mooncake Push | 8 |
178,020.58 | 1.3582 | 22.31 | 89.65% | 0.00% |

Relative to A, C recorded 2.65% lower input throughput, 2.64% lower QPS,
and 2.99% higher mean TTFT. D recorded 3.53% lower input throughput,
3.52% lower QPS, and 3.74% higher mean TTFT. Both met the 5% target.

Hit rates use the P-side token counters during the measured requests.
The external rate counts additional hits among tokens queried after
local prefix lookup. In D, HBM covered the shared prefix and the worker
restored the rotating layers through AscendStore.

#### P-side KV block capacity

The P-side startup logs for the B and C above both report **23.92 GiB**
available for KV cache per rank. Both used TP8/DP1, FP8 KV, MTP5, and
the same `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`. Block counts are the
`num_gpu_blocks` values from the P-side `vllm:cache_config_info` metric.

| Case | Available KV-cache HBM per P rank | Configured
`layerwise_num_shared_buffers` | KV blocks |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| B — ordinary layerwise pooling | 23.92 GiB | Unset (offload disabled)
| 3,137 |
| C — layerwise pooling with offload | 23.92 GiB | 4 | 5,663 |

C had **2,526 more KV blocks (+80.52%)** than B. C used independent
layers `[0, 1, 2, 3]` and `layerwise_prefetch_layers: 2`.

#### GPQA Diamond

AISBench ran 198 questions per evaluated case through the PD proxy with
concurrency 16, temperature 1, top-p 0.95, seed 1024, and a maximum of
65536 output tokens. Each evaluated case finished 190 responses with
`stop` and 8 with `length`.

| Case | P-side configuration | Correct | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| A | HBM prefix caching and Mooncake Push | 177/198 | 89.39% |
| C | Layerwise pool with offload, HBM prefix caching disabled | 177/198
| 89.39% |
| D | HBM prefix caching and layerwise pool with offload | 177/198 |
89.39% |

The archived GPQA results cover A, C, and D. These runs predate the
worker merge-conflict resolution and the current planner update.

#### GPQA Diamond rerun

C and D ran the same 198 questions through the PD proxy on the published
source tree with the same runtime integrations used for the performance
run. The evaluation used concurrency 16 and the generation settings
listed above.

| Case | Correct | Accuracy | Stopped normally | Reached token limit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C | 178/198 | 89.90% | 189 | 9 |
| D | 177/198 | 89.39% | 190 | 8 |

D returned all 198 responses and AISBench completed scoring. The P
service exited during the decode tail, so the post-run GPQA metrics
snapshot is unavailable for D. The AISBench performance run recorded its
full metrics separately.

commits.message:
[BugFix] Restore pre-fusion QSA preparation with current main ABI (#22633)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Roll back #22086's QSA preparation fusions on current vLLM Ascend main,
using the parent of its first commit
`151915c775f9eed9a060c87ceb7291d0b0034157`
(`03f69b977b088680686af6198cc52ab2a5bae542`) as the preparation
baseline. This is the compatibility-reviewed replacement for #22630;
only one rollback PR should be merged.

Restore the pre-PR preparation behavior:

- Gather clamped rotary cache rows outside the Indexer RMSNorm/MRoPE
kernel. The RMSNorm/MRoPE fusion that already existed before #22086
remains.
- Produce pooled compressed keys and their first positions, then
normalize, rotate and store them separately. Preserve compression before
raw-ring cache updates.
- Prepare native LightningIndexerV2 request lengths, query bounds and
FP32 score weights with the previous PyTorch operations. Keep V2,
request page tables, scheduling metadata reuse and the original
effective score weight.
- Inherit main QKV/Gate projection from upstream instead of using
#22086's Ascend projection override.

The five affected production modules have the same executable AST as the
pre-PR baseline, excluding docstrings; comments now describe the
restored behavior. Later main changes, including unrelated
operator-index additions, are retained.

### Compatibility with current main

Based on vLLM Ascend main `a285b50d4be519f0d4a713f01eb1d563592fbc3c` and
checked against its pinned vLLM commit
`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`.

The current packed-input ABI is retained: Indexer `attn`, `qkv`,
`slot_mapping` and `gate_out` arguments remain accepted, and its result
remains `(selected_indices, None)`. The Ascend attention owner still
materializes Q/K/V and the gate for packed inputs, updates the main
cache and dispatches attention through the current main interface.
Existing release-version dispatch is preserved.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next returns to its pre-#22086 preparation behavior,
removing the preparation speedups introduced by that PR. No
configuration change is required. No accuracy improvement or specific
runtime defect is claimed by this rollback.

### How was this patch tested?

- LightningIndexerV2 CPU contract and Qwen4Exp source guards: 14 passed,
with repository conftest excluded.
- QSA ABI tests: 9 passed in a dependency-isolated CPU audit using the
actual restored Ascend methods and the pinned upstream method
definitions. This includes new coverage for main's packed Indexer
arguments and external 1-axis/3-axis rotary-cache gathering.
- Audited executable AST equivalence of all five preparation modules
against `151915c7^` and verified main Indexer argument names, defaults
and keyword-only structure against the pinned upstream source.
- Ruff 0.14.0 lint/format, Markdownlint for the changed operator
documents/index, Python AST and whitespace checks passed.
- Full repository lint could not run locally because pre-commit is
unavailable. The isolated tests do not replace full vLLM/plugin imports
or hardware tests; NPU E2E, model accuracy and performance remain for
CI.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

---------

Signed-off-by: Zoezxb <35328307+Zoezxb@users.noreply.github.com>

-# prepare_qsa_lightning_v2_inputs
-
-## Description
-
-- **Function:** Prepare native LightningIndexerV2 inputs for Qwen QSA in one
-  Triton launch. The production caller is
-  `models/qwen4_exp/lightning_indexer.py::qsa_select_paged_tokens_lightning_v2`.
-- **Formula:** For request length `L`, compression ratio `r` and query row count
-  `T`, produce `L // r`, `L % r` and `min(query_start_loc, T)`. Fill weights with
-  `float32(bfloat16(1 / sqrt(128)))`, preserving the existing effective value.
-- **Algorithm flow:** Each vector tile independently writes request lengths,
-  query boundaries and query-head weights with separate bounds masks.
-- **Devices:** Requires NPU and Triton Ascend. CPU contract checks do not
-  establish device support.
-
-## Parameters
-
-| Parameter | Input/Output/Attribute | Description | Data type | Data format |
-| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| `query` | Input | Only shape and device are used | Model BF16; contents are not read | `[T, H, 128]` |
-| `sequence_lengths` | Input | Nonnegative original-token lengths | INT32 or INT64 | `[B]`, strided allowed |
-| `query_start_loc` | Input | Packed query boundaries | INT32 or INT64 | At least `[B + 1]`, strided allowed |
-| `compress_ratio` | Attribute | Positive tokens per group; QSA uses 4 | Integer | Scalar |
-| `weights` | Output | Uniform score weights | FP32 | `[T, H]`, contiguous |
-| `cu_query` | Output | Boundaries clamped to T | Boundary input dtype | `[B + 1]`, contiguous |
-| `compressed` | Output | Complete compressed-group counts | Length input dtype | `[B]`, contiguous |
-| `residual` | Output | Remaining original-token counts | Length input dtype | `[B]`, contiguous |
-
-Outputs are returned in table order: weights, cu_query, compressed, residual.
-
-## Constraints
-
-- Inputs share a device; metadata vectors may be strided. `H` must be positive.
-  Zero query rows and zero requests are supported by the wrapper. The model
-  caller bypasses preparation entirely for zero query rows.
-- Outputs are fresh contiguous allocations. Inputs are not mutated. There is
-  no head padding, query copy or per-token block-table gather.
-- Valid model metadata describes contiguous query suffixes per request. Padded
-  boundaries are clamped, without discarding the original request capacity.
-- The wrapper reads no device values on the host. Graph replay must observe
-  updated lengths and boundaries at the captured addresses.
-- CANN schedule generation and reuse remain unchanged. The input adapter still
-  prepares the reusable schedule outside the layer loop. A trimmed query causes
-  the selector to regenerate it from the same fused outputs passed to Indexer.
-- Output index-buffer initialization and group packing remain separate.
-
-## Origin and Differences
-
-- **Origin:** Replaces four PyTorch operations in the native V2 selector:
-  `floor_divide`, `remainder`, `clamp_max` and `full`.
-- **Differences:** V2 keeps original heads and request-level page tables.
-  This operator replaces input
-  preparation only; CANN still performs scoring and TopK.
-- **JIT:** Compression ratio, score weight and vector tile size are compile-time
-  parameters. Counts and strides are runtime integers, subject to the backend's
-  ordinary scalar specialization classes. Metadata contents do not specialize.
-  Pointer dtypes/alignment and compiler options can create variants. The fixed
-  256-element tile is a starting configuration, not a measured optimum. No
-  explicit warmup registration is added; actual compilation counts are pending.

-
-## Description
-
-- **Implementation**: `qsa_compress_groups_with_ratio` wraps
-  `_compress_qsa_groups_kernel` in `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/qwen4_exp/qsa.py`.
-- **Caller**: Qwen QSA Indexer `_update_and_compress`.
-- **Algorithm**: each row pools a completed group from current keys and the
-  historical ring: `pooled = sum(keys) / compress_ratio`.
-  Ordinary mode returns pooled keys and the first token's positions. Supplying
-  `compressed_cache` additionally computes
-  `normalized = pooled * rsqrt(mean(pooled**2) + eps) * (1 + weight)`, applies
-  partial MRoPE, and writes the result directly to compressed slots.
-  BF16 intermediate rounding matches the decomposed path.
-- **Devices**: requires NPU and Triton. The fused path has prior A3 test evidence;
-  the latest revision requires fresh device validation.
-
-## Parameters
-
-| Parameter | Role | Shape / meaning |
-| --- | --- | --- |
-| `raw_keys` | Input | `[rows, 1, head_dim]` current keys |
-| `raw_positions` | Input | int64 `[rows, 1, 3]` positions |
-| `compressor_state_cache` | Input | `[blocks, ring_size, 1, head_dim]` historical keys |
-| `compressor_state_block_table` | Input | 2D per-request ring block IDs |

-| `compressed_cache` | Optional input/output | BF16 `[pages, page_size, 1, 128]`, written in place |
-| `norm_eps` | Attribute | RMS epsilon, default `1e-6` |

-
-## Constraints
-

[Misc][KV Transfer] Log Mooncake heartbeat timing at initialization (#22643)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

MooncakeConnectorV2 heartbeat logs do not expose the configured lease
timing, and timestamps alone cannot identify the heartbeat interval when
requests arrive intermittently.

Add one DEBUG `MooncakeHeartbeat event=config` per pull scheduler after
lease configuration validation. It includes the engine ID, KV role,
`initial_lease_s`, `renewal_window_s`, and `heartbeat_interval_s` (120,
80, and 20 seconds by default). The renewal window is measured from the
heartbeat processing time, not added to the old deadline.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

One initialization DEBUG record only. No configuration or runtime
behavior changes. No release-note fragment is included because
`release_notes/README.md` exempts internal logging changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- Passed Ruff lint, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` for the
final change, which adds only one logger call in `pull_scheduler.py`.
- Unit and NPU tests were not executed locally; runtime validation is CI
testing only. Updated the existing scheduler initialization test to
supply engine ID and KV role in its base-class mock, and assert exactly
one initialization DEBUG record with default (120/80/20 seconds) and
custom (60/40/10 seconds) values.
- The full `bash format.sh ci` check was attempted during preparation
but could not complete successfully on Windows: clang-format failed to
execute, shellcheck was unavailable, and shell/Python hooks encountered
`/bin/bash` not found or WinError 193. Linux CI is required for the
complete check.

[CI][Revert] Revert AISBench tag bump (#22644)

---

## 1. 背景

2026-11-16，PR #21848 将 nightly Dockerfile 中的 AISBench tag 从：

```text
v3.1-20261013-master
```

升级到：

```text
v3.1-20261113-master
```

2026-11-19 01:27 UTC（北京时间 09:27），PR #22189 合入，在 accuracy 用例中无条件启用
`--response-anomaly`，并对所有 anomaly 指标执行 hard fail。

随后 11-19 14:30 UTC 起，A2、A3、A3-560T、A5、310P 的 nightly 同时出现大面积 accuracy
失败：

- QWEN3_235B：`rare_character 835`，anomaly rate 63.53%；
- 310P Qwen3-8B：15 个 rare_character + 2 个 repetition，1.3% 异常率即失败；
- Kimi-K2.6 / Kimi-K3：`TikTokenTokenizer has no attribute
backend_tokenizer`；
- GLM-5.2 DSpark/MTP：3 条异常即失败。

根因不是模型精度回归，而是：

1. `--response-anomaly` 被无条件启用；
2. `tools/aisbench.py` 把任意非零 anomaly 指标（包括 `count`、`rate`）都当作失败；
3. msProbe 的 response anomaly 配置生成不兼容 TikToken；
4. `rare_character` 规则对中文/数学输出误报严重；
5. 没有开关、灰度、阈值。

[BugFix] Fix KDA RecoverSSM small-norm accuracy (#22523)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes #22413.

After the A3 fla_npu update in #22141, AscendC RecurrentKDA added `1e-6`
to the squared Q/K norm. RecoverSSM still normalized small nonzero
vectors to unit length, which caused four A3 Nightly verify-output
failures. The same mismatch could also change accepted-state
reconstruction.

Use `rsqrt(sum(x * x) + 1e-6)` in Triton verify, regular commit, and A5
grouped commit. Apply the same formula in the independent FP64
reference, document the formula, and restore the four regression cases
skipped by #22407. The constant is embedded in the FP32 arithmetic for
the existing kernels.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

RecoverSSM now matches native AscendC RecurrentKDA for near-zero Q/K
during KDA speculative decoding.

### How was this patch tested?

1. A3 r120, CANN 9.3.0 and
`flash-linear-attention-npu-a3==26.10.0+feature`. Reproduced the Nightly
failure at `405617bae` using image digest
`sha256:be1ff781b1d316c4f317c0b3925d2d1b6fc23c8993c30571ee5b5f5acd9e78c8`.
The unmodified image failed 4 of the 6 amplitudes. With the candidate
sources, all 6 amplitudes passed, including verify and accepted states
at prefix lengths 1, 3, and 6. All 6 ragged-tile cases also passed
against the FP64 reference.
2. A5 r120, CANN 9.3.0 and
`flash-linear-attention-npu-a5==26.10.0+feature` (image digest
`sha256:6b68469fdcb3fb3fa0d4fed564d75640d1e957c6c759c3e20b906951c804d79e`).
All 4 grouped-commit cases passed against the FP64 reference. The cases
assert grouped dispatch and cover 32/64 heads with a six-token window in
eager and graph modes.
3. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.

Run the A3 regression and FP64 reference cases with

```bash
pytest -v tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_kda_recoverssm_npu.py \
  -k 'test_recoverssm_matches_ascendc_small_norms or test_recoverssm_ragged_tiles'
```

Run the A5 grouped-commit cases with

```bash
pytest -v tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_kda_recoverssm_npu.py \
  -k 'test_commit_window_uses_device_path and (6-32 or 6-64)'
```

| Accuracy comparison | Minimum element pass ratio | Maximum absolute
error |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Small-norm BF16 verify against AscendC | 100% | `3.052e-5` |
| Small-norm FP32 commit against AscendC | 100% | `5.960e-8` |
| Ragged BF16 verify against the FP64 reference | 100% | `7.344e-4` |
| Ragged FP32 commit against the FP64 reference | 100% | `8.979e-8` |
| A5 grouped-path BF16 verify against the FP64 reference | 100% |
`1.216e-4` |
| A5 grouped FP32 commit against the FP64 reference | 100% | `1.577e-7`
|

BF16 uses `rtol=atol=2^-6` with a maximum absolute error limit of `1`.
FP32 uses `rtol=2^-10`, `atol=2^-16`, and a maximum absolute error limit
of `0.01`. This validation covers operator correctness. Model-level
accuracy, performance, and recompilation measurements have not been run.

[Performance][KV Transfer] Reuse upstream hash truncation for Mooncake V2 (#22167)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

In Mooncake V2 P/D disaggregation, the producer removes the final prompt
token after block hashes have already been computed. The original
implementation clears all existing block hashes and rebuilds them for
the entire prompt before prefix-cache lookup, causing redundant hashing
of unchanged cached prefixes and increasing P-side scheduling overhead,
especially for long-context requests. This PR leverages the upstream
`Request.truncate_block_hashes()` API to preserve valid prefix hashes
and recompute only the affected suffix, avoiding unnecessary full-prompt
rehashing. In the previous NPU A/B benchmark (128K input / 1K output,
concurrency 32), this optimization improved output throughput by
**11.31%**, reduced mean P-side queue time by **18.1%**, and reduced
mean TTFT by **18.4%**. These performance results are from the original
implementation in #21857; no new NPU benchmark was performed for this
revision.

Related to #21437: its description explicitly proposes migrating
truncation sites to the upstream primitive to avoid full-prompt
rehashing. This PR implements that performance follow-up for the
**Mooncake V2 base scheduler**. #21437's hybrid/layerwise changes remain
a separate scope. The correctness rebuild was introduced by #20213; the
upstream primitive comes from [vLLM
#64096](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64096). This PR reuses
the upstream primitive and retains the original proposal's hardware
evidence below.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. With native hash-truncation support, long-context Mooncake V2
producer requests avoid hashing their unchanged cached prefix again
after the final prompt token is removed. Older cores keep the original
full-rebuild behavior. No new settings are required. A performance
release note is included in `release_notes/fragments/22167.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

CPU tests used independent checkouts of the Ascend and verified vLLM
commits above in the `pp-dspark` container. They execute real upstream
`Request` objects and the real truncation method, comparing the results
with an independent full rebuild.

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 VLLM_PLUGINS= VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty \
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -m pytest -q \
  --confcutdir=tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2 \
  tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_base_scheduler.py \
  tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_pull_scheduler.py \
  tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_prefill_hash_truncation.py
```

- **351 passed**, including block boundaries, hash sizes 1/2/16/32,
lookahead 0/1/5, embeddings, missing suffixes, unresolved geometry,
idempotency, and unchanged consumer/short requests.
- Eighteen added cases cover an absent, `None`, or noncallable
truncation method with token IDs/embeddings and lookahead 0/1/5; they
compare against full rebuilding and verify repeated-hook idempotency.
All 18 fail against the preceding unguarded implementation and pass with
the guard.
- Six 128K regression cases assert zero new hash-function calls for
preserved hashes. Restoring the unmodified main scheduler makes all six
fail; the patched scheduler passes them.
- Ruff 0.14.0 `check` and `format --check`, plus `git diff --check`,
pass for the changed Python files.
- Changed-file pre-commit Ruff, codespell, typos, package-init,
forbidden-import, boolean-context, and filename checks pass. The logger,
long-function, and symbolic-meta checks were run directly with the
available interpreters because the Windows hook entry points cannot find
`/bin/bash` or `python3`.
- Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but could not install Go for
actionlint: the network closed the download connection
(`RemoteDisconnected`). The Windows gitleaks hook could not find
`/bin/bash`; full CI lint/secret scanning remains required. The diff
contains no credentials.
- The standard invocation without `--confcutdir` fails before collection
in the unrelated global Kimi patch:
`kimi_k25_vit.get_rope_shape_decorate` is absent at the verified core
pin. The focused invocation avoids that global model-patch bootstrap; it
does not replace the scheduler or request implementation.
- No new NPU E2E or throughput measurement was performed for this
revision. The original hardware data, complete configuration, and
original related-PR references are preserved below with their original
software baseline.

#### Historical NPU E2E comparison preserved from #21857

Hardware: one node with **8 Ascend950PR NPUs**. Model:
**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (`0731` weight snapshot), MooncakeConnectorV2,
Model Runner V2, DSpark with 5 speculative tokens, FP8 KV/indexer cache.

Hardware A/B environment: vLLM
`4ba787ec9959e566d3b587a796dff07673324da5` (`0.33.0+empty`), vLLM-Ascend
`06a25402991cae7fb198f99d66c22b390647a219`, torch `2.10.0+cpu`,
torch-npu `2.10.0.post7`, transformers `5.19.0`. Existing
transport/profiler environment changes were held fixed; only this
scheduler change differed between variants. These measurements were
produced by the earlier tail-truncation/backport implementation in
#21857 at the software baseline above. They are preserved as historical
evidence, not as a new benchmark of this revision.

| Setting | P | D |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NPUs | 0-3 | 4-7 |
| DP / TP / PCP | 1 / 1 / 4 | 4 / 1 / 1 |
| Max batched tokens | 8192 | 768 |
| Max sequences | 128 | 128 |
| Memory utilization | 0.94 | 0.92 |
| Execution | eager + async scheduling | FULL_DECODE_ONLY + async
scheduling |
| Prefix caching | enabled | enabled |

Both roles used `max-model-len=262144`, CLI `block-size=32`, enabled
hybrid KV cache management, and CPU binding. P/D were restarted with the
same arguments and environment to load the source change; the proxy
process was unchanged. All formal requests went through proxy -> P -> KV
handoff -> D.

Benchmark invocation (external AISBench prefix harness):

```bash
python3 aisbench_test.py \
  --input_len 131072 --output_len 1024 --data_num 128 \
  --request_rate 0 --concurrency 32 --seed 1024 \
  --dataset_type prefix_cache --repeat_rate 0.90 --prefix_test
```

The input dataset and common prefix were generated once and frozen
across all four runs. Each run reset P/D prefix caches and performed
verified stable warmup, excluded from formal throughput and metrics.
Hashes of the actual 128 formal API inputs were checked individually
across all runs. Chat templating resulted in 131155-131156 actual input
tokens per request; every response generated exactly 1024 output tokens.

**`repeat_rate=0.90` is the generator setting; measured P-side local
prefix hit rate was 87.445267% in every run. These results do not claim
an exact 90% measured cache hit rate.**

| Variant | Run | Output token/s | Request/s | P mean queue time (s) |
Success / failure |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original | 1 | 1020.1770 | 0.9963 | 10.7354 | 128 / 0 |
| Original | 2 | 1021.2707 | 0.9973 | 10.7255 | 128 / 0 |
| Patched | 1 | 1132.5363 | 1.1060 | 9.0245 | 128 / 0 |
| Patched | 2 | 1139.7220 | 1.1130 | 8.5545 | 128 / 0 |

Pooled throughput is total generated tokens divided by total formal
benchmark duration, rather than an average of displayed request rates:

| Metric | Original | Patched |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Output token/s | 1020.7235 | 1136.1178 (**+11.31%**) |
| Request/s | 0.996800 | 1.109490 |
| P mean queue time (s) | 10.7304 | 8.7895 |
| Client mean TTFT (s) | 15.0254 | 12.2593 |
| Client mean E2E latency (s) | 29.4803 | 26.1859 |

All 512 formal requests succeeded. Seven additional temperature=0, C1
smoke requests (short inputs, adjacent lengths, long cold/warm prefix
reuse, and a long-input extension) produced exactly matching messages
before/after. This is targeted validation; a full model accuracy
evaluation was not run. Hardware evidence covers the V2 path above,
without a claim about all other Mooncake connectors or hardware
configurations. Upstream CI is still required before merge.

For the supported EngineCore initialization paths,
EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches() resolves and populates
KVCacheConfig.hash_block_size before constructing the scheduler and
Mooncake connector. The native truncation path relies on this
initialization contract, and the assertion checks that invariant. Full
hash rebuilding is used only when Request.truncate_block_hashes is
missing or non-callable; an unresolved hash block size is not a fallback
condition. On older cores without that API, it retains full hash
rebuilding for correctness; the historical speedup above is not claimed
for that fallback. Current-version NPU validation remains for
CI/reviewers.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage.
- [x] Deterministic regression coverage against unmodified main.
- [x] Real Request correctness oracle and upstream-method delegation
checks.
- [ ] Current-version NPU E2E/performance validation (CI/reviewers).

[Doc] Clarify release note rule for changes that cancel out before a release (#22660)

## What this PR does / why we need it?

Clarifies that the unit of a release note is the **net change relative
to the previous release**, not the individual PR, and spells out two
recurring cases that current guidance does not cover:

1. **Bugfix cancelling an unreleased bug.** A fix for a bug that already
shipped in a released version needs a `bugfix` fragment. A fix for a bug
that never reached a released artifact (bug and fix both land between
two releases) needs no fragment of its own — instead the fix PR must
remove or amend the buggy PR's not-yet-archived fragment, otherwise the
release would announce a bug no released artifact ever contained.
2. **Reverting an unreleased PR.** A revert of a PR merged after the
last release has zero net change: no fragment, and the reverted PR's
not-yet-archived fragment is removed in the revert PR. Reverting
something that *did* ship is a user-visible behavior change and must
have a fragment (`breaking`, or `bugfix` if it reverts a regression).

Changes:
- `release_notes/README.md`: new section "Changes that cancel out before
a release"; explicit exception to the "fragments are archived, never
deleted" rule.
- `AGENTS.md`: one-paragraph summary in the Release Notes section,
linking to the README section.

## Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. Contributor-facing documentation only; no release note fragment
needed (this PR itself is the documentation change).

## How was this patch tested?

- Documentation-only change; no code affected.
- `markdownlint` passes on both modified files.

+
+The unit of a release note is the **net change relative to the previous release**, not the
+individual PR. Two cases follow from this:
+
+**A bugfix immediately following the bug it fixes:**

+- **The buggy PR was already included in a released version.** The fix must have a

+  the buggy PR's **not-yet-archived fragment must be removed or amended in the fix PR**.

commits.message:
[Core][Misc] Move Ascend KV cache planning out of the kv_cache_utils patch (#21345)

## Summary
vLLM's pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder` (#53558) is available on both
supported lanes now that the release lane tracks v0.33.0, so the monkey
patch no longer needs to carry Ascend's KV-cache planning decisions.

- `AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder` now owns grouping, pool accounting, and
materialization: it overrides `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` to
convert `num_blocks` through `_get_pool_bytes_per_block` and then
delegates to Ascend's planner.
- `patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py` is deleted entirely (640 -> 0
lines). Each of its two remaining patches had a concrete reason to go:
- **`_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups` duplicated the upstream
generic admission formula.** The generic planner derives admission from
two extension points: the builder `_get_pool_bytes_per_block` hook
(which already implements the kimi_k31 / turboquant / glm5next /
qwen4exp / DSV4 divisors) and spec-level `max_memory_usage_bytes` /
`max_memory_usage_pages`. The patch re-implemented the same product per
model in five dispatch branches; for `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups
the per-group block terms are algebraically identical
(`cdiv(spec.max_memory_usage_bytes, page_size)` ==
`max_memory_usage_pages`). The dispatch, its registration, and the four
model accounting functions whose only caller was the dispatch
(`paired_sfa_max_memory`, `get_glm5_next_max_memory_usage`,
`get_qwen4_exp_max_memory_usage`, `tq_cache.max_memory_usage`) are
removed as dead code. The affected UTs now assert admission through the
generic planner against the inline physical formulas, and the cpu-ut
dual-version gate verifies the equivalence on both lanes.
- **The Qwen4Exp MTP `_annotate_eagle_groups` patch was a no-op on both
lanes.** Upstream vLLM #61455 (merged 10-17) replaced that module-level
function with explicit `spec.is_draft` draft-layer tags; both CI pins
(main `ba15685ab7` from 11-05, v0.33.0 from 10-26) are newer, so the
`getattr` guard resolved to `None` and the registration never fired. Its
four UTs called the dead helper directly and only proved the function
itself, not that it was installed; they are removed with it.
- Carries over the replicated dense draft allocation that #15851 added
to the patched planner. The GQA draft of Kimi-K3 DSpark is replicated
rather than DCP-sharded, so its contiguous K/V pages must not alias the
target/Mamba pool; `_get_replicated_draft_pools` splits it into its own
pool and `get_ascend_kv_cache_config_from_groups` stacks the per-pool
descriptors over a disjoint byte range. The code is moved verbatim; no
behavior change.
- Keeps the removals from #21734 instead of restoring the obsolete
`UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs.max_num_blocks_per_req` shim and the
`KVCacheConfig.has_mamba_layers` override while resolving the rebase.
- Carries over the Qwen4-Exp MTP grouping dispatch from the patched
`get_kv_cache_groups`. The builder path never calls that function, so
without it the QSA composite-group merge would be skipped for Qwen4-Exp
MTP. Other models are unaffected (`_prepare_qsa_composite_groups`
returns `None`).
- UT updated to reference the builder instead of the removed patch
symbols.
- Carries over the Step-5 KV cache integration (#20946) that upstream
added to the deleted patch while resolving the rebase: the grouping,
pool-bytes, and materialization dispatch for Step-5 groups now live in
`AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder`. `get_step5_max_memory_usage` is not
carried over — its formula (sum of per-group page claims times the
envelope divisor) is identical to the generic admission derivation via
`_get_pool_bytes_per_block` + spec-level `max_memory_usage_bytes`.
- Adapts the upstream Step-5 UT to the new architecture: the dispatch
test asserts through the generic planner with
`AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder`, and the DSV4.1 UT assertions adopt the
unified-allocation layout from #21083.
- Attaches the transfer/speculation metadata to the upstream default
materializer result as well (review feedback): a generic layout matching
no Ascend divisor previously returned without the PD role, so the hybrid
coordinator treated the instance as standalone. Covered by a generic
hybrid PD consumer UT through the public builder.

## Motivation
Keeping Ascend rules in a monkey patch forces us to track upstream
private signatures on every bump. The builder is the supported extension
point, so planning rules belong there. A platform patch is only
justified when it is (a) required by one of the two CI lanes' pinned
vLLM versions, or (b) expresses logic that has no builder/platform hook
upstream — both removed patches satisfied neither.

## Test plan
- CI

AI assistance was used for this change; all lines were reviewed by the
submitter.

-def _get_deepseek_v4_cache_layout(
-    kv_cache_groups: list[KVCacheGroupSpec],
-) -> tuple[list[int], list[dict[int, list[str]]], list[str], int, int]:

-    Precondition: kv_cache_groups[0] is the full-MLA group; its page sizes
-    define the canonical bucket set. Non-full-MLA groups must have been
-    page_size-padded upstream (see _get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_groups) so
-    every layer's page_size matches one of the full-MLA bucket sizes.
-
-    For each group, bucket its layers by page_size_bytes and place each layer
-    at tuple_idx = position-within-bucket.
-    """
-    full_mla_spec = kv_cache_groups[0].kv_cache_spec
-    assert isinstance(full_mla_spec, UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs)
-    page_sizes = sorted(_page_sizes(full_mla_spec))
-
-    # Pre-bucket each group's layers by page_size (registration order within
-    # bucket). bucketed[g_idx][page_size] = [layer_name, ...].
-    mtp_layer_names = []
-    mtp_page_size = 0
-    bucketed: list[dict[int, list[str]]] = []
-    for group in kv_cache_groups:
-        assert isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs)
-        specs = group.kv_cache_spec.kv_cache_specs

-        for name in group.layer_names:
-            padded = getattr(specs[name], "page_size_padded", None)
-            page_size = padded if padded is not None else specs[name].page_size_bytes
-            if "mtp" not in name:
-                b[page_size].append(name)
-            else:
-                mtp_layer_names.append(name)
-                mtp_page_size = page_size
-        bucketed.append(b)

-    # full-MLA group this equals the count of layers in the largest
-    # per-page-size bucket (= get_num_layer_tuples()); for SWA sub-groups
-    # this equals the sub-group size (each has a single page_size).
-    num_layer_tuples = max(len(layers) for b in bucketed for layers in b.values()) + len(mtp_layer_names)

-    return page_sizes, bucketed, mtp_layer_names, mtp_page_size, num_layer_tuples

-def _get_kv_cache_config_deepseek_v4_main(
-    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
-    kv_cache_groups: list[KVCacheGroupSpec],
-    available_memory: int,
-) -> tuple[int, list[KVCacheTensor]]:
-    if tq_cache.uses_turboquant_groups(kv_cache_groups):
-        return tq_cache.cache_config(vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, available_memory)
-    (
-        page_sizes,
-        bucketed,
-        mtp_layer_names,
-        mtp_page_size,
-        num_tuple_slots,
-    ) = _get_deepseek_v4_cache_layout(kv_cache_groups)
-
-    bytes_per_tuple = sum(page_sizes)
-    num_blocks = available_memory // (bytes_per_tuple * num_tuple_slots)
-    num_blocks = may_override_num_blocks(vllm_config, num_blocks)
-
-    tuple_stride = bytes_per_tuple * num_blocks
-    backing_size = tuple_stride * num_tuple_slots
-
-    # Within every tuple slot, page-size buckets are placed consecutively.
-    page_offsets: dict[int, int] = {}
-    page_prefix = 0
-    for page_size in page_sizes:
-        page_offsets[page_size] = page_prefix * num_blocks
-        page_prefix += page_size
-
-    tensors: list[KVCacheTensor] = []
-
-    # Keep each descriptor inside one cache group. Descriptors from different
-    # groups alias corresponding tuple slots by using identical geometry.
-    for group_buckets in bucketed:
-        for page_size in page_sizes:
-            layer_names = group_buckets.get(page_size)
-            if not layer_names:
-                continue
-
-            tensors.append(
-                KVCacheTensor(
-                    size=backing_size,
-                    layers=list(layer_names),
-                    offset=page_offsets[page_size],
-                    layer_stride=tuple_stride,
-                    block_stride=page_size,
-                )
-            )
-
-    # MTP layers receive trailing tuple slots. Unused page buckets remain
-    # padding so num_blocks and memory accounting retain the existing contract.
-    normal_tuple_slots = num_tuple_slots - len(mtp_layer_names)
-    for index, layer_name in enumerate(mtp_layer_names):
-        slot = normal_tuple_slots + index
-        tensors.append(
-            KVCacheTensor(
-                size=backing_size,
-                layers=[layer_name],
-                offset=slot * tuple_stride + page_offsets[mtp_page_size],
-                layer_stride=0,
-                block_stride=mtp_page_size,
-            )
-        )
-
-    return num_blocks, tensors

[CI] Explicitly disable static kernel for PIECEWISE SIT cases (#22631)

## Motivation

After #21921, `enable_static_kernel` is honored under the PIECEWISE and
FULL_AND_PIECEWISE cudagraph modes instead of being silently overridden
by `platform.py`. Static kernel compilation then runs per piece and per
cudagraph capture size at service startup.

The nightly cases touched here regress from tens of seconds of graph
capture to ~150-215 s **per capture-size step**, and are killed before
the accuracy stage:

| case | before (14:30 nightly, pre-#21921) | after (20:00 nightly,
post-#21921) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-A2 | 19 steps, ~43 s total | 150.85 s/step -> ~48 min,
hits `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` (1800 s) |
| qwen3-32b-int8 | 35 steps, ~26 s total | 214.76 s/step -> ~125 min,
hits the 2800 s `/health` timeout |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8_piecewise_fullgraph_A3 | 16 steps, ~52 s + ~41 s
| 98 s/step -> 26 min, then stuck on `FULL 0/16` |
| qwen3-32b-int8-prefix-cache | 35 steps, ~18 s total | 155.87 s/step ->
~91 min, hits the 2800 s `/health` timeout |

Evidence: both nightly rounds pin the same vLLM commit (`4ba787ec99`);
the only difference is vllm-ascend `6f60cb8fce` (pre-#21921) vs
`a38556f695` (post-#21921). The startup log shows `AscendCompiler hash
factors: {..., 'enable_npugraph_ex': False, 'enable_static_kernel':
False, 'enable_super_kernel': False}` before and all `True` after.
`running aisbench cmd` appears 0 times in all four failing jobs.

## What this PR does

Make the intended compile state explicit instead of relying on the old
silent force-off:

- `tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-A2.yaml` (2
server configs): `enable_static_kernel: false` **and**
`enable_npugraph_ex: false`
- `tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3-32B-Int8.yaml`:
`enable_static_kernel: false`
-
`tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Prefix-Cache-Qwen3-32B-Int8.yaml`:
`enable_static_kernel: false`
-
`tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-W8A8_piecewise_fullgraph_A3.yaml`
(2 test cases): `enable_static_kernel: false`
- `tests/SIT/cases/models/configs/Qwen/Qwen3-32B-Int8-A2.yaml`:
`enable_static_kernel: false` (same flag, same PIECEWISE startup path)

The other keys on those `additional-config` lines (`enable_flashcomm1`,
`weight_nz_mode`, `pa_shape_list`) are untouched.

`enable_super_kernel` is deliberately not written: `ascend_config.py`
makes it inherit `enable_static_kernel`, so it also becomes `False`.
Writing only `enable_static_kernel: true` was in practice enabling super
kernel as well.

### Why Qwen3-235B-A22B-A2 also turns `enable_npugraph_ex` off

#21921 removed a force-off that covered **all three** flags under
PIECEWISE, not just static/super:

```python
-        additional_config["ascend_compilation_config"]["enable_npugraph_ex"] = False
-        additional_config["ascend_compilation_config"]["enable_static_kernel"] = False
-        additional_config["ascend_compilation_config"]["enable_super_kernel"] = False
```

So this case's recorded perf baseline (`1152.0278`, `threshold: 0.97`)
was measured with npugraph_ex inactive. It is also the slowest of the
five to start even with everything off (~17 min of weight loading + FX
compile across 2 nodes, 2xDP x TP8, `--max-num-seqs 128` -> the largest
capture-bucket set), which leaves it the tightest margin against the
1800 s engine-ready timeout. Setting `enable_npugraph_ex: false` here
reproduces the pre-#21921 effective configuration exactly, so both
startup cost and measured performance stay on the baseline this case is
guarded against. The other four cases keep `enable_npugraph_ex: true`
(its default) to keep the FX optimization layer.

## Notes

- For the four cases that keep npugraph_ex on, this restores their
pre-#21921 startup behaviour while keeping the npugraph_ex FX
optimization layer active. It is a temporary mitigation to unblock
nightly; static kernel coverage for these models should be re-enabled
once compile artifacts can be cached/reused across runs (the static
kernel output directory is per-process today) or once the startup
timeout is raised together with a pre-warmed cache.
- Other case configs still enabling static kernel are out of scope of
this PR.
- No accuracy/perf gate semantics change: only the startup flags change;
the anomaly/accuracy gates are unaffected.
