[BugFix] Fix DeepSeek V4.1 Engram post-load compatibility on Ascend (#22521)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Recent vLLM versions invoke `process_weights_after_loading()` on child
modules at the end of a load or reload. DeepSeek V4.1's Ascend Engram
embedding inherits a GPU peer-table finalizer that reads `peer_rows`,
which the Ascend constructor never creates. Startup fails with an
`AttributeError` after checkpoint loading.

Override the hook in `AscendParallelEngramEmbedding`. Ascend prepares
its own Engram storage during checkpoint loading, so there is no GPU
peer table to finalize. The regression test runs the vLLM finalizer on a
model containing an Ascend Engram embedding and verifies that the loaded
weight is preserved.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It fixes DeepSeek V4.1 startup with the verified vLLM main revision
when the Engram post-load hook runs.

### How was this patch tested?

- With the verified vLLM revision `c410543d9f`, reproduced the missing
`peer_rows` error through `finalize_model_weights()` in an Ascend
runtime container.
- Reran the same CPU-tensor probe after the patch in two Ascend runtime
containers. Both calls completed and preserved the weight parameter.
- The focused pytest regression passed in the Ascend runtime with CPU
tensors.
- Scoped Ruff, codespell, typos, and repository Python checks passed.
The local Windows runner could not complete the actionlint and gitleaks
hooks.
- Full-model startup and inference on NPU remain for CI or a separate
hardware run.

### Checklist

- [x] **Regression test**
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

[Feature] Opt-in layer-level BF16 MM ReduceScatter for SP (#21498)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Under sequence parallelism (SP), every attention O-projection on MiniMax
M3 is a TP-sharded GEMM immediately followed by a ReduceScatter. This PR
installs a layer-level `SequenceParallelMMReduceScatterOp` on those
projections so the GEMM and the ReduceScatter can execute as one fused
BF16 MM+ReduceScatter via `torch_npu.npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base`,
eliminating the standalone ReduceScatter kernel and its extra memory
traffic.

Why we need it: on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-bf16 (TP4+DP4+EP, decode-oriented
serving), the fusion delivers **1.16x–1.30x end-to-end throughput** and
**13–19% lower mean TTFT** across ISL 64–2048, with no regression
observed in the tested range (full data below).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. There is no API, configuration, or behavior change: the fusion is
opportunistic and only engages when SP is active and every gate passes;
otherwise the layer follows the stock path bit-for-bit. No release note
fragment is added.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests** (all passing, ruff clean; compatible with CPU-only CI
environments):

- `tests/ut/ops/test_mmrs.py` (new, 52 cases): every fusion gate (token
range [256, 16384), K range [256, 65535],
bias/LoRA/kv_consumer/PCP/existing custom op, weight
dtype/layout/format), numerical equivalence of the fallback path vs. MM
+ ReduceScatter, fresh weight view per forward, fused failure is not
silently retried as another collective, and hardware-capability gating.
- `tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_minimax_m3.py`: the op is installed
on attention O-projections only when SP is active, with the
model-supplied token limits.
- `tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`: the new
`MM_REDUCE_SCATTER_BF16` capability.

**Performance benchmark: BF16 ISL sweep (OSL=1)**

- **Model:** MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-bf16
- **Parallelism:** TP4 + DP4 + EP
- **Configuration:** `max-num-seqs=4`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`,
`weight_nz_mode=1`, `max-model-len=2560`
- **vLLM main:**
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15
- **Benchmark:** `vllm bench serve` with random dataset; ISL
64/128/256/512/1024/2048, OSL 1, 64 prompts, `--request-rate inf
--max-concurrency 16 --ignore-eos`
- **Methodology:** 1 warm-up run + 3 measured runs with different seeds;
numbers are median [min, max] across the 3 measured runs
- **Comparison:** Baseline vs. prefill-only MMRS fusion (`62410cd3`)

| ISL | Baseline (tok/s) | MMRS (tok/s) | Speedup | Mean TTFT Reduction
|
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64 | 949.1 [816–1048] | 1199.3 [1178–1265] | **1.264x** | 18.8% |
| 128 | 1978.6 [1919–2109] | 2561.8 [2392–2634] | **1.295x** | 18.8% |
| 256 | 4204.0 [3847–4238] | 5159.3 [5062–5197] | **1.227x** | 17.7% |
| 512 | 7683.7 [7577–8105] | 9644.4 [9173–10018] | **1.255x** | 17.3% |
| 1024 | 9442.2 [9019–9660] | 10971.9 [10865–11767] | **1.162x** | 13.3%
|
| 2048 | 8818.7 [8774–9117] | 10353.8 [10101–10589] | **1.174x** | 14.4%
|

MMRS achieves **1.16x–1.30x end-to-end throughput speedup** across all
tested ISLs, with **13–19% lower mean TTFT**. No performance regression
was observed within the tested range.

+from vllm.config import get_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.forward_context import get_forward_context, is_forward_context_available
+from vllm.logger import logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import UnquantizedLinearMethod
+
+from vllm_ascend.device.device_op import DeviceOperator
+from vllm_ascend.device.hardware_profile import HardwareCapability, get_current_hardware_profile
+from vllm_ascend.models.common.ops.sequence_parallel import sp_reduce_scatter
+from vllm_ascend.ops.linear_op import CustomRowParallelOp
+from vllm_ascend.utils import ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_ND
+
+
+class SequenceParallelMMReduceScatterOp(CustomRowParallelOp):
+    """Unquantized BF16 projection owning the post-attention ReduceScatter.
+
+    The model installs the op on the O-projection when sequence parallelism
+    is active (without SP the projection keeps its plain GEMM forward). It
+    replaces the whole forward: fused MMRS when possible, otherwise plain
+    MM + ReduceScatter. Both paths return the SP token shard, so the caller
+    never branches.
+
+    Every gate is evaluated dynamically in _can_fuse, keeping the only
+    fused/fallback branch in run(). Facts that cannot change after loading
+    (config, hardware capability, layer layout) are cached once at
+    construction; the weight layout is re-checked per forward (a cheap
+    metadata read) and passed as a fresh transposed view. The backend
+    targets BF16 MMRS with BF16 output and requires ND weights (the
+    production BF16 configuration, weight_nz_mode=1); any other weight
+    format stays on the fallback.
+    """
+
+    SUPPORTED_TP_SIZES = (2, 4, 8)
+    # GEMM inner-dimension range supported by the fused kernel, same bounds
+    # as the Kimi O-projection backend.
+    MIN_K = 256
+    MAX_K = 65535
+
+    def __init__(self, layer, attention_layer_name: str, *, min_tokens: int, max_tokens: int):
+        super().__init__(layer)
+        self.update_attrs()
+        self.attention_layer_name = attention_layer_name
+        self.min_tokens = min_tokens
+        self.max_tokens = max_tokens
+        # A custom op already owning the layer's communication (e.g.
+        # fine-grained OTP) keeps ownership; this op only delegates to it.
+        self._previous_op = layer.custom_op
+        backend = self.comm_group.device_group._get_backend(torch.device("npu"))
+        self.hcom = backend.get_hccl_comm_name(self.tp_rank)
+        self._static_reason = self._find_static_reason()
+        if self._static_reason is None:
+            logger.info_once("Layer MMRS enabled for %s", self.prefix)
+        else:
+            logger.info_once("Layer MMRS disabled for %s: %s", self.prefix, self._static_reason)
+
+    def _find_static_reason(self) -> str | None:
+        """Collect the facts fixed after loading; None leaves fusion possible."""
+        layer = self.layer
+        if self._previous_op is not None:
+            return "an existing custom linear op owns the communication"
+        if layer.reduce_results or not layer.input_is_parallel or layer.disable_tp:
+            return "requires a TP-partitioned input and an external ReduceScatter"
+        if layer.bias is not None:
+            return "only bias-free projections are supported"
+        if self.tp_size not in self.SUPPORTED_TP_SIZES:
+            return "requires TP size 2, 4 or 8"
+        if not callable(getattr(torch_npu, "npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base", None)):
+            return "requires the torch_npu fused MM+ReduceScatter interface"
+        if not isinstance(layer.quant_method, UnquantizedLinearMethod):
+            return "requires an unquantized linear method"
+        weight = getattr(layer, "weight", None)
+        if weight is None or weight.ndim != 2 or weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+            return "requires unquantized BF16 projection weights"
+        config = get_current_vllm_config()
+        # Pure decode nodes (PD-disaggregated kv_consumer) never see a
+        # prefill batch, so the fused path could never fire.
+        transfer = config.kv_transfer_config
+        if transfer is not None and transfer.is_kv_consumer and not transfer.is_kv_producer:
+            return "a pure decode node never runs a prefill batch"
+        if config.lora_config is not None:
+            return "LoRA owns the projection weights"
+        # Context-parallel weight/group adaptations have a separate
+        # ownership contract. Only the original TP group is supported.
+        if (
+            config.parallel_config.prefill_context_parallel_size != 1
+            or config.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size != 1
+        ):
+            return "context parallelism owns the TP group"
+        if not get_current_hardware_profile().supports(HardwareCapability.MM_REDUCE_SCATTER_BF16):
+            return "hardware does not support the BF16 MM ReduceScatter kernel"
+        return None
+
+    def apply_impl(self, input_: torch.Tensor):
+        if self._previous_op is not None:
+            return self._previous_op.apply_impl(input_)
+        return self.run(input_), self.bias if self.skip_bias_add else None
+
+    def run(self, input_: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # The only fused/fallback branch; every gate lives in _can_fuse and
+        # is evaluated per forward, before any collective.
+        if not self._can_fuse(input_):
+            return self._run_fallback(input_)
+        return self._run_fused(input_)
+
+    def _can_fuse(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+        if self._static_reason is not None:
+            return False
+        if not is_forward_context_available():
+            return False
+        metadata = get_forward_context().attn_metadata
+        if isinstance(metadata, dict):
+            metadata = metadata.get(self.attention_layer_name)
+        # Missing metadata includes dummy/profile runs. Decode and mixed
+        # batches stay on the existing path, including FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture.
+        if metadata is None or getattr(metadata, "num_prefills", 0) <= 0 or getattr(metadata, "num_decodes", None) != 0:
+            return False
+        if x.ndim != 2 or x.dtype != torch.bfloat16 or x.shape[0] == 0:
+            return False
+        if not self.MIN_K <= x.shape[1] < self.MAX_K:
+            return False
+        # The model gates the token count to the range where fusion pays
+        # off; TP ranks see the same count after the SP all-gather.
+        if not self.min_tokens <= x.shape[0] < self.max_tokens:
+            return False
+        return self._weight_supported(x)
+
+    def _weight_supported(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+        """Check the weight layout for the fused kernel, per forward.
+
+        The loaded weight is [N, K]; the fused operator takes a fresh
+        transposed [K, N] view of it (no copy, nothing cached), so a
+        replaced or in-place-mutated weight is seen on the very next call.
+        """
+        weight = self.layer.weight
+        basic = (
+            weight.ndim == 2
+            and weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+            and weight.shape[0] == self.layer.output_size
+            and weight.shape[1] == x.shape[1]
+            and self.layer.output_size > 0
+            and weight.is_contiguous()
+        )
+        return basic and torch_npu.get_npu_format(weight) == ACL_FORMAT_FRACTAL_ND
+
+    def _run_fallback(self, input_: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Plain MM + ReduceScatter fallback returning the SP token shard."""
+        assert self.quant_method is not None
+        input_parallel = self.get_input_parallel(input_)
+        # Only rank 0 adds the bias, so the ReduceScatter does not duplicate it.
+        bias = None if (self.tp_rank > 0 or self.skip_bias_add) else self.bias
+        output = self.quant_method.apply(self.layer, input_parallel, bias)
+        # The caller dropped its external ReduceScatter; this op returns
+        # the SP token shard on every path.
+        return sp_reduce_scatter(output)
+
+    def _run_fused(self, input_: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """BF16 MM + ReduceScatter through the fused path.
+
+        sp_reduce_scatter zero-pads the GEMM result to the TP multiple, so
+        padding the bias-free input rows beforehand yields the same shard.
+        _can_fuse has already validated the weight layout; the [K, N]
+        transposed view is created here per call (no copy).
+        """
+        logger.info_once("Layer MMRS fused path active")
+        padding = (-input_.shape[0]) % self.tp_size
+        if padding:
+            input_ = F.pad(input_, (0, 0, 0, padding))
+        # comm_mode is left to the device adaptor's per-platform default
+        # (AIV on A2/A3, AI CPU or CCU on A5).
+        return DeviceOperator.npu_mm_reduce_scatter_base(
+            input_.contiguous(),
+            self.layer.weight.t(),
+            self.hcom,
+            self.tp_size,
+            reduce_op="sum",
+        )

[BugFix][DSV4] Load KV cache epilog before use (#22553)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix DeepSeek V4 FP8 KV-cache writes that reach `kv_compress_epilog`
before its CANN package has been imported. An empty-query PCP worker
still updates global KV, but can skip the query metadata path that
previously registered the operator.

Resolve the operator at its use site in `dsa_attn_kv_plan.py`: import
`cann_ops_transformer`, retrieve the operator, and cache the successful
lookup per process. KV writes then own their dependency independently of
query metadata. Package import and missing-operator errors propagate.
Existing dispatch, cache layout, slot mapping, and quantization
arguments are preserved.

The production change is confined to the KV writer. The failure analysis
and original fix came from
[li1how/vllm-ascend@07c8c40a](https://github.com/li1how/vllm-ascend/commit/07c8c40a5887f1a22edb4e1b6f6b6f433988eddc).

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DeepSeek V4 on Ascend A5 with FP8 KV caching can update global KV
from an empty-query PCP worker without depending on prior metadata
construction to register the operator. No configuration changes are
required. The installed CANN package must still provide
`kv_compress_epilog`.

### How was this patch tested?

- Reproduction: the first-use regression fails on the unpatched KV
writer with `AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'kv_compress_epilog'`.
- Fixed implementation: **9 CPU tests passed**:
  ```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --confcutdir=tests/ut/attention
tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_kv_epilog_cpu.py
  ```
These tests execute the actual writer and loader functions with
dependency stubs, following the repository's isolated CPU-test pattern.
They cover first use without query metadata, cached reuse, import
failures, a missing operator after import, absent updates, and
non-epilog cache plans. They do not execute CANN kernels.
- Passed: Python syntax; the repository's Ruff, codespell, typos,
forbidden-import, and boolean-context-manager hooks; the direct
long-function check; and `git diff --check`.
- Full pre-commit remains pending: WSL Git 2.43 rejects the shared
repository's `relativeworktrees` extension. The native long-function
hook also cannot resolve `python3`; running that same checker with the
installed Python succeeds.
- **A5 real-NPU KV-writer regression passed** (CANN 9.2.1, torch 2.10.0,
torch-npu 2.10.0.post7): executing the production writer without query
metadata reproduced the original missing-operator `AttributeError`
before the fix. With the fix, first and repeated writes succeeded,
output bytes matched the original writer after explicit operator
registration, and unmapped cache rows remained unchanged. This isolated
check used real CANN/NPU tensors, not dependency stubs.
- The validation reported here covers the isolated KV writer. The full
P4+D4 before/after inference run was cancelled before obtaining a
complete comparison.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: First-use registration without
query metadata, absent updates, and other cache plans.
- [x] **Regression test**: The first-use case fails before the fix and
passes after it.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: Import failures and missing
operator errors remain visible.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: CPU tests execute the production
functions and check dependency ordering, cache reuse, and tensor storage
forwarding.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: A5 inference and graph validation remain
pending.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+"""Check KV writer dependency loading without importing the NPU model stack."""
+
+import ast
+from functools import lru_cache
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import Mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+
+def _load_scatter():
+    source = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_attn_kv_plan.py"
+    tree = ast.parse(source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    functions = [
+        node for node in tree.body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == "_get_kv_compress_epilog"
+    ]
+    plan = next(node for node in tree.body if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and node.name == "DsaAttnKvPlan")
+    functions.append(
+        next(node for node in plan.body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == "dsa_kv_compress_scatter")
+    )
+    future = ast.ImportFrom(module="__future__", names=[ast.alias(name="annotations")], level=0)
+    module = ast.fix_missing_locations(ast.Module(body=[future, *functions], type_ignores=[]))
+    namespace = SimpleNamespace()
+    native_scatter, bf16_scatter = Mock(), Mock()
+    torch_api = SimpleNamespace(
+        uint8=torch.uint8,
+        ops=SimpleNamespace(
+            cann_ops_transformer=namespace,
+            _C_ascend=SimpleNamespace(npu_scatter_nd_update_sk=native_scatter),
+        ),
+    )
+    load = Mock()
+    scope = {
+        "torch": torch_api,
+        "torch_npu": SimpleNamespace(npu_scatter_nd_update_=bf16_scatter),
+        "lru_cache": lru_cache,
+        "import_module": load,
+    }
+    exec(compile(module, str(source), "exec"), scope)
+    return scope["dsa_kv_compress_scatter"], load, namespace, native_scatter, bf16_scatter
+
+
+def test_fp8_scatter_loads_epilog_without_query_metadata():
+    scatter, load, namespace, _, _ = _load_scatter()
+    plan = SimpleNamespace(uses_sparse_flash_mla=False, uses_kv_compress_epilog=True)
+    cache = torch.zeros(2, 32, 1, 608, dtype=torch.uint8)
+    updates = torch.ones(3, 1, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    slots = torch.tensor([0, 1, 2], dtype=torch.int32)
+    events = []
+    epilog = Mock(side_effect=lambda **kwargs: events.append("write"))
+
+    def register(name):
+        events.append("import")
+        namespace.kv_compress_epilog = epilog
+
+    load.side_effect = register
+    # An empty-query PCP rank still writes the restored global KV rows.
+    # Start with no registered epilog and do not build any query metadata.
+    scatter(plan, cache, updates, slots)
+    scatter(plan, cache, updates, slots)
+
+    assert events == ["import", "write", "write"]
+    load.assert_called_once_with("cann_ops_transformer")
+    assert epilog.call_count == 2
+    passed = epilog.call_args.kwargs
+    assert passed["cache"].data_ptr() == cache.data_ptr()
+    assert passed["cache"].dtype == torch.uint8
+    assert passed["x"].shape == (3, 512)
+    assert passed["x"].data_ptr() == updates.data_ptr()
+    assert passed["slot_mapping"] is slots
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure", [ImportError("missing package"), RuntimeError("package initialization failed")])
+def test_fp8_scatter_preserves_import_errors(failure):
+    scatter, load, _, _, _ = _load_scatter()
+    plan = SimpleNamespace(uses_sparse_flash_mla=False, uses_kv_compress_epilog=True)
+    load.side_effect = failure
+
+    with pytest.raises(type(failure)) as raised:
+        scatter(plan, torch.zeros(1), torch.zeros(1, 512), torch.tensor([0]))
+
+    assert raised.value is failure
+
+
+def test_fp8_scatter_reports_missing_epilog_after_import():
+    scatter, load, _, _, _ = _load_scatter()
+    plan = SimpleNamespace(uses_sparse_flash_mla=False, uses_kv_compress_epilog=True)
+
+    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="kv_compress_epilog"):
+        scatter(plan, torch.zeros(1), torch.zeros(1, 512), torch.tensor([0]))
+
+    load.assert_called_once_with("cann_ops_transformer")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "uses_sparse_flash_mla,uses_kv_compress_epilog", [(True, False), (False, False), (False, True)]
+)
+def test_scatter_loads_no_package_for_none_updates(uses_sparse_flash_mla, uses_kv_compress_epilog):
+    scatter, load, _, native, bf16 = _load_scatter()
+    plan = SimpleNamespace(
+        uses_sparse_flash_mla=uses_sparse_flash_mla,
+        uses_kv_compress_epilog=uses_kv_compress_epilog,
+    )
+
+    scatter(plan, torch.zeros(1), None, torch.tensor([0]))
+
+    load.assert_not_called()
+    native.assert_not_called()
+    bf16.assert_not_called()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("uses_sparse_flash_mla", [False, True])
+def test_other_scatter_plans_do_not_load_cann(uses_sparse_flash_mla):
+    scatter, load, _, native, bf16 = _load_scatter()
+    plan = SimpleNamespace(uses_sparse_flash_mla=uses_sparse_flash_mla, uses_kv_compress_epilog=False)

+    load.assert_not_called()

+    (native if uses_sparse_flash_mla else bf16).assert_not_called()

[Feature][Model] Enable DeepSeek V4.1 MRV2 PP with arbitrary layer partitions (#19284)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable experimental DeepSeek V4.1 pipeline parallelism on Model Runner
V2 with arbitrary contiguous, nonempty layer partitions. For example,
with `23,17`, the second stage still consumes KV/index data produced by
layer 20, as well as shared selection state. These dependencies now
travel with the PP activations.

- Derive each boundary's live dependencies from the model topology,
including dependencies needed beyond the immediate next stage. Transfer
updated KV/index-cache rows and scales, Top-K selections and valid
lengths, candidates, HC activations, FP32 pre-mix coefficients and
DSpark auxiliary states.
- Register cache-only mirrors with the original logical names/specs.
Keep global scheduler block IDs and independent physical allocations.
Preserve main's capacity accounting while handling empty
compression-state groups and uneven stage-local SWA groups.
- Put wire-buffer allocation, native cache-row gathering/scattering,
state snapshots and custom-op execution ordering in
`worker/v2/pp_transport.py`. The model declares its boundary manifests
and mirrors. Reuse the existing PCP gather kernel without modifying its
module.
- For PCP, copy caches using canonical global write slots while keeping
query state local. A PCP-sized cache axis preserves the leading
local-token extent expected by PP slicing; replicated source caches need
no additional PCP collectives.
- Retain bounded Prefill replay on every eligible stage when SP is
disabled. Finish full-batch source-cache writes before trimming when
using the supported cut-layer writer and restore token correspondence
before exporting PP state. Keep the replay-state implementation
identical to main; SP execution uses the original full query batch.
- Construct/query only stage-local Engram tables, selecting their
original global hash slots for both local and remote readers. Preserve
main's shared-reader/shared-pool lifecycle. Follow main's zero-based
checkpoint layer IDs and capture each selected layer's input in both
normal and replay paths. Receiving PP stages capture their own
start-layer inputs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION` can specify counts such as `23,17` or
`24,16`, summing to the backbone layer count. Stages must be nonempty
and fit device memory. MRV2 is required; existing Engram TP restrictions
and DCP1 remain.

`--swa-bounded-replay` enables per-stage decoder-tail Prefill trimming
after the final shared-KV source when sequence parallelism is disabled.
PCP, SP execution, DSpark with async scheduling and target Decode graphs
remain supported, but SP configurations skip decoder-tail compaction and
execute the full query batch. The graph configuration is
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: model compilation remains enabled, while Prefill
stays outside full ACL Graph capture. Existing replay restrictions for
DCP, microbatching, LoRA and incompatible drafters remain. A5 and
multimodal execution need separate qualification.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Current validation — 2026-11-20

Head `f8f2549e9d0c22d4203a2b1576394f356367bc43` is based on main
`1e0f0da1f740400a1d6796bcc23a13b53ca0b464`. The vLLM pin is
`c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15`, identical to main.

- Four linear commits with no merge commits: the PP implementation,
real-CLiang's A5 packed-cache fix, its CPU regression, and the Engram
backend-dispatch fixture update. The A5 fix retains its original
authorship and [source
reference](https://github.com/real-CLiang/vllm-ascend/commit/1028b45ba3be4e1bc2ea3ef7ae797f9dabb135eb).
- Rebased onto main's upstream embedding-API compatibility fix (#22530)
without conflicts. `git range-diff` confirms all four PP commit patches
are unchanged. Main's A5 replay-plan ratios and the PP output-row
restoration remain together.
- Related CPU regression against the pinned vLLM source: **1594 passed,
10 skipped** across 32 test files, including the embedding-API, PCP
multimodal embedding-padding and vocabulary-embedding regressions. The
source-archive harness explicitly selects the CPU platform; it does not
provide NPU validation.
- All 15 changed Python files pass mypy for Python 3.10/3.11/3.12, with
runtime and tests checked separately. `bash format.sh ci` passes with
Gitleaks/ShellCheck skipped because their local binaries are
unavailable; the PR diff passes whitespace checks.
- The PR changes **15 files**. The release-note fragment remains
removed; no new E2E file is added. Generic
runner/attention/cache-builder paths, the PCP kernel module, decoder
replay state and the model tutorial match main.
- **Current-head online CI passed:** [E2E run
44677403602](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/44677403602),
**30 jobs passed, 5 skipped**. Both CPU lanes (paired vLLM main and
v0.33.0), pre-commit, upstream E2E, the selected A2/A3/310P device
tests, CODEOWNERS coverage/approval and the final gate passed. DCO and
both Read the Docs checks also passed, with no failed or pending PR
checks at verification. A5 E2E was skipped by CI selection; this run
does not qualify A5.
- Main's embedding-API fix (#22530) is included in this head. The former
argument-count failure did not occur in the passing run.
- **No new standalone DeepSeek V4.1 real-weight, GSM8K or profiling run
was performed for this head.** A5 results were [reported by real-CLiang
before the subsequent main
updates](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19284#issuecomment-6997504258).
Historical results below do not qualify the current head.

#### Earlier A3 qualification — 2026-11-17

**Historical evidence:** the SP-on cases below used an older
implementation with SP compaction enabled. Current SP execution
intentionally skips that compaction, so those cases and the older GSM8K

+        local_slots += [-1] * (n - len(local_slots))

+    receiver.receive(payload, n)

+class _ModelLayer(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, index):

+    def forward(self, positions, hidden, pre_mix, scaling, input_ids=None):

[Feature][Model] Add MiniMax-M3 Union attention with native fallback (#21860)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add Union sparse prefill attention for MiniMax-M3/M3.1 on Ascend A2, A3
and A5. Union merges up to eight adjacent queries within each request
while preserving each query's selected KV blocks and causal mask.

The matching optional operators are [UnionSparseGen (ops-nn
#14010)](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-nn/pull/14010) and [GBSA
exact-mask (ops-transformer
#15473)](https://gitcode.com/cann/ops-transformer/pull/15473). Build
matching device-specific `.run` packages and standard `cann_ops_nn` /
`cann_ops_transformer` wheels. Leave `TORCH_EXTENSION_OPS` unset when
building the wheels. `_can_use_union_attention` checks dtype, geometry
and optional native backend availability before graph capture. There is
no Union-specific hardware capability gate: A2 follows the same
selection rules. Missing or unloadable extensions retain native prefill.
Neither the hardware-profile module nor its tests are changed by this
PR.

Prepare Union GBSA metadata in the sparse metadata builder, following
the persistent-buffer pattern in #18426. Each build updates one capacity
schedule per `(num_heads, topk)` configuration and shares it across
matching layers. The exact-mask kernels use each layer's runtime
`union_count` to bound KV work. Metadata and int64 query-prefix buffers
retain stable addresses for graph execution; layer forward reuses the
initialization-time Union eligibility result.

Move cuQ conversion into the builder, reuse existing int32 sequence
lengths, omit redundant cuKV when `seqused_kv` is supplied, and reduce
counts directly to int32. No new configuration flags are added.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Supported prefill configurations use **Union -> KV-gather-Q ->
Q-gather-KV** according to operator availability, including BF16/FP16 on
A2. Existing FP8 restrictions remain: A2/A3 FP8 KV-cache is unsupported;
A5 FP8 uses BF16 queries/output. Decode, including speculative
verification, retains its native attention and existing metadata reuse.
Runtime attention execution errors propagate.

### How was this patch tested?

Current revision: `f7f70a05c6cd692cfdb835bd1b8b00006fad3159`, based on
upstream main `8cd3c3762d8a10cd9bd814110c5a3b69999b6269`.

- Ruff 0.14.0 lint/format, Python syntax parsing and `git diff --check`
passed locally. Confirmed that the hardware-profile implementation and
tests match the PR base and all references to the removed Union
capability are gone.
- Updated the existing operator-availability dispatch test to expect
Union on A2 as well as A3/A5, and extended the existing FP8 rejection
test to cover A2. CPU/NPU tests were not run for this revision because
the local environment lacks PyTorch, vLLM and an NPU runtime. `bash
format.sh ci` was attempted but stopped because pre-commit is not
installed. Current runtime validation remains for CI/reviewers,
including A2/A3 hardware execution.
- The earlier mypy fix is retained: ignore missing optional
`cann_ops_nn` imports and assert that Union metadata exists before
indexing it.

Previously recorded validation below applies to revision
`6babfe5d2bb13818f7016b17bf4f7544cbbe638e` against metadata baseline
`9b3308c4b938dd349c8b2ab7d442f9edb6ad6c87`; it was not rerun for the
current revision:

- **583 CPU tests passed**: `pytest -q
tests/ut/models/minimax_m3/test_msa_m3.py
tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`, with NPU entry points mocked.
Coverage included shared metadata, stable buffer addresses and refresh,
BF16/FP16/FP8, mixed prefill/decode and unavailable/unloadable-extension
fallback.
- **Machine 26, Ascend 950DT, physical card 7:** CANN `9.3.0` (Nov 9
build), matching Nov 14 canonical operator wheels, PyTorch `2.10.0+cpu`
and `torch_npu 2.10.0.post7`. Both real native backends loaded and
executed on NPU.
- **13 synthetic single-layer NPU A/B cases passed**, including 16k/128k
BF16/FP8, multiple requests, chunked/small prefill, uneven groups and
FP16. Eager and NPUGraph outputs matched the baseline bitwise for three
sparse-selection patterns per case.
- **Real module/builder integration passed for FP8, BF16 and FP16:** two
same-geometry layer forwards with different selections matched the
baseline in eager and NPUGraph execution. Rebuilding metadata preserved
addresses and graph results. Kernel profiles confirmed one Metadata call
in builder plus two layers, zero Metadata calls in layer forwards alone,
and two UnionSparseGen calls.

For 16 local Q heads, one KV head, head dimension 128 and topk 16,
alternating baseline/candidate NPUGraph device-time medians were
recorded over 20 rounds, five calls per sample:

| Workload | Baseline (us) | Candidate (us) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16k FP8 | 1341.06 | 1267.48 | 5.49% |
| 16k BF16 | 1609.28 | 1533.06 | 4.74% |
| 128k FP8 | 11463.93 | 11122.06 | 2.98% |
| 128k BF16 | 14291.70 | 13889.91 | 2.81% |

These are synthetic single-layer measurements. Candidate times exclude
metadata preparation moved into the builder and amortized across layers;
they do not establish full-model throughput or accuracy. Kernel profiles
showed five fewer tasks per layer: three query-prefix casts, one count
cast, and metadata generation moved out of layer forward. Full-model E2E
and A2/A3 hardware execution remain unverified.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Optional Union sparse prefill attention for MiniMax-M3 on Ascend."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm_ascend.models.minimax_m3.ops.msa_m3_npu import (
+    _sort_valid_gbsa_prefix,
+    _split_main_kv_cache,
+    _to_fp8_e4m3,
+)
+
+# UnionSparseGen merges eight adjacent query rows, restarting at each request.
+UNION_SIZE = 8
+# Sparse selection width in KV tokens; this is not the paged KV-cache page size.
+_SPARSE_KV_BLOCK_SIZE = 128
+
+# CANN enum values shared by metadata preparation and attention execution.
+_UNION_LAYOUT = 4  # Head-major compressed sparse query groups.
+_UNION_MASK_MODE = 3  # Union's exact per-query block mask; disables FlashDecode.
+_FP8_STATIC_CAST_P = 5  # CANN quant mode: FP8 inputs with static probability casting.
+_NO_QUANT = 0  # CANN quant mode: unquantized attention.
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def prepare_union_gbsa_metadata(
+    cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    num_union_groups: int,
+    max_kv_blocks: int,
+    max_query_len: int,
+    max_seq_len: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+    topk: int,
+    kv_dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Prepare one capacity schedule for all layers with the same geometry."""
+    from cann_ops_transformer import generic_block_sparse_attention_metadata
+
+    capacity = min(UNION_SIZE * topk, max_kv_blocks)
+    # One sparse-pattern head is shared by all query heads in MiniMax-M3.
+    counts = torch.full((1, num_union_groups), capacity, dtype=torch.int32, device=seq_lens.device)
+    # Metadata reads counts and the indices' shape, not selected block IDs.
+    indices = torch.empty((*counts.shape, capacity), dtype=torch.int32, device=seq_lens.device)
+    # Union disables FlashDecode. The exact-mask kernels use each layer's
+    # runtime union_count to bound KV work, so capacity counts can share a
+    # schedule even when layers select different numbers of distinct blocks.
+    return generic_block_sparse_attention_metadata(
+        indices,
+        counts,
+        num_heads,
+        1,  # MiniMax-M3 has one KV head per rank.
+        _SPARSE_KV_BLOCK_SIZE,  # Head dimension is also 128 in supported M3 geometry.
+        [UNION_SIZE, _SPARSE_KV_BLOCK_SIZE],
+        cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens_q,
+        seqused_kv=seq_lens,
+        max_seqlen_q=max_query_len,
+        max_seqlen_kv=max_seq_len,
+        layout_q="TND",
+        layout_kv="PA_BBND",
+        layout_sparse_pattern=_UNION_LAYOUT,
+        mask_mode=_UNION_MASK_MODE,
+        quant_mode=_FP8_STATIC_CAST_P if kv_dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn else _NO_QUANT,
+        softmax_precision=0,  # Union requires precision 0, including FP8.
+        win_left=-1,  # No sliding-window limit.
+        win_right=-1,
+        residual_block_mode=0,  # No separate residual block.
+        is_consistent_topk=False,
+    )
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def minimax_m3_sparse_attn_union(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_cache: torch.Tensor | tuple[torch.Tensor, ...] | list[torch.Tensor],
+    topk_idx: torch.Tensor,
+    block_table: torch.Tensor,
+    cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    num_union_groups: int,
+    max_kv_blocks: int,
+    max_query_len: int,
+    max_seq_len: int,
+    sm_scale: float,
+    output: torch.Tensor,
+    metadata: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """Union eight adjacent queries while preserving their exact selected KV sets.
+
+    The caller selects supported geometry and supplies host-side capacities.
+    Group boundaries restart for each request.
+    """
+    from cann_ops_nn import union_sparse_gen_launch
+    from cann_ops_transformer import generic_block_sparse_attention
+
+    key, value = _split_main_kv_cache(kv_cache)
+    quantized = torch.float8_e4m3fn == key.dtype
+    # Reduce directly to the operator's int32 counts, avoiding an int64 result Cast.
+    counts = (topk_idx >= 0).sum(dim=-1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices = _sort_valid_gbsa_prefix(topk_idx, counts)
+    union_idx, union_count, exact_mask = union_sparse_gen_launch(
+        indices,
+        counts,
+        cu_seqlens_q,
+        None,  # seqused_kv below already supplies each request's KV length.
+        None,
+        seq_lens,
+        block_shape=[1, _SPARSE_KV_BLOCK_SIZE],  # One query row per input sparse pattern.
+        union_size=UNION_SIZE,
+        mask_type=1,  # Causal mask.
+        max_q_seqlen=max_query_len,
+        max_kv_seqlen=max_seq_len,
+        layout_sparse_pattern=_UNION_LAYOUT,
+        is_input_idx_sorted=True,
+        residual_block_mode=0,  # No separate residual block.
+        totalq_union_num=num_union_groups,
+        max_logical_blocks=max_kv_blocks,
+    )
+    # Union mask mode requires precision 0, including FP8; the native
+    # non-Union FP8 path's precision 1 is a different operator contract.
+    result, _ = generic_block_sparse_attention(
+        _to_fp8_e4m3(q) if quantized else q,
+        key,
+        value,
+        union_idx,
+        union_count,
+        [UNION_SIZE, _SPARSE_KV_BLOCK_SIZE],
+        metadata=metadata,
+        block_table=block_table,
+        attn_mask=exact_mask,
+        softmax_scale=sm_scale,
+        return_softmax_lse=False,
+        attention_out_dtype=output.dtype,
+        cu_seqlens_q=cu_seqlens_q,
+        cu_seqlens_kv=None,
+        seqused_kv=seq_lens,
+        layout_q="TND",
+        layout_kv="PA_BBND",
+        layout_sparse_pattern=_UNION_LAYOUT,
+        mask_mode=_UNION_MASK_MODE,
+        quant_mode=_FP8_STATIC_CAST_P if quantized else _NO_QUANT,
+        softmax_precision=0,
+        win_left=-1,  # No sliding-window limit.
+        win_right=-1,
+        residual_block_mode=0,  # No separate residual block.
+        is_consistent_topk=False,
+    )

[BugFix][KVPool] Request lazy store init for sparse-indexer models (#20538)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`KVPoolWorker` requests `lazy_init` from the storage backend only for
compressed models (`use_compress`, DSV4 `compress_ratios`) — the
deferral introduced for that family in #9771. Models that run the packed
C8 sparse-indexer KV pool path route their indexer KV through the pool
the same way but were never covered by that request, so the backend
always set the store up eagerly in its constructor.

The v0.26-based production chain shows what that ordering costs on
fabric memory (`ASCEND_ENABLE_USE_FABRIC_MEM=1`): with the packed C8
path active and the store set up eagerly at `KVPoolWorker` construction
— before the KV caches are registered — KV Pool startup hangs. Two
observations bracket the trigger:

- Turning the packed path off (eager setup unchanged) avoids the
failure.
- Deferring the store setup to the first `put()` — exactly what the
compressed path has done since #9771 — fixes it, with the packed path
itself untouched.

So the remedy is the store-setup ordering, but the failing surface is
the packed C8 path: eager setup plus a non-packed path does not
reproduce the hang. The gate therefore tracks the packed-path condition
rather than the model family alone. On main the v0.26 knob
(`c8_enable_reshape_optim`) no longer exists — the packed path is the
dtype-derived native default, active exactly when a sparse-indexer model
runs with an fp8/int8 `cache_dtype` (AscendConfig
`enable_sparse_sfa_c8`). The worker derives the same condition locally
from `vllm_config`, because the connector may be constructed before
AscendConfig is initialized:

```python
cache_dtype = vllm_config.cache_config.cache_dtype
packed_c8_path = self.use_sparse and cache_dtype in ("fp8", "int8")
backend_kwargs["lazy_init"] = self.use_compress or packed_c8_path
```

Blast radius is narrow: backends only honor `lazy_init` under fabric
memory (Mooncake) / `device_sdma` (Memcache), so other deployments see
no behavior change, and the lazy semantics (`exists()` reports misses
before init, `put()` triggers initialization) are unchanged since #9771.
Sparse models with other cache dtypes keep eager init — the trigger does
not reproduce there. `turboquant` stays out of the gate: it is a
different packed variant and was not part of the reproduced trigger.

A documentation section (motivation, semantics, and the affected model
families) has also been added to the Ascend Store KV Cache Pool guide,
as requested in review.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, a behavioral fix: for models on the packed C8 cache path (sparse +
fp8/int8 KV) on fabric-memory (Mooncake) or `device_sdma` (Memcache)
deployments, the KV Pool store is now initialized lazily on first use
instead of eagerly at startup, matching the compressed-model behavior
from #9771.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit test added in
`tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py`
(`TestLazyInitGate`): dense models request eager init; compressed models
request lazy init (#9771 unchanged); sparse + int8 and sparse + fp8
request lazy init (this fix); sparse + non-C8 dtype keeps eager init
(narrow-gate regression case). Full ascend_store UT suite: 999 passed,
12 skipped.
- Production chain on a v0.26-based deployment (GLM-5.x SFA + packed c8
indexer KV + Mooncake fabric-memory KV Pool): eager startup store setup
fails as described above; with the deferral the deployment starts and
pool operations initialize the store on first use.
- Doc section added to
`docs/source/user_guide/feature_guide/kv_cache_pool_ascend_store.md`
("Lazy Store Initialization"), covering why lazy init exists, the
first-`put()` semantics, and the affected model families.

[Refactor][MRV2][Attention] Refactor MLA Decode with UpdatableGraph (#21329)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Refactors MLA decode graph capture and replay in
`vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py` to use `UpdatableGraph`. The previous
`AscendMLAImpl.update_graph_params()` path rebuilt captured FIA calls
from parallel parameter, handle, and event lists, so updates depended on
the order of attention layers.

- Registers each `npu_fused_infer_attention_score_v2.out` call as a
graph task during capture. The task retains its operation arguments and
output tensors, removing the MLA-specific graph parameter bookkeeping.
- Adds `MLAParamProvider` to resolve runtime parameters from the current
layer's decode metadata. It pads target KV lengths, builds EAGLE target
query lengths, and supplies draft query lengths, KV lengths, and block
tables, including trimming the draft block table when padded batches are
disabled.
- Uses `get_capture_resource()` to allocate and reuse the FIA workspace
across captures. The speculative decoders are updated to pass MLA FIA
sequence-length and block-table parameters in the new form.

Related design: #13058; earlier `UpdatableGraph` work: #16798.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This changes the internal MLA graph capture and replay path without
changing public APIs, configuration, or defaults.

### How was this patch tested?

- Pre-commit, CPU unit tests against vLLM main and v0.33.0, and
DCO/title checks passed.
- `tests/ut/attention/test_mla_v1.py` covers target KV padding, EAGLE
query lengths, and draft block-table trimming.
`tests/ut/attention/test_mla_fp8_decode_layout.py` checks registered FIA
task arguments, outputs, layouts, and provider resolution.
- `tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_mla_fp8_decode_layout_a5.py`
exercises capture, update, and replay with changed inputs for regular
and speculative decode in FP8/BF16 paths.
- A3 targeted test with Kimi-K2.6 W4A8 + Eagle3 MLA and
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`: GSM8K accuracy was **92/100** (same-configuration
pre-PR baseline **93/100**). All 128 performance requests completed with
0 failures; output throughput was **346.1076 token/s** versus **348.6677
token/s** on the baseline (−0.73%), with mean TTFT **419.7 ms** versus
**436.9 ms** and mean TPOT **22.6 ms** versus **22.4 ms**. This run
exercised MLA decode and Eagle3 graph capture/replay, including the
changed `mla_v1.py` FIA task registration and runtime parameter handling
paths.

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] Boundary cases: sequence-length padding, EAGLE query lengths, and
draft block-table trimming.
- [x] Regression coverage: updated graph inputs and metadata are
exercised on replay.
- [x] Error paths and test assertions reviewed.
- [x] A3 Kimi-K2.6 W4A8 + Eagle3 MLA accuracy and performance compared
against the same-configuration pre-PR baseline.

[BugFix][Scheduler] Sync copied schedulers with upstream encoder input handling (#22206)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

The Balance (`patch_balance_schedule.py`), DyntraLB and Recompute
schedulers each keep a local copy of upstream `Scheduler.schedule()`, so
upstream fixes inside that method do not reach them. This PR syncs three
upstream changes into the copies and fixes one connector side effect
they expose.

- **vllm-project/vllm#59942** made `_try_schedule_encoder_inputs` return
a fifth value (duplicate encoder inputs) and added
`_allocate_encoder_inputs`. The Balance and DyntraLB copies still
unpacked four values, so on vLLM 0.32 and later every multimodal request
raised `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 4)` and killed
EngineCore. Text-only requests never reach that line, which is why it
went unnoticed. The copies now take the fifth value and allocate through
the upstream helper, which also keeps the cache reference of a repeated
image. Recompute already followed upstream.
- **vllm-project/vllm#57368** lets the scheduler tell the Model Runner
V2 worker to drop a multimodal input's CPU payload once its placeholder
range is consumed, and to reinstall it when a rewind needs it again.
None of the copies, Recompute included, filled
`SchedulerOutput.encoder_input_updates`, so the worker kept every
request's pixels until the request finished. Each copy now forwards
`_get_encoder_input_updates()`.
- **vllm-project/vllm#41567** asks the EC connector
(`ensure_cache_available`) before each running chunk and before a
waiting request that resumes with computed tokens, not only for new
waiting requests. With `ECMooncakeConnector` that call is what starts a
load; `has_cache_item` also answers True for an item that is available
on the Encoder but not loaded. The Balance and DyntraLB copies only
checked new waiting requests, so an image whose encoder output was
evicted from the local cache between prefill chunks was scheduled as an
external load that no worker load served, and the model runner raised
`Encoder cache miss`. The two checks are added; Recompute already had
them. The connector hooks that change added to `update_from_output()`
and freeing are inherited unchanged.
- **`ECMemcacheConnector`**: with the running check above, the scheduler
asks the EC connector about every running multimodal request on every
step. `ECMemcacheConnector.ensure_cache_available` ignored
`num_computed_tokens` and forgets its hits each step, so each decode
step queried memcache again for inputs consumed long ago and counted
every answer as a hit. It now skips inputs whose placeholder range ends
before `num_computed_tokens`, as `ECMooncakeConnector` does. This
already happened with the default upstream scheduler, which has had the
running check since #41567.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Bug fixes only; see `release_notes/fragments/22206.yaml`. No new options
or default changes.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests** (CPU mode, vLLM v0.33.0): the 16 affected files under
`tests/ut/core`, `tests/ut/patch/platform` and `tests/ut/distributed`
pass (442 passed, 1 skipped; the skip also happens on main). New tests
in `tests/ut/core/test_scheduler_encoder_inputs.py` run against every
copied scheduler class:

- repeated-image cache references for waiting and running requests;
- CPU payload released after prefill and reinstalled after preemption;
- an evicted encoder output and a resumed waiting request, driven
through the real `AscendECMooncakeScheduler` consumer: the request is
deferred and a load is dispatched. With the Balance and DyntraLB checks
reverted, exactly those 6 cases fail; Balance then schedules the request
with no load dispatched for the image.

**End-to-end on Atlas A3** (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, Balance with DP=2,
`--enforce-eager`, vLLM v0.33.0):

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #59942: one text and one image request through Balance | text OK;
image request returns HTTP 500, EngineCore dies with `too many values to
unpack (expected 4)` at `patch_balance_schedule.py` `schedule()` | both
OK, server alive; outputs match the default scheduler token for token |
| #57368: worker `update_encoder_inputs` traced | with the three
`encoder_input_updates` lines removed from Balance: no release | one
`{0: None}` per image request after prefill; under forced preemption
(2560-token KV cache, 8 concurrent image requests) the 2 preempted
requests are reinstalled and released again, all 8 complete |
| #41567: E + PD with `ECMooncakeConnector` (`mooncake_protocol:
ascend`, HCCS), Balance DP=2 on PD. Image B is warm in the PD cache,
request R = image A + ~4.5k tokens + image B is chunked 64 tokens per
step, and a request with 6 new images evicts B mid-prefill | with the
Balance checks reverted: PD raises `Encoder cache miss` for B and
EngineCore dies | R reloads B from the Encoder at computed=2816 and
answers correctly |

Not covered: DyntraLB and Recompute end to end (they run on
PD-disaggregated D nodes, which the EPD guide does not give an EC
connector; covered by the unit tests above), the streaming-input path of
the resumed-waiting check (unit test only), and the unit tests against
the pinned vLLM main commit (CI runs them).

Note: `/reset_encoder_cache` cannot be used to reproduce the #41567 case
on v0.33.0. That version does not reset the Mooncake connector on it and
crashes with `Encoder cache miss` with or without this PR; upstream
fixed that separately in vllm-project/vllm#66846.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: I reviewed whether this change
involves
boundary conditions (e.g. empty input, single/zero element, min/max
values,
off-by-one, sequence-length limits, integer overflow). Where applicable,
I
added unit tests covering these edge cases in `tests/ut/` or
`tests/e2e/`.
- [x] **Regression test**: If this PR fixes a bug, I added a regression
test
  that would fail without the fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: I covered abnormal paths
(exceptions,
timeouts, out-of-range, division by zero) in addition to the happy path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: New tests assert real behavior
and are
  not written merely to satisfy CI.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: If this PR touches a performance-sensitive
path,
  I attached benchmark results and added performance regression tests.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15

+def _make_scheduler(scheduler_cls: type[Scheduler]) -> Scheduler:
+    config = make_dyntra_test_config(max_num_batched_tokens=MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS, block_size=BLOCK_SIZE)
+    config.kv_transfer_config = None
+    config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching = False
+    config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling = issubclass(scheduler_cls, AsyncScheduler)
+    scheduler = create_dyntra_lb_scheduler(config, scheduler_cls=scheduler_cls)
+    # Releasing CPU payloads is an MRV2 contract; the fixture defaults to V1.
+    scheduler.use_v2_model_runner = True
+    # Supply the encoder budget directly: these CPU tests exercise the real
+    # scheduler without loading a multimodal model or running its processor.
+    scheduler.encoder_cache_manager = EncoderCacheManager(cache_size=ENCODER_BUDGET)
+    scheduler.max_num_encoder_input_tokens = ENCODER_BUDGET
+    if isinstance(scheduler, BalanceScheduler):
+        # Exercise the local schedule implementation, not its super fallback.
+        scheduler._balance_enabled = True
+        scheduler.balance_queue = [torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int)]
+    return scheduler
+

+def _image_request(images: list[tuple[str, int]], request_id: str = "image-request") -> Request:
+    """Build a request whose prompt starts with the given (identifier, length) images."""
+    sampling_params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=4)
+    sampling_params.update_from_generation_config({}, EOS_TOKEN_ID)
+    features = []
+    offset = 0
+    for identifier, length in images:
+        features.append(
+            MultiModalFeatureSpec(
+                data=MultiModalKwargsItem.dummy(),
+                modality="image",
+                identifier=identifier,
+                mm_position=PlaceholderRange(offset=offset, length=length),
+            )
+        )
+        offset += length
+    return Request(
+        request_id=request_id,
+        prompt_token_ids=[1] * PROMPT_TOKENS,
+        sampling_params=sampling_params,
+        pooling_params=None,
+        mm_features=features,
+    )
+
+
+def _mooncake_consumer() -> tuple[AscendECMooncakeConnector, AscendECMooncakeScheduler]:
+    """Build the real scheduler-side Mooncake consumer without a control plane."""
+    consumer = AscendECMooncakeScheduler.__new__(AscendECMooncakeScheduler)
+    consumer._is_producer = False
+    consumer._is_consumer = True
+    consumer._local_cache = set()
+    consumer._failed_saves = set()
+    consumer._store_candidates = []
+    consumer._cross_encoder_cache = False
+    consumer._pushes_to_prepare = {}
+    consumer._prepared_push_transfer_ids = set()
+    consumer._scheduler_pending_work = False
+    consumer._push_wait_timeout = 5.0
+    consumer._transfers = SchedulerTransferTable(1 << 20, 300)
+    consumer._drain_pending = False
+    consumer._event_ready_shards = OrderedDict()
+    consumer._pending_cancels = {}
+    consumer._control_executor = MagicMock()
+    consumer._control_addr = ""
+    consumer._drain_push_notifications = lambda: None
+    consumer._note_awaiting_push = lambda *args, **kwargs: None
+    consumer._store_get_enabled = False
+    consumer._store_get_states = {}
+    consumer._store_get_sizes = {}
+    consumer._store_get_waiters = {}
+    consumer._store_get_to_dispatch = {}
+    consumer._store_get_to_consume = set()
+    consumer._store_get_to_recompute = set()
+    consumer._store_get_to_discard = set()
+    connector = AscendECMooncakeConnector.__new__(AscendECMooncakeConnector)
+    connector._scheduler = consumer
+    connector._worker = None
+    connector._closed = False
+    return connector, consumer

+def _offer_from_encoder(consumer: AscendECMooncakeScheduler, request: Request) -> None:
+    """Record that the Encoder pushed every image of the request and can serve a load."""
+    request.ec_transfer_params = {
+        "ec_items": [
+            {"mm_hash": feature.identifier, "transfer_id": f"xfer-{feature.identifier}"}
+            for feature in request.mm_features
+        ]
+    }
+    for feature in request.mm_features:
+        consumer._transfers.observe_ready(
+            ECMooncakeLoadSpec(
+                mm_hash=feature.identifier,
+                nbytes=64,
+                shape=(feature.mm_position.length, 4),
+                dtype="float16",
+                transfer_id=f"xfer-{feature.identifier}",
+            ),
+            deadline=1e18,
+        )
+
+
+def _finish_prefill_chunk(scheduler: Scheduler, request: Request, scheduler_output) -> None:
+    runner_output = create_model_runner_output([request])
+    runner_output.sampled_token_ids = [[]]
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, runner_output)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheduler_cls", SCHEDULER_CLASSES)
+def test_waiting_duplicate_encoder_input_keeps_cache_reference(scheduler_cls):
+    scheduler = _make_scheduler(scheduler_cls)
+    request = _image_request([("shared", 4), ("shared", 4)])
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+
+    assert output.scheduled_encoder_inputs == {request.request_id: [0]}
+    manager = scheduler.encoder_cache_manager
+    assert manager.get_cached_input_ids(request) == {0, 1}
+    scheduler.finish_requests(request.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    assert manager.get_cached_input_ids(request) == set()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheduler_cls", SCHEDULER_CLASSES)
+def test_running_duplicate_encoder_input_keeps_cache_reference(scheduler_cls):
+    scheduler = _make_scheduler(scheduler_cls)
+    scheduler.max_num_scheduled_tokens = 2
+    request = _image_request([("first", 2), ("shared", 2), ("shared", 2)])
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    first = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert first.scheduled_encoder_inputs == {request.request_id: [0]}
+    _finish_prefill_chunk(scheduler, request, first)
+    assert request in scheduler.running
+
+    scheduler.max_num_scheduled_tokens = 4
+    with patch.object(scheduler, "_allocate_encoder_inputs", wraps=scheduler._allocate_encoder_inputs) as allocate:
+        output = scheduler.schedule()
+
+    assert output.scheduled_encoder_inputs == {request.request_id: [1]}
+    allocate.assert_called_once_with(request, [1], [2])
+    assert {1, 2} <= scheduler.encoder_cache_manager.get_cached_input_ids(request)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheduler_cls", SCHEDULER_CLASSES)
+def test_consumed_cpu_encoder_input_is_released(scheduler_cls):
+    """The worker drops its pixels once the placeholder range is confirmed."""
+    scheduler = _make_scheduler(scheduler_cls)
+    request = _image_request([("image", 8)])
+    payload = request.mm_features[0].data
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    prefill = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert prefill.num_scheduled_tokens == {request.request_id: PROMPT_TOKENS}
+    assert prefill.scheduled_encoder_inputs == {request.request_id: [0]}
+    # The placeholder range is still in flight, so the worker keeps its payload.
+    assert prefill.encoder_input_updates == {}
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(prefill, create_model_runner_output([request]))
+    decode = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert decode.encoder_input_updates == {request.request_id: {0: None}}
+    # EngineCore keeps the original payload for replay.
+    assert request.mm_features[0].data is payload
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(decode, create_model_runner_output([request]))
+    assert scheduler.schedule().encoder_input_updates == {}
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheduler_cls", SCHEDULER_CLASSES)
+def test_preempted_request_reinstalls_cpu_encoder_input(scheduler_cls):
+    """A resumed request gets its pixels back and releases them again."""
+    scheduler = _make_scheduler(scheduler_cls)
+    request = _image_request([("image", 8)])
+    payload = request.mm_features[0].data
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    prefill = scheduler.schedule()
+    scheduler.update_from_output(prefill, create_model_runner_output([request]))
+    decode = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert decode.encoder_input_updates == {request.request_id: {0: None}}
+    scheduler.update_from_output(decode, create_model_runner_output([request]))
+
+    assert scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)
+    resumed = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert resumed.scheduled_new_reqs[0].mm_features[0].data is payload
+    assert resumed.encoder_input_updates == {}
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(resumed, create_model_runner_output([request]))
+    assert scheduler.schedule().encoder_input_updates == {request.request_id: {0: None}}
+

+def _loads(scheduler_output) -> list[str]:
+    return [spec.mm_hash for spec in scheduler_output.ec_connector_metadata.loads]

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheduler_cls", SCHEDULER_CLASSES)
+def test_running_request_reloads_evicted_encoder_output(scheduler_cls):
+    """An output evicted between prefill chunks is loaded before the chunk uses it.
+
+    Mooncake still reports the request's own reservation as available, so
+    without the running check the chunk is scheduled as an external load that
+    no worker load serves, and the model runner raises "Encoder cache miss".
+    """
+    scheduler = _make_scheduler(scheduler_cls)
+    connector, consumer = _mooncake_consumer()
+    scheduler.ec_connector = connector
+    images = [("first", 2), ("second", 2)]
+    # An earlier request left both outputs in the local encoder cache.
+    earlier = _image_request(images, request_id="earlier-request")
+    for input_id in range(len(images)):
+        scheduler.encoder_cache_manager.allocate(earlier, input_id)
+    scheduler.encoder_cache_manager.free(earlier)
+    consumer._local_cache.update(identifier for identifier, _ in images)
+    request = _image_request(images)
+    _offer_from_encoder(consumer, request)
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    scheduler.max_num_scheduled_tokens = 2
+    first = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert first.num_scheduled_tokens == {request.request_id: 2}
+    assert _loads(first) == []
+    _finish_prefill_chunk(scheduler, request, first)
+
+    # Another allocation evicts "second" before the next chunk reaches it.
+    assert scheduler.encoder_cache_manager.can_allocate(
+        _image_request([("other", ENCODER_BUDGET - 2)], request_id="other-request"), 0, ENCODER_BUDGET, 0
+    )
+    connector.build_connector_meta(
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            free_encoder_mm_hashes=scheduler.encoder_cache_manager.get_freed_mm_hashes(),
+            preempted_req_ids=set(),
+        )
+    )
+
+    scheduler.max_num_scheduled_tokens = 4
+    deferred = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert request.request_id not in deferred.num_scheduled_tokens
+    assert _loads(deferred) == ["second"]
+
+    consumer._transfers.complete_load("second")
+    resumed = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert resumed.num_scheduled_tokens == {request.request_id: 4}
+    assert request.request_id not in resumed.scheduled_encoder_inputs
+

[BugFix][Quantization] Recognize native packed MXFP4 checkpoints (#22426)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Native compressed-tensors checkpoints can contain static, symmetric FP4
weights in `mxfp4-pack-quantized` format, with group size 32 and
omitted/null activation quantization. Ascend rejects this recipe with
`No compressed-tensors compatible quantization type was found.` Add
recognition of the native weight-only recipe and dispatch it to the
existing `W4A8_MXFP` backend, which dynamically quantizes activations to
MXFP8.

**Known parsing limitation:** the existing `from_config()`
activation-format whitelist does not recognize top-level
`mxfp4-pack-quantized`. Explicit activation metadata can therefore be
discarded before scheme detection. This PR currently leaves that parser
behavior unchanged; the explicit-activation review concern remains
unresolved. The actual native Kimi K3 checkpoint has `input_activations:
null`, so it continues to select `W4A8_MXFP`.

**Companion vLLM dependency:** Kimi K3 also needs its vLLM model-config
hook to preserve compressed-tensors metadata on NPU. Restrict the
existing rewrite to CUDA/ROCm:

```python
from vllm.platforms import current_platform

if not current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
    return
```

This companion change belongs in vLLM and is not included here. With an
unmodified Kimi K3 hook, the earlier `mxfp4 quantization is currently
not supported in npu` error still occurs before Ascend scheme detection.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Native packed MXFP4 checkpoints without activation recipes can use
the existing Ascend W4A8 MXFP backend. No new CLI parameter or platform
patch module is introduced. ModelSlim code and kernels are unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

- **24 CPU configuration unit tests passed** in
`tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_compressed_tensors_config.py` after
rolling back the explicit-activation parser follow-up. Tests ran in an
isolated process against installed vLLM `0.30.0+empty` / vllm-ascend
`0.30.0rc2.dev304+geac9c0cf3` dependencies, with
`TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0`, `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`,
and pytest `--noconftest`. Running service sources and bindings were not
changed.
- Coverage retains the original native recipe, global-format fallback,
checkpoint metadata parsing, invalid weight geometry/format rejection,
and existing detector-level schemes. These tests do not establish
correct parsing of explicit activations in top-level packed MXFP4
configurations.
- A fresh configuration probe using each PR-pinned vLLM helper confirms
the known limitation: explicitly configured dynamic FP4 activations
under top-level `mxfp4-pack-quantized` are dropped and the native
fallback selects W4A8. The actual native Kimi K3 checkpoint, whose
activations are null, still selects W4A8.
- Focused Ruff 0.14.0 lint/format, Python parsing, and `git diff
--check` passed. Full local `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but could
not start because `pre-commit` is not installed. New-head GitHub CI is
pending.

- Existing integration evidence for the native-recipe routing plus the
companion vLLM guard: a four-node A5 service, TP8/DP4, with vLLM
`0.30.0+empty` (`ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607`) and
vllm-ascend `eac9c0cf346edea79b68b9694ece9286dc60ef7e`. AISBench
completed 128/128 requests at 4096 input / 1024 output tokens and
concurrency 32. Repeated inputs were prewarmed; measured token cache hit
rate was 93.75% with 768-token blocks. This is prior serving evidence on
that runtime, not a new run of the current branch head, accuracy
validation, or a performance comparison.

Remaining before merge: resolution of the explicit-activation parsing
review concern, the companion vLLM routing change, new-head CI, and any
accuracy validation requested by maintainers.

[BugFix][Model] Skip unused DeepSeek V4.1 HC buffer for DSpark (#22485)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 currently uses `use_eagle()` to decide whether to allocate
the full HC hidden-state buffer. That predicate includes DSpark, even
though DSpark consumes the selected auxiliary hidden states through its
own storage. Serving with DSpark therefore reserves an unused
`[max_num_batched_tokens, hc_mult * hidden_size]` buffer and copies into
it on each target forward. With SP enabled, its presence also selects
the full-HC/pre-mix gather path.

Exclude DSpark at the V4.1 allocation condition. The existing
buffer-free forward path then handles collapse/gather, while MTP,
Eagle/Eagle3, DFlash and regular draft-model conditions remain
unchanged. No runner, shared `use_eagle()` semantics, or automatic-KV
accounting changes are included.

Target: `main`. Upstream vLLM uses the same exclusion in its [DeepSeek
buffer
predicate](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5173b1d5607ac9f0592e7600955fe8567f72e14b/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/common/spec_decode.py#L6-L16).
Related #16621 concerns DeepSeek V4 forward/runner operations; this
change fixes V4.1 allocation itself.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. DSpark leaves more device memory available for KV cache and avoids
the unused HC copy. No configuration changes are required. With
automatic KV sizing, total HBM usage need not fall because the released
capacity can become KV cache.

### How was this patch tested?

**This branch's source allocation regression:**

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 python3 -m pytest -q \
  --confcutdir=tests/ut/models tests/ut/models/test_deepseek_v41_mtp_buffer.py
```

Result: **14 passed**. The test executes the actual constructor
allocation statements using real CPU tensors and upstream
`SpeculativeConfig`, without loading decoder weights/native model
operators. It covers disabled speculation, DSpark, MTP, Eagle, Eagle3,
DFlash, regular draft models, and last/non-last PP ranks. A negative
control on the unfixed main allocation block fails the DSpark allocation
assertion (1 failed, 13 passed).

**Prior real-weight hardware evidence for the same guard, not a pristine
checkout of this branch:**

Two A3 nodes, 16 logical NPUs/node, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash W4A8, BF16
hidden states, DSpark K5, V2 runner. P: DP4/PCP4/TP1, eager, batch-token
limit 8192. D: DP16/TP1, FULL_DECODE_ONLY, batch-token limit 168. SP
disabled, automatic KV enabled. Other-role code held fixed for each
comparison; warmup excluded; three fixed-output synthetic rounds.

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| P HC allocation/rank | 320 MiB | 0 |
| P automatic KV budget/rank | 17.06 GiB | 17.37 GiB |
| D HC allocation/rank | 6.5625 MiB | 0 |
| D automatic KV budget/rank | 16.54 GiB | 16.55 GiB |
| P mean prefill, median of rounds (16K input/64 output, concurrency 32)
| 2264.6 ms | 2267.4 ms |
| D effective TPOT, median of rounds (1K input/1024 output, concurrency
128) | 12.354 ms | 12.291 ms |
| PD output throughput under D workload | 8039 token/s | 8144 token/s |

All measured requests succeeded, with zero preemptions and zero P
local-prefix hits. D external KV hits matched input length minus one;
successful KV transfers were logged. D draft acceptance was about 96.6%,
so these synthetic results do not establish business-workload throughput
gains. P is effectively unchanged; the small D change should not be
interpreted as a broad speedup. P output text hashes matched 189/192
requests and D 384/384; strict token/logprob equivalence and the cause
of the P differences remain unverified.

Each branch tip's full-model/SP-enabled hardware regression remains for
CI/reviewers; the hardware numbers above are supporting evidence from
the previously measured adapted 0.32 deployment, not three independent
branch-tip hardware acceptance runs.

**Static checks and limits:**

- Ruff check/format and `git diff --check`: passed for changed Python
files.
- Changed text files use LF. The repository-wide external LF checker
reports pre-existing upstream CRLF files and missing LF-policy metadata;
no unrelated files were rewritten.
- Full `format.sh ci` / equivalent manual pre-commit run could not
complete locally: Go/actionlint environment bootstrap stalled/timed out.
Full lint remains pending CI; this is not reported as a pass.

### Design-principles review

Reviewed: minimal model-local change, no new
configuration/dependencies/state, no timeout/error-path changes, no
added hot-path work or control-plane device initialization. The change
removes bounded per-rank allocation; the regression exercises real
allocation behavior. Existing unrelated changes and runtime
configuration are preserved. Validation evidence and remaining
branch-tip/SP/precision checks are distinguished above.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage: no speculation and non-last PP
ranks covered.
- [x] Regression test: old DSpark condition fails; guarded allocation
passes.
- [ ] Error / failure path coverage: no error path is changed by this
predicate-only fix.
- [x] Meaningful & reliable tests: actual constructor allocation with
real CPU tensors.
- [x] Performance impact: manual before/after evidence above and
allocation regression coverage; no automated throughput threshold is
claimed.

[BugFix] Handle padded graph rows in DSpark SWA indices (#22350)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix DSpark SWA indices when a captured graph keeps a fixed output row
count while the number of active token rows decreases.

- **PyTorch fallback:** for either caller-provided `buffer` or
`indices_output`, clone and pad the repeat counts to the fixed output
size, then mask inactive rows to indices `-1` and lengths `0` before
copying to stable output storage. This prevents the `repeat_interleave`
size mismatch.
- **Fused Triton path:** load `active_rows = query_start_loc[num_reqs]`
on device once per program and use it as the padding-cleanup lower
bound. Keep `num_rows` as the fixed output extent and buffer-check
value. The existing kernel clears padding in the same launch, without a
CPU synchronization or an additional mask operator. No constexpr keys or
specialization controls change.
- Add a regression that keeps six request slots and reuses the same
90-row index/length buffers for `[0,15,30,45,60,75,90]`,
`[0,15,30,30,30,30,30]`, then an all-zero batch. Every fused call uses
`num_decode_tokens=90`. Both direct launches and ACL graph
capture/replay check exact active rows, padding `-1/0`, fixed output
shapes, and buffer addresses.
- Update the operator documentation to distinguish the fixed output
extent from the device-side active row count.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Fix DSpark SWA metadata construction and stale padding when graph
replay has fewer active tokens than the fixed graph output size. No
configuration change is required.

### How was this patch tested?

- The branch is based on main `de6351f`, which includes the shared
dummy-embedding interface fix from #22530. This PR contains one commit
changing only the five DSpark implementation, test, and documentation
files.
- Local validation: `git rebase origin/main` completed successfully. The
complete five-file patch was verified byte-for-byte against the previous
PR diff; the worker implementation and dummy-embedding tests match main.
Python AST parsing and `git diff --check` passed.
- `bash format.sh ci` passed all 18 checks on the rebuilt branch.
- Existing CPU evidence: the six fallback cases passed in the earlier
isolated harness using unchanged production function/test ASTs. A fresh
attempt on this host could not run: the available Python/PyTorch test
environment exited with code 139 before producing test results. This is
not a new CPU test pass or a full repository unit-test run.
- Existing hardware evidence: the [A3 single-operator
validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/22350#issuecomment-7009645758)
and [reviewer
validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/22350#pullrequestreview-5976805418)
report the shrinking-buffer fix working on the tested A3/A5 paths. The
DSpark patch is unchanged; these are prior reported results, not new
local hardware runs.
- NPU validation for this revision is CI-only. The focused regression
can be run with:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_dspark_swa_indices.py
```

No new model accuracy or performance result is claimed. A full CI run
was requested on rebuilt commit `68cd4b2` with
[`/run`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/22350#issuecomment-7032555975).

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Full, shrinking, and
all-padding batches; both fallback output paths and persistent Triton
output buffers.
- [x] **Regression test**: Added tests for the repeat-count mismatch and
stale rows across direct launches/graph replay.
- [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: No new exception path is
introduced.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Assert exact indices/lengths,
output shapes, and buffer aliasing. CI validation of the rebuilt
revision is pending.
- [ ] **Performance impact**: No new hardware performance benchmark was
run for this revision.

- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c410543d9ffff03f5f6c4a8c0ae1d3ad082c4a15
